We define this as <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta \times \alpha\)" src="images/1364.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1364.svg_10">, rather than
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times \beta\)" src="images/1849.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1849.svg_1">, for the sake of certain analogies with
products in relation-arithmetic. Cf. <a href="#_166" class="pginternal">*166</a>.</p>

</div>
</div>


<hr class="chap x-ebookmaker-drop">

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_124">[Pg 124]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_114">
*114. THE ARITHMETICAL PRODUCT OF A CLASS OF CLASSES.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *114.</p>

<p>The kind of multiplication defined in <a href="#_113" class="pginternal">*113</a> cannot be extended beyond
a finite number of factors. We therefore, as in the case of addition,
introduce another definition, defining the product of the numbers of a
class of classes, and capable of being applied to an infinite number of
factors. We define the product of the numbers of members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_80">
as <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2065.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.749ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2065.svg">; thus we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/2066.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.137ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2066.svg"></span></p>

<p>It is to be observed that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/161.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.059ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_161.svg_3"> is not a function of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.719ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1360.svg_5">, because, if two members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_81"> have the
same number, this will count only once in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.719ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1360.svg_6">, but
will count twice in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/161.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.059ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_161.svg_4">.</p>

<p>It is very easy to see that, in case <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_82"> is finite,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2065.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.749ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2065.svg_1"> will be what we should ordinarily
regard as the product of the numbers of members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_83">. For
suppose (<i>e.g.</i>)
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \kappa  = \iota ʻ\alpha \cup \iota ʻ\beta \cup \iota ʻ\gamma , \]" src="images/2067.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 20.411ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2067.svg"></span>
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \neq \beta . \alpha \neq \gamma . \beta \neq \gamma\)" src="images/2068.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 18.977ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_2068.svg">. Then
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa  = \hat{R} \{(\exists x,y,z).R = x\downarrow \alpha \unicode{x228d} y\downarrow \beta \unicode{x228d} z\downarrow \gamma .x\in \alpha .y\in \beta .z\in \gamma\}. \]" src="images/2069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 63.56ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_2069.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_23"> is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2070.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2070.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_24"> is
determinate when <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_30">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_10">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg"> are given, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_31">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_11">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg_1">
being the referents to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_164">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_115">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma\)" src="images/35.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.229ex; height: 1.486ex;" id="img_images_35.svg_21">. Whether
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_165">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_116">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma\)" src="images/35.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.229ex; height: 1.486ex;" id="img_images_35.svg_22"> overlap or not, the choice of any
one of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_32">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_12">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg_2"> is entirely independent of the choice of
the other two, and therefore the total number of choices possible
is obviously the product of the numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_166">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_117">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma\)" src="images/35.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.229ex; height: 1.486ex;" id="img_images_35.svg_23">. Thus our definition will not conflict with what is commonly
understood by a product.</p>

<p>The propositions of this number are less numerous and less important
than those of <a href="#_113" class="pginternal">*113</a>. We shall deal first with products of a single
factor, and products in which one factor is null (<a href="#_114_2" class="pginternal">*114·2</a>—<a href="#_114_27" class="pginternal">·27</a>). We
shall then deal (<a href="#_114_3" class="pginternal">*114·3</a>—<a href="#_114_36" class="pginternal">·36</a>) with the relations between the sort of
multiplication here defined and the sort defined in *113. Then we have
a few propositions (<a href="#_114_4" class="pginternal">*114·4</a>—<a href="#_114_43" class="pginternal">*114·43</a>) showing that unit factors make no
difference to the value of a product. Then we prove (<a href="#_114_5" class="pginternal">*114·5</a>—<a href="#_114_52" class="pginternal">·52</a>) that
the value of the product is the same for two classes having double
similarity, and then (<a href="#_114_53" class="pginternal">*114·53</a>—<a href="#_114_571" class="pginternal">·571</a>) we give extensions of this result
which depend upon the multiplicative axiom. Finally, we give some new
forms of the associative law of multiplication.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_125">[Pg 125]</span></p>

<p>Among the more important propositions in this number are the following:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  . \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\iota ʻ\alpha  = \text{Nc}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/2072.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.274ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2072.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> a product of one factor is equal to that factor.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\Lambda \in \kappa .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = 0\)" src="images/2073.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 23.258ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2073.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> a product vanishes if one of its factors is zero. The
converse requires the multiplicative axiom, as appears from the
proposition</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}. \equiv  :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = 0. \equiv _{\kappa } .\Lambda \in \kappa\)" src="images/2074.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 37.13ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2074.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the multiplicative axiom is equivalent to the assumption
that a product vanishes when, and only when, one of its factors is zero.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·301.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \cap \lambda  = \lambda .\supset .{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ(\kappa  \cup  \lambda )\text{ sm } {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  \times  {\in}_{\Delta}     ʻ\lambda \)" src="images/2075.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 45.238ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2075.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">whence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \cap \lambda  = \Lambda .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  \times _{c} \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ(\kappa \cup \lambda )\)" src="images/2076.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.585ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2076.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which is a form of the associative law, and</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·35.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha  \neq  \beta .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ(\iota ʻ\alpha \cup \iota ʻ\beta ) = \text{Nc}ʻ\alpha  \times _{c} \text{Nc}ʻ\beta\)" src="images/2077.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 46.743ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2077.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which connects the two sorts of multiplication.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\lambda \subset 1.\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ(\kappa \cup \lambda ) = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2078.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.859ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2078.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> unit factors make no difference to the value of a product.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·51.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :T\upharpoonright sʻ\lambda \in \kappa \,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \lambda .\supset .(T\parallel \breve{T} _{\in })\upharpoonright {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda     \in ({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa )\,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, ({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda )\)" src="images/2079.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 67.225ex; height: 2.966ex;" id="img_images_2079.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition gives a correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2070.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2070.svg_1"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2080.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.706ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2080.svg"> as a function of a double correlator of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_84"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_39">, and thus leads to</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·52.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \text{ sm }\text{ sm }\lambda .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda .{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2081.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 50.309ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2081.svg"></p>

<p>Hence, by the propositions of <a href="#_111" class="pginternal">*111</a>, we infer</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·571.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :\mu ,\nu \in \text{NC}.\kappa ,\lambda \in \mu \cap \text{Cl}ʻ\nu .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2082.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 61.838ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2082.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> assuming the multiplicative axiom, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_85"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_40"> each consist of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_116"> classes of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_77"> terms each,
their products are equal.</p>

<p>We have next various forms of the associative law, beginning with</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·6.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  : \kappa  \in  \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl} . \supset  . \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta }ʻʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻsʻ\kappa \)" src="images/2083.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 43.753ex; height: 2.495ex;" id="img_images_2083.svg"></p>

<p>which is an immediate consequence of *85·44. The other form is</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·632.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{aligned}\vdash :S\upharpoonright &amp;\gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1.\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻS.\gamma \cap Sʻʻ\gamma  = \Lambda .\supset .\\ &amp;{\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\hat{\mu}\{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  Sʻ\alpha\}\text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ(\gamma \cup Sʻʻ\gamma )\end{aligned}\]" src="images/2084.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.104ex; width: 57.665ex; height: 5.339ex;" id="img_images_2084.svg"></span></p>

<p>As to the sense in which this is a form of the associative law, see the
observations following <a href="#_114_6" class="pginternal">*114·6</a>.</p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*114·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta }ʻ\kappa  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2085.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 24.508ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2085.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_114_1">*114·1</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  . \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  \quad[(*114·01)]\)" src="images/2086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.916ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2086.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\beta \in \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa . \equiv  .\beta \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa . \equiv  .\beta \in \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa      \quad[*114·1.*100·31]\)" src="images/2087.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 66.83ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2087.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·12.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa \in \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  \quad[*100·3.*114·1]\)" src="images/2088.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.639ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2088.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_114_2">*114·2</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\Lambda  = 1 \quad[*83·15 .*101·2]\)" src="images/2089.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.97ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2089.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_126">[Pg 126]</span></p>

<p>Thus a product of no factors is 1. This is the source of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu^{0} =1\)" src="images/2090.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.5ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_2090.svg">,
as we shall see later.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\iota ʻ\alpha  = \text{Nc}ʻ\alpha  \quad[*83·41]\)" src="images/2091.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.085ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2091.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  . \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\iota ʻ\Lambda  = 0 \quad[*114·21.*101·1]\)" src="images/2092.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.888ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2092.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\Lambda \in \kappa .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = 0 \quad[*83·11.*101·1]\)" src="images/2093.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 42.994ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2093.svg"></p>

<p>Thus an arithmetical product is zero if any of its factors is zero. To
prove the converse, we have to assume the multiplicative axiom, which,
in fact, is equivalent to the proposition that an arithmetical product
is only zero when at least one of its factors is zero.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda  \neq  0.\kappa \subset \lambda .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  \neq  0\)" src="images/2094.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 35.11ex; height: 2.183ex;" id="img_images_2094.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*114·1.*101·1. &amp;\supset \vdash :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda  \neq  0.\supset .\exists !{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash  . (1) . *80·6. \supset \vdash :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda  \neq  0.\kappa \subset \lambda .&amp;\supset .\exists !{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa .\\ [*114·1.*101·1] &amp;\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  \neq  0:\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2095.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 75.403ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_2095.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}. \equiv  :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = 0.\supset _{\kappa }.\Lambda \in \kappa\)" src="images/2096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 37.13ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2096.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*88·37.\text{Transp}.\supset \\ \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}. &amp;\equiv  :{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  = \Lambda .\supset _{\kappa }.\Lambda \in \kappa :\\ [*114·1.*101·1] &amp;\equiv  :\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = 0.\supset _{\kappa }.\Lambda \in \kappa \colon\ldotp \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2097.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 58.37ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_2097.svg"></span></p>

<p>Note that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda \in \kappa . \equiv .0\in \text{Nc}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2098.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.28ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2098.svg">.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*114·561.*85·61.\supset \\ \vdash \colon\ldotp (\exists S).S\in 1\rightarrow 1.S\,\unicode{x2abd}\, \text{ sm }.\text{D}ʻS = \kappa .\text{ᗡ}ʻS = \lambda .\supset :\\ \in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\kappa ,\in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\lambda \in \text{Cls}^{2}     \text{excl}:(\exists T).T\in 1\rightarrow 1.T\,\unicode{x2abd}\, \text{ sm }.\text{D}ʻT = \in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\kappa .\text{ᗡ}ʻT = \in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\lambda :\\ [*111·5] \supset :\text{Mult ax}.\supset .\in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\kappa \text{ sm } \text{ sm }\in \unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\lambda \colon\ldotp \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2135.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.49ex; width: 84.749ex; height: 12.111ex;" id="img_images_2135.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*114·57.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{aligned}\vdash \colon\ldotp &amp;\text{Mult ax}.\supset :\\ &amp;(\exists S).S\in 1\rightarrow 1.S\,\unicode{x2abd}\, \text{ sm }.\text{D}ʻS = \kappa .\text{ᗡ}ʻS = \lambda .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda \end{aligned}\]" src="images/2136.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 66.927ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_2136.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*114·562·52.\supset \\ \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :(\exists S).&amp;S\in 1\rightarrow 1.S\,\unicode{x2abd}\, \text{ sm }.\text{D}ʻS = \kappa .\text{ᗡ}ʻS = \lambda .\supset .\\ &amp;\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\in \downarrow ʻʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\in \downarrow ʻʻ\lambda .\\ [*114·56] &amp;\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda \colon\ldotp \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2137.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 63.419ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_2137.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_114_571">*114·571</a>.</b>
    <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{aligned}&amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :\mu ,\nu \in \text{NC}.\kappa ,\lambda \in \mu \cap \text{Cl}ʻ\nu .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda \\ &amp;[*111·52 . *114·57]\end{aligned}\]" src="images/2138.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 62.466ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_2138.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_114_6">*114·6</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}.\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻsʻ\kappa  \quad[*85·44]\)" src="images/2139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 54.564ex; height: 2.609ex;" id="img_images_2139.svg"></p>

<p>This is the most general form of the associative law for arithmetical
multiplication.</p>

<p>Owing to the fact that we have two kinds of multiplication, namely
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times \beta\)" src="images/1849.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1849.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_5">, we have four
forms of the associative law of multiplication, namely:</p>

<p>(1) *114·6, above,</p>

<p>(2) <a href="#_113_54" class="pginternal">*113·54</a>, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .(\mu \times _{c} \nu ) \times _{c}\varpi = \mu \times _{c} (\nu \times _{c} \varpi )\)" src="images/2140.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.384ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2140.svg">,</p>

<p>(3) <a href="#_114_31" class="pginternal">*114·31</a>, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \cap \lambda = \Lambda.\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa \times _{c} \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ(\kappa \cup \lambda )\)" src="images/2141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.585ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2141.svg">,</p>

<p>(4) a form of the associative law which has not yet been proved, which
may be explained as follows.</p>

<p>Suppose we have a number of pairs of classes, <i>e.g.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\((\alpha_{1}, \beta _{1})\)" src="images/2142.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2142.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\((\alpha _{2}, \beta _{2})\)" src="images/2143.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2143.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\((\alpha _{3},\beta _{3})\)" src="images/2144.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2144.svg">,....
Suppose we form the products <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{1} \times\beta _{1}\)" src="images/2145.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2145.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{2} \times \beta _{2}\)" src="images/2146.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2146.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{3} \times\beta _{3}\)" src="images/2147.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2147.svg">, ...
and multiply all these products together. We wish to
prove that (with a suitable hypothesis) the result is similar to the
product of all the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_167">'s and all the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_118">'s taken together
as one class; <i>i.e.</i> if we call <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_41"> the class of products
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{1} \times \beta _{1}\)" src="images/2148.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2148.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{2} \times \beta _{2}\)" src="images/2146.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2146.svg_1">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{3} \times \beta _{3}\)" src="images/2149.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.47ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2149.svg">, ..., and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_117"> the class whose
members are <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{1}\)" src="images/1377.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.436ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_1377.svg_4">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{2}\)" src="images/1378.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.436ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_1378.svg_3">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha _{3}\)" src="images/1379.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.436ex; height: 1.375ex;" id="img_images_1379.svg_2">, ...,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta _{1}\)" src="images/1637.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.268ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1637.svg_2">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta _{2}\)" src="images/1638.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.268ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1638.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta _{3}\)" src="images/2150.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.268ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2150.svg">, ..., we wish to prove
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\lambda  = \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\mu . \]" src="images/2151.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 17.841ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2151.svg"></span>
In order to express this proposition in symbols, let <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_8"> be the
correlator of the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_168">'s and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_119">'s, so that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta_{\nu} =Sʻ\alpha_{\nu}\)" src="images/2152.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.634ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2152.svg">.
(The suffix <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_78"> will not be used further, since it implies that the
number of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_169">'s and of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_120">'s is finite or denumerable.)
Then our class of products of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times \beta\)" src="images/1849.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1849.svg_3"> is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  Sʻ\alpha\}, \]" src="images/2153.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.036ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2153.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_130">[Pg 130]</span>
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma\)" src="images/35.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.229ex; height: 1.486ex;" id="img_images_35.svg_24"> is the class of all the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_170">'s ; and the product
of this class of products is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  Sʻ\alpha\}. \]" src="images/2154.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.423ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2154.svg"></span>
On the other hand, the class of all the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_171">'s and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_121">'s is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma \cup Sʻʻ\gamma\)" src="images/2155.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 9.146ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2155.svg">, and the product of this class is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ(\gamma \cup Sʻʻ\gamma ). \]" src="images/2156.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.922ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2156.svg"></span>
Thus what we have to prove (with a suitable hypothesis) is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  Sʻ\alpha\} \text{ sm } {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ(\gamma \cup Sʻʻ\gamma ). \]" src="images/2157.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 52.623ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2157.svg"></span>
The hypothesis required is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ S\upharpoonright \gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1.\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻS.\gamma \cap Sʻʻ\gamma  = \Lambda . \]" src="images/2158.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 37.853ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2158.svg"></span></p>

<p>A smaller hypothesis suffices, however, for a proposition which, in
virtue of <a href="#_114_301" class="pginternal">*114·301</a>, is closely allied to the above, namely
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\gamma  \times  {\in}_{\Delta}ʻSʻʻ\gamma  \text{ sm } {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  Sʻ\alpha\}. \]" src="images/2159.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 55.501ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2159.svg"></span>
For this, a sufficient hypothesis is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ S\upharpoonright \gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1.\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻS. \]" src="images/2160.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 23.114ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2160.svg"></span>
Thus <i>e.g.</i> we may write <img alt="" data-tex="\(I\)" src="images/723.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.14ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_723.svg_1"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_9">, and we find
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash .{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\gamma  \times  {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\gamma  \text{ sm } {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in \gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  \alpha\}. \]" src="images/2161.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 50.898ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2161.svg"></span></p>

<p>We shall now prove the above propositions. What follows, down to
<a href="#_114_621" class="pginternal">*114·621</a>, consists of lemmas.</p>

<p>For convenience, we write <img alt="" data-tex="\(S_{\times }ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/2162.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.625ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2162.svg"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times Sʻ\alpha\)" src="images/2163.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.478ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2163.svg">
in the course of these lemmas; this notation is introduced in the
hypotheses of the lemmas.</p>

<p>As in *114·601, we prove</p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash  . *114·63 \frac{S\mid\, \breve{R},\,Rʻʻ\gamma}{S,\,\gamma}. \supset \\ \vdash :S\mid \breve{R} \upharpoonright &amp;Rʻʻ\gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1.Rʻʻ\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻ(S\mid \breve{R} ).\supset .\\ &amp;{\in}_{\Delta}ʻRʻʻ\gamma  \times  {\in}_{\Delta}ʻSʻʻRʻʻRʻʻ\gamma \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu}     \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in Rʻʻ\gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  (S\mid \breve{R} )ʻ\alpha\} &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .*74·14 .*35·354. \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.&amp;\supset .S\mid \breve{R} \upharpoonright Rʻʻ\gamma  = S\upharpoonright \gamma \mid \gamma \upharpoonleft \breve{R} .\breve{R} \upharpoonright Rʻʻ\gamma  = \gamma \upharpoonleft \breve{R} .\\ [*71·252] &amp;\supset .S\mid \breve{R} \upharpoonright Rʻʻ\gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1 &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .*37·2.\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.&amp;\supset .Rʻʻ\gamma \subset Rʻʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻS.\\ [*37·32] &amp;\supset .Rʻʻ\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻ(S\mid \breve{R} ) &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .*74·171. &amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .\breve{R} ʻʻRʻʻ\gamma  = \gamma  &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \vdash .(4).*74·14. \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.&amp;\supset .(Rʻʻ\gamma )\upharpoonleft R = R\upharpoonright \gamma .\\ [*35·7.*71·4] &amp;\supset .\hat{\mu} \{(\exists \alpha ).\alpha \in Rʻʻ\gamma .\mu  = \alpha  \times  (S\mid \breve{R} )ʻ\alpha \}\\ &amp;= \hat{\mu} \{(\exists z).z\in \gamma .\mu  = Rʻz \times  Sʻ\breve{R} ʻRʻz\}\\ [*74·53] &amp;= \hat{\mu} \{(\exists z).z\in \gamma .\mu  = Rʻz \times  Sʻz\} &amp;\qquad \text{(5)}\\ \vdash .(1).(2).(3).(4).(5).\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2199.svg" style="vertical-align: -23.376ex; width: 120.746ex; height: 47.883ex;" id="img_images_2199.svg"></span></p>

<p>In the above proposition, the hypothesis has to be such as to yield
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{R} ʻʻRʻʻ\gamma = \gamma\)" src="images/2200.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 14.338ex; height: 2.903ex;" id="img_images_2200.svg">. Various other forms of hypothesis
will secure this result, and will give other forms of the above
proposition. This subject is treated in *74, above.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_135">[Pg 135]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="id_115_MULTIPLICATIVE_CLASSES_AND_ARITHMETICAL_CLASSES">
*115. MULTIPLICATIVE CLASSES AND ARITHMETICAL CLASSES.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *115.</p>

<p>Whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_88"> is a class of mutually exclusive
classes, <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_6"> is similar to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1388.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1388.svg_2">; hence
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \text{Nc}ʻ\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/2202.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 24.897ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2202.svg"></span></p>

<p>Now <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1388.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1388.svg_3"> is of the same type as
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_89">; and when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_90"> is a class of mutually exclusive
classes, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1388.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1388.svg_4"> consists of all classes
formed by selecting one representative from each member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_91">.
It often happens that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1388.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1388.svg_5"> is easier
to deal with than <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_7">; hence when possible
(<i>i.e.</i> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl})\)" src="images/2203.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.923ex; height: 2.609ex;" id="img_images_2203.svg">, it
is convenient to use <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1388.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1388.svg_6">, rather
than <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_8">, as the standard member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi\text{Nc}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/271.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.059ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_271.svg_2">. We therefore put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻ\kappa  = \text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/2204.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.94ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2204.svg"></span></p>

<p>We shall call <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2205.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.477ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2205.svg"> the "multiplicative class" of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_92">.</p>

<p>The associative law,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa  \text{ sm } \text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa , \]" src="images/2206.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 29.441ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2206.svg"></span>
requires not merely <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}\)" src="images/2207.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.043ex; height: 2.133ex;" id="img_images_2207.svg">, but also
<img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}\)" src="images/2208.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.462ex; height: 2.495ex;" id="img_images_2208.svg">. The combination of these
two hypotheses gives a completely disjointed class of classes of
classes, <i>i.e.</i> a class of classes of classes <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_93"> which can
be obtained by dividing a given class <img alt="" data-tex="\((sʻsʻ\kappa)\)" src="images/2209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.9ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2209.svg"> into mutually
exclusive portions, and then dividing each of those portions into
mutually exclusive portions. For example, take a square (a class of
points) and divide it by horizontal lines, and then divide each of the
resulting rectangles by vertical lines; then the resulting rows of
little rectangles form such a class, each row of rectangles being one
member of the class. Such a class we call an "arithmetical" class, and
denote by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}\)" src="images/2210.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 11.189ex; height: 2.089ex;" id="img_images_2210.svg">."</p>

<p>The present number is concerned with the properties of multiplicative
classes and arithmetical classes. Some of these properties will be
useful in dealing with exponentiation.</p>

<p>The present number begins with various propositions concerning
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2205.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.477ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2205.svg_1"> which are merely repetitions of previous
propositions of *83, *84, *85 or <a href="#_113" class="pginternal">*113</a>. Thus we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·141.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa .\supset .sʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa  = sʻ\kappa     \quad\text{by *83·66}\)" src="images/2211.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.462ex; width: 43.977ex; height: 2.158ex;" id="img_images_2211.svg">,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·142.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Prod}ʻ\iota ʻ\alpha  = \iotaʻʻ\alpha    \quad\text{by *83·7}\)" src="images/2212.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.462ex; width: 30.584ex; height: 2.158ex;" id="img_images_2212.svg">,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·143.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Prod}ʻ\iotaʻʻ\alpha  = \iota ʻ\alpha  \quad\text{by *83·71}\)" src="images/2213.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.462ex; width: 31.715ex; height: 2.158ex;" id="img_images_2213.svg">,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·16.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa \subset \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  \quad\text{by *100·64}\)" src="images/2214.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.462ex; width: 46.757ex; height: 2.505ex;" id="img_images_2214.svg">,</p>

<p class="nind">and various other properties.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_136">[Pg 136]</span></p>

<p>We then proceed to consider <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}\)" src="images/2210.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 11.189ex; height: 2.089ex;" id="img_images_2210.svg_1">. We prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset :sʻʻ\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2}     \text{excl}:\alpha ,\beta \in \kappa .\exists !sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta .\supset _{\alpha ,\beta }.\alpha =\beta\)" src="images/2215.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 73.238ex; height: 2.693ex;" id="img_images_2215.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
and <a href="#_115_23" class="pginternal">*115·23</a> gives a similar proposition substituting "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}\)" src="images/2216.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.817ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_2216.svg">"
for <img alt="" data-tex="\(s\)" src="images/721.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.061ex; height: 1.023ex;" id="img_images_721.svg_2">.</p>

<p>After a few more propositions on <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}\)" src="images/2210.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 11.189ex; height: 2.089ex;" id="img_images_2210.svg_2">,
we proceed to the associative law for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}\)" src="images/2216.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.817ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_2216.svg_1"> (<a href="#_115_34" class="pginternal">*115·34</a>),
<i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa \text{ sm }\text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/2217.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 51.111ex; height: 2.494ex;" id="img_images_2217.svg"></span></p>

<p>(This proposition, <a href="#_115_34" class="pginternal">*115·34</a>, also states that, with the same hypothesis,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻsʻ\kappa)\)" src="images/2218.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.792ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2218.svg">. Hence we
have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·35.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset     .\text{Nc}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa &amp;=\text{Nc}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa =\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa \\ &amp;=\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa =\Pi \text{Nc}ʻsʻ\kappa\end{align}\]" src="images/2219.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.208ex; width: 75.317ex; height: 5.548ex;" id="img_images_2219.svg"></span></p>

<p>We have also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa =\text{D}ʻʻʻ\text{Prod}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa     =\text{D}ʻʻʻ\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2220.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 83.415ex; height: 2.494ex;" id="img_images_2220.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·44.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa =sʻʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2221.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 53.368ex; height: 2.494ex;" id="img_images_2221.svg"></p>

<p>We have next to prove that if two classes of classes have double
similarity, so have their multiplicative classes. The proof is simple,
since the double correlator is the same as for the original classes,
<i>i.e.</i></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·502.</b>
    <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :T\upharpoonright sʻ\lambda \in \kappa \,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \lambda .\supset .T\upharpoonright sʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\lambda \in (\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa )\,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, (\text{Prod}ʻ\lambda )\)" src="images/2222.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 72.944ex; height: 2.296ex;" id="img_images_2222.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">whence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·51.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \text{ sm }\text{ sm }\lambda .\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa \text{ sm }\text{ sm }\text{Prod}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2223.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 39.634ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2223.svg"></p>

<p>The number ends with some propositions which result from <a href="#_114_64" class="pginternal">*114·64</a><a href="#_114_65" class="pginternal">·65</a> and
are analogous to them. One of these is used in the following number, in
proving <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^{\varpi }\times _{c}\nu ^{\varpi }=(\mu \times _{c}\nu)^{\varpi }\)" src="images/2224.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.851ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2224.svg">,
namely,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·6.</b>
    <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :(Rʻʻ\gamma )&amp;\upharpoonleft R,S\upharpoonright \gamma \in 1\rightarrow 1.\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻR.\gamma \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻS.Rʻʻ\gamma ,Sʻʻ\gamma \in \text{Cls}^{2}     \text{excl}.\supset .\\ &amp;\text{Prod}ʻRʻʻ\gamma \times \text{Prod}ʻSʻʻ\gamma \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\hat{\mu} \{(\exists z).z\in \gamma .\mu =Rʻz\times Sʻz\}\end{align}\]" src="images/2225.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.277ex; width: 74.43ex; height: 5.685ex;" id="img_images_2225.svg"></span></p>

<p>The subject of this number will be useful in dealing with
exponentiation, since we shall define <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_5"> by means
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\alpha\downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/2226.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.083ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2226.svg">, where
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu=\text{N}_{0}\text{c}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/1599.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 10.876ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_1599.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{c}ʻ\beta\)" src="images/2227.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.543ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2227.svg">.</p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*115·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa =\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.311ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2228.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}=\hat{\kappa} (\kappa ,sʻ\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}) \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2229.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 38.724ex; height: 2.609ex;" id="img_images_2229.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa =\text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa      \quad[(*115·01)]\)" src="images/2230.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.719ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2230.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·101.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \alpha \in \kappa .\supset _{\alpha }.\varpi \cap \alpha \in 1:\varpi \subset sʻ\kappa :\supset .\varpi \in \text{Prod}ʻ\kappa  \quad[*84·411]\)" src="images/2231.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 62.209ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2231.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*115·11.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash \colon\colon \kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2}     \text{excl}.\supset \colon\ldotp \varpi \in \text{Prod}ʻ\kappa .\equiv :\alpha \in \kappa .\supset _{\alpha }.\varpi \cap \alpha \in 1:\varpi \subset sʻ\kappa\\ &amp;[*84·412]\end{align}\]" src="images/2232.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.209ex; width: 67.717ex; height: 5.55ex;" id="img_images_2232.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_137">[Pg 137]</span></p>

<p>Owing to this proposition, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2205.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.477ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2205.svg_2"> can be treated
without any reference to <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_9"> whenever

<p>Observe that, although "<img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻʻ\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}\)" src="images/2258.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 15.819ex; height: 2.495ex;" id="img_images_2258.svg">"
follows from
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \unicode{x201c}\alpha ,\beta \in \kappa .\exists !sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta .\supset _{\alpha ,\beta }.\alpha  = \beta ,\unicode{x201d} \]" src="images/2259.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 36.125ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2259.svg"></span>
the converse implication does not hold. If there were two different
classes <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_172"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_122"> having the same sum, we might have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists !sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta\)" src="images/2260.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.967ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2260.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists !sʻ\alpha\)" src="images/2261.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.753ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2261.svg">,
without having <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha = \beta\)" src="images/2262.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.746ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2262.svg">, in spite of "<img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻʻ\kappa \in\text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}\)" src="images/2263.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 15.819ex; height: 2.495ex;" id="img_images_2263.svg">."
In proofs, less use can be made of "<img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻʻ\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl}\)" src="images/2258.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 15.819ex; height: 2.495ex;" id="img_images_2258.svg_1">"
than of "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha ,\beta \in \kappa .\exists !sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta.\supset_{\alpha,\beta }.\alpha = \beta\)" src="images/2264.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 32.856ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2264.svg">."
If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda {\sim} \in\kappa\)" src="images/2265.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 7.399ex; height: 1.71ex;" id="img_images_2265.svg"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻ\Lambda {\sim} \in \kappa\)" src="images/2266.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.558ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2266.svg">,
the latter implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(s\upharpoonright \kappa \in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/2267.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 13.112ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_2267.svg">.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*83·62. &amp;\supset \vdash :\varpi \in \text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \cap \text{Prod}ʻ\beta .\supset .\varpi \subset sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*24·58. &amp;\supset \vdash :\varpi \in \text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \cap \text{Prod}ʻ\beta .\exists !\varpi .\supset .\exists !sʻ\alpha \cap sʻ\beta  &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .(2).*115·22. &amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\alpha ,\beta \in \kappa .\varpi \in \text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \cap \text{Prod}ʻ\beta .\exists !\varpi .\supset .\alpha  = \beta  &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .*83·16. \text{Transp}.&amp;\supset \vdash :\Lambda \in \text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \cap \text{Prod}ʻ\beta .\supset .\alpha  = \Lambda .\beta  = \Lambda  &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \vdash .(3).(4). \supset \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.&amp;\supset :\alpha ,\beta \in \kappa .\exists !\text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \cap \text{Prod}ʻ\beta .\supset .\alpha  = \beta . &amp;\qquad \text{(5)}\\ [*30·37] &amp;\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\alpha  = \text{Prod}ʻ\beta  &amp;\qquad \text{(6)}\\ \vdash .(5).(6).*84·11.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2269.svg" style="vertical-align: -10.068ex; width: 93.323ex; height: 21.267ex;" id="img_images_2269.svg"></span></p>

<p>In the above proposition, <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa\subset 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/2273.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.233ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2273.svg">

<p class="nind"><b>*115·27.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset .\kappa \subset \text{Cls}^{2} \text{excl} \quad[*115·2.*84·25.*40·13]\)" src="images/2275.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 62.626ex; height: 2.609ex;" id="img_images_2275.svg"></p>

<p>We have now to prove the associative law for "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}\)" src="images/2216.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.817ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_2216.svg_2">,"
<i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \kappa \in \text{Cls}^{3}\,\text{arithm}.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻsʻ\kappa  \text{ sm } \text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/2276.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 48.472ex; height: 2.494ex;" id="img_images_2276.svg"></span></p>

<p>In virtue of <a href="#_115_12" class="pginternal">*115·12</a>, we have only to prove (under the hypothesis)
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻsʻ\kappa \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa \]" src="images/2277.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.238ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2277.svg"></span>
which, by *85·44, will follow from
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa \text{ sm }{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa \]" src="images/2278.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 28.563ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2278.svg"></span>
which, by <a href="#_114_52" class="pginternal">*114·52</a>, will follow from
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa \text{ sm }\text{ sm }\text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/2279.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 24.326ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2279.svg"></span></p>

<p>Now
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻʻ\kappa  = \text{D}_{\in}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/2280.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.227ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2280.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus the correlator which will give our proposition will be
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}\upharpoonright sʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2281.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.395ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2281.svg">. We have only to
prove that this is a <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/1429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.782ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_1429.svg_1">, and the rest follows.</p>

<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2205.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.477ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2205.svg_4"> is more convenient than
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_10">. We cannot have <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\text{ sm } \text{ sm } {\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2312.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 19.21ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2312.svg">,
because <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_11"> is a class of <i>relations</i>, not a
class of classes; and the correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1376.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.69ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1376.svg_12"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2313.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.706ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2313.svg"> is by no means so simple a function of the
correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_94"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_43"> as <img alt="" data-tex="\(T_{\in } \upharpoonright\text{Prod}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2314.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.27ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2314.svg">,
which correlates <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\kappa\)" src="images/2205.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.477ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2205.svg_5"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\lambda\)" src="images/2315.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.493ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2315.svg">, in virtue of <a href="#_115_502" class="pginternal">*115·502</a>.</p>

<p>The following propositions are a continuation of those given in
<a href="#_114_601" class="pginternal">*114·601</a> ff.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_143">[Pg 143]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_116">*116. EXPONENTIATION.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *116.</p>

<p>In this number, we define "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\, \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2324.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.697ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2324.svg">," meaning
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_173"> to the exponent <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_123">," where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_174"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_124">
are classes, as
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta . \]" src="images/2325.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.712ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2325.svg"></span>
Now <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/2326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.083ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2326.svg"> consists of
all ways of selecting one each from the members of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/1371.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 8.909ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_1371.svg_3">, <i>i.e.</i> from the classes
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow yʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/1844.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 7.031ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_1844.svg_2">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\in \beta\)" src="images/1845.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 5.155ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_1845.svg_1">. Thus to get a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\alpha \downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/2326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.083ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2326.svg_1">, take a set of couples
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow y\)" src="images/1842.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.791ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1842.svg_1">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_33"> is always an <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_175">, and there
is only one <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_34"> for a given <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_13">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_14"> is each member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_125"> in succession. Thus for each member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_126">, we have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/135.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.507ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_135.svg_62"> possible referents; hence it is plain that the
number of possible sets of couples consists of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ\beta\)" src="images/157.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.339ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_157.svg_32">
factors each equal to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/135.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.507ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_135.svg_63">, and is therefore fit to be
taken as defining <img alt="" data-tex="\((\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha )^{\text{Nc}ʻ\beta}\)" src="images/1707.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.23ex; height: 2.587ex;" id="img_images_1707.svg_1">.</p>

<p>The definitions of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_6"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\((\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha)^{\text{Nc}ʻ\beta}\)" src="images/2327.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.23ex; height: 2.587ex;" id="img_images_2327.svg">
are derived from the definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \,\,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2328.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.697ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2328.svg">
exactly as the definitions of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu +_{c} \nu\)" src="images/151.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.21ex; height: 1.808ex;" id="img_images_151.svg_9">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha +_{c} \text{Nc}ʻ\beta\)" src="images/282.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.492ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_282.svg_2">, or of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \times_{c} \nu\)" src="images/2329.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.21ex; height: 1.6ex;" id="img_images_2329.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha \times _{c} \text{Nc}ʻ\beta\)" src="images/2330.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.492ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2330.svg">, were
derived respectively from <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha + \beta\)" src="images/1300.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1300.svg_11"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times\beta\)" src="images/2331.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2331.svg">.</p>

<p>The chief difficulty in this number lies in the proof of the three
formal laws of exponentiation, namely
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} \mu ^\nu  \times _{c} \mu ^{\varpi } &amp;= \mu ^{\nu  +_{c} \varpi },\\ \mu ^{\varpi } \times _{c} \nu ^{\varpi } &amp;= (\mu  \times _{c} \nu )^{\varpi },\\ \text{and}\qquad (\mu ^\nu )^{\varpi } &amp;= \mu ^{\nu  \times _{c} \varpi }. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/2332.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.603ex; width: 26.973ex; height: 8.338ex;" id="img_images_2332.svg"></span>
The proofs of the second and third of these, in particular, require
various lemmas; but there is no difficulty involved except the
complexity of the classes and relations concerned.</p>

<p>The definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_7"> is so framed as to minimize the
necessity for the multiplicative axiom (see the note on *<a href="#_113_31" class="pginternal">*113·31</a> in the
introduction to *113). We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·36.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :\mu ,\nu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\kappa \in \nu \cap \text{Cl}ʻ\mu .\supset .\Pi \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa  = \mu ^\nu\)" src="images/2333.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 61.332ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2333.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
that is, assuming the multiplicative axiom, the product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_79">
factors each equal to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_118"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_8"> (assuming <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_119"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_80"> to be cardinals which are not null).</p>

<p>If we had <i>defined</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_9"> as the product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_81"> factors
each equal to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_120">, we should<span class="pagenum" id="Page_144">[Pg 144]</span> have required the multiplicative
axiom for almost all propositions on <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_10"> but by taking the
particular class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/1368.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 8.909ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_1368.svg_10">, we avoid the
multiplicative axiom except in a few propositions. Among these few is
the above proposition connecting exponentiation with multiplication.</p>

<p>Cantor has defined <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_11"> by means of the class of "Belegungen,"
<i>i.e.</i> the class
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \hat{R} (R\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.\text{D}ʻR\subset \alpha .\text{ᗡ}ʻR = \beta ) \]" src="images/2334.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.775ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_2334.svg"></span>
which (<a href="#_116_12" class="pginternal">*116·12</a>) = <img alt="" data-tex="\((\alpha \uparrow \beta )_{\Delta }ʻ\beta\)" src="images/1704.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.035ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1704.svg_1">.
By *85·53 and <a href="#_113_103" class="pginternal">*113·103</a>, this class is equal to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{s}ʻʻ(\alpha\,\text{exp}\,\,\beta)\)" src="images/2335.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.855ex; height: 2.301ex;" id="img_images_2335.svg">
(as is proved in <a href="#_116_13" class="pginternal">*116·13</a>), whence, since
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{s} \upharpoonright \alpha \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta \in 1\rightarrow1\)" src="images/2336.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 19.128ex; height: 2.174ex;" id="img_images_2336.svg">,
it follows (<a href="#_116_15" class="pginternal">*116·15</a>) that the class of "Belegungen" is similar to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\, \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2324.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.697ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2324.svg_1">. Hence our definition gives the same
value of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu^\nu\)" src="images/163.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_163.svg_3"> as Cantor's.</p>

<p>The propositions of the present number begin with various simple
properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\, \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2324.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.697ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2324.svg_2">. Its existence follows
from</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·152.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :x\in \alpha .\supset .x\downarrow ʻʻ\beta \in \alpha\,  \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2337.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 30.061ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2337.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
whence (<a href="#_116_16" class="pginternal">*116·16</a>) <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Cnv}ʻʻʻ\beta \downarrow_{,,}ʻʻ\alpha \subset \alpha\, \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2338.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 30.17ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2338.svg">, and</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·18.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \exists !\alpha .\lor.\beta  = \Lambda : \equiv  .\exists !\alpha\,  \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2339.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 29.725ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_2339.svg"></p>

<p>We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·19.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \text{ sm }\gamma .\beta \text{ sm }\delta .\supset .(\alpha\,  \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta)\text{ sm } \text{ sm }(\gamma \, \,\text{exp}\,\, \delta \)" src="images/2340.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 45.547ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2340.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
in virtue of <a href="#_113_13" class="pginternal">*113·13</a> and <a href="#_115_51" class="pginternal">*115·51</a>. <a href="#_116_192" class="pginternal">*116·192</a> shows that, if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\upharpoonright \gamma\)" src="images/2341.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 5.146ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_2341.svg"> correlates <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_176"> with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\gamma\)" src="images/35.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.229ex; height: 1.486ex;" id="img_images_35.svg_25">, and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(S\upharpoonright \delta\)" src="images/2342.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.664ex; height: 2.061ex;" id="img_images_2342.svg"> correlates <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_127"> with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\delta\)" src="images/302.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.005ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_302.svg_19">, then
<img alt="" data-tex="\((R\parallel \breve{S})\upharpoonright (\delta \times \gamma)\)" src="images/2343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.284ex; height: 3.029ex;" id="img_images_2343.svg"> is a
double correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\, \,\text{exp}\,\, \beta\)" src="images/2324.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.697ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_2324.svg_3"> with <img alt="" data-tex="\((\gamma\,\,\text{exp}\,\, \delta)\)" src="images/2344.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.962ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2344.svg">.</p>

<p>We then proceed to a set of propositions on <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_12"> which are
analogous to <a href="#_113_2" class="pginternal">*113·2</a> ff. on <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \times _{c }\nu\)" src="images/2345.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.21ex; height: 1.6ex;" id="img_images_2345.svg">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·203.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\mu ^\nu .\supset .\mu ,\nu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\mu ,\nu \in \text{N}_{0}\text{C}\)" src="images/2346.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 38.518ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2346.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .(\text{Nc}ʻ\gamma )^{\text{Nc}ʻ\delta } = \text{Nc}ʻ(\gamma \, \,\text{exp}\,\, \delta)\)" src="images/2347.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.241ex; height: 2.587ex;" id="img_images_2347.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">and various other less useful propositions.</p>

<p>We then have various propositions on 0 and 1 and 2. We prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·301.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\supset .\mu ^{0} = 1\)" src="images/2348.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 26.867ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_2348.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·311.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda  - \iota ʻ0.\supset .0^\nu  = 0\)" src="images/2349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 33.075ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2349.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·321.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\supset .\mu ^{1} = \text{ sm }ʻʻ\mu\)" src="images/2350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 33.722ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_2350.svg"></p>

<p>(Observe that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ sm }ʻʻ\mu\)" src="images/148.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 7.986ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_148.svg_14"> is the same cardinal as <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_121">, but
rendered typically ambiguous.)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·331.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \in \text{NC} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\supset .1^\mu  = 1\)" src="images/2351.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 27.05ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_2351.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*116·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\mu ^{2} = \mu  \times _{c} \mu\)" src="images/2352.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 14.132ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_2352.svg"></p>

<p>(This proposition does not require that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_122"> should be a cardinal.)</p>
