<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_253">[Pg 253]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_122">*122. PROGRESSIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *122.</p>

<p>By a "progression" we mean a series which is like the series of the
inductive cardinals in order of magnitude (assuming that all inductive
cardinals exist), <i>i.e.</i> a series whose terms can be called
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ 1_{R}, 2_{R}, 3_{R}, ... \nu _{R}, ..., \]" src="images/3638.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.809ex; height: 1.946ex;" id="img_images_3638.svg"></span>
where every term of the series is correlated with some inductive
cardinal, and every inductive cardinal is correlated with some term
of the series. Such series belong to the relation-number (cf. <a href="#_152" class="pginternal">*152</a>
and *263) which Cantor calls <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_1">. Their generating relation
may be taken to be the transitive relation of earlier and later, or
the one-one relation of immediate predecessor to immediate successor.
We shall reserve the notation <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_2"> for the <i>transitive</i>
generating relations of progressions; for the present, we are concerned
with the one-one relations which generate progressions. The class of
these relations we shall call "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prog}\)" src="images/3639.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 4.69ex; height: 2.011ex;" id="img_images_3639.svg">."</p>

<p>It is not convenient to <i>define</i> a progression as a series which
is ordinally similar to that of the inductive cardinals, both because
this definition only applies if we assume the axiom of infinity,
and because we have in any case to show that (assuming the axiom of
infinity) the series of inductive cardinals has certain properties,
which can be used to afford a direct definition of progressions. The
existence of progressions, however, is only obtainable by means of the
axiom of infinity, and is then most easily obtained from the fact that
the inductive cardinals form a progression. We shall not consider the
existence-theorem until the next number (<a href="#_123" class="pginternal">*123</a>).</p>

<p>From this number onwards convention <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Infin}\,T\)" src="images/3640.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 6.624ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_3640.svg"> of the Prefatory
Statement is used when relevant.</p>

<p>The characteristics of the generating relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_31"> of a progression,
which we employ in the definition, are the following:</p>

<p>(1) <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_32"> is a one-one relation;</p>

<p>(2) there is a first term, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!BʻR\)" src="images/3641.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.962ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3641.svg">;</p>

<p>(3) the whole field is contained in the posterity of the first term,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3642.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 17.399ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3642.svg">. (If this failed, <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/389.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_389.svg_2">
would consist of two or more distinct families, of which, since we have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!BʻR\)" src="images/3641.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.962ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3641.svg_1">, all but one would have to be cyclic families.)</p>

<p>(4) every term of the field has a successor, <i>i.e.</i> the series is
endless. This is secured <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\subset \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/3643.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.252ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3643.svg">, or (what is
equivalent) <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR=\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/3644.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.614ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3644.svg">.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_254">[Pg 254]</span></p>

<p>These four properties suffice to define the one-one generating
relations of progressions. It will be observed that (2), (3) and (4)
are all secured by
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{D}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR. \]" src="images/3645.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 18.037ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3645.svg"></span></p>

<p>This secures <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!BʻR\)" src="images/3641.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.962ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3641.svg_2">, by *14·21; it secures
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\subset \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/3643.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.252ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3643.svg_1">, by *37·25 and *90·163; hence, by
*33·181, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR=CʻR\)" src="images/3646.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.614ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3646.svg">, and therefore
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ CʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR. \]" src="images/3647.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 18.028ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3647.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence our definition of progressions is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prog}=(1\rightarrow 1)\cap \hat{R} (\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)  \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/3648.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.961ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3648.svg"></span></p>

<p>Instead of stating in the definition that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_33"> is to
be a one-one relation, it is sufficient to put
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in\text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/3649.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 20.056ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3649.svg">,
which, with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3650.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3650.svg">, implies
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/3651.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_3651.svg">, and may be substituted for
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/3651.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_3651.svg_1"> without altering the force of the definition
(<a href="#_122_17" class="pginternal">*122·17</a>).</p>

<p>In the present number we shall prove, among other propositions, that
every existent class contained in a progression has a first term
(<a href="#_122_23" class="pginternal">*122·23</a>), <i>i.e.</i> that progressions are well-ordered series;
that in a progression <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/3652.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 7.14ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3652.svg"> (<a href="#_122_16" class="pginternal">*122·16</a>),
which makes the propositions of <a href="#_121" class="pginternal">*121</a> available; that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_133"> is
any inductive cardinal other than 0, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu _{R}\)" src="images/3653.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.373ex;" id="img_images_3653.svg"> exists (<a href="#_122_33" class="pginternal">*122·33</a>),
<i>i.e.</i> the series has a <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_134">th term; that any class contained
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_1"> and having a last term is an inductive class
(<a href="#_122_43" class="pginternal">*122·43</a>), and that any class contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_2"> and not
having a last term is itself the domain of a progression (<a href="#_122_45" class="pginternal">*122·45</a>), so
that every class contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_3"> is either inductive or
the domain of a progression (<a href="#_122_46" class="pginternal">*122·46</a>); that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_36"> is a many-one,
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_82"> a member of its domain, and if the descendants of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_83">
have no last term and are none of them descendants of themselves,
then <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_37"> arranges these descendants in a progression (<a href="#_122_51" class="pginternal">*122·51</a>);
and that the same holds if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_38"> is a one-one and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}(xPx)\)" src="images/3654.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.808ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3654.svg">
(<a href="#_122_52" class="pginternal">*122·52</a>); and that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/2890.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.247ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_2890.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_84"> belongs to
one of the generations of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_39">, but not to one of the generations
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_40"> arranges the whole family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_85"> in a
progression (<a href="#_122_54" class="pginternal">*122·54</a>).</p>

<p>The following general observations on the families of one-one relations
may serve to elucidate the bearing of the propositions of this section.</p>

<p>Given any relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_41">, we call <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx\)" src="images/3656.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.275ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3656.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx\cup \overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx\)" src="images/3657.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.881ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3657.svg">
the family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_86">. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_42"> is a one-one, this family may be of four
different kinds. (1) It may be a closed series, like the angles of a
polygon. This occurs if <img alt="" data-tex="\(xP_{\text{po}}x\)" src="images/3377.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.918ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_3377.svg_1">. In this case the family
forms an inductive class. (2) It may be an open series with a beginning
and an end; this occurs if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\sim}(xP_{\text{po}}x).\text{E}!\text{min}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx.\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx. \]" src="images/3658.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 42.444ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3658.svg"></span></p>

<p>In this case also the family forms an inductive class. (3) It may
be an<span class="pagenum" id="Page_255">[Pg 255]</span> open series with a beginning and no end, or an end and no
beginning. This occurs if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\sim}(xP_{\text{po}}x).\text{E}!\text{min}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx.{\sim}\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx, \]" src="images/3659.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 44.204ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3659.svg"></span>
or if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\sim}(xP_{\text{po}}x).{\sim}\text{E}!\text{min}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx.\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx. \]" src="images/3660.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 44.204ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3660.svg"></span>
In this case, the series is of the type <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_3"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cnv}ʻʻ\omega\)" src="images/3661.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.208ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3661.svg">, and is non-inductive and reflexive. (4) The
series may be open and have neither beginning nor end. This occurs if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ {\sim}(xP_{\text{po}}x).{\sim}\text{E}!\text{min}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx.{\sim}\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx \]" src="images/3662.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 45.336ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3662.svg"></span>
In this case we get a series whose relation-number is the sum (in the
sense of <a href="#_180" class="pginternal">*180</a>) of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cnv}ʻʻ\omega\)" src="images/3661.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.208ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3661.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_4">, which again is
non-inductive and reflexive. In all four cases, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_53"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg_16"> be
any two members of the family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_87">, the interval between <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_54"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg_17"> is an inductive class.</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_88"> is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/3663.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3663.svg">, or if the family of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_89"> contains a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/3663.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3663.svg_1">, cases (1) and (4)
are excluded, since the series has a beginning. In this case the number
of predecessors of any term is an inductive number. It will be observed
that every family is either wholly contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/3664.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.869ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3664.svg"> or
wholly contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/3665.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3665.svg">; families of kinds (2)
and (3) (excluding, in (2), those which have an end but no beginning)
are contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/3664.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.869ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3664.svg_1">, while families of kinds (1) and
(4), and those of (2) which have an end but no beginning, are contained
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/3665.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3665.svg_1">; families containing a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/3663.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3663.svg_2"> are contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/3664.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.869ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3664.svg_2">, while all
others are contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/3665.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3665.svg_2">.</p>

<p>Thus a one-one relation in general gives rise to a number of wholly
disconnected series, some closed, others open and with or without a
beginning or an end. The condition that all the series should be open
is <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/2888.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.875ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_2888.svg_4">.</p>

<p>The case of a <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_5">-shaped family, considered in *96, cannot arise when
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/2890.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.247ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_2890.svg_2">, for in a <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_6">-shaped family the term at the
junction of the tail and the circle has two predecessors, one in the
tail and one in the circle, so that the relation in question is not
<img alt="" data-tex="\(1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/1429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.782ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_1429.svg_5">. It follows that, when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/2890.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.247ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_2890.svg_3">, if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_208"> is a family containing a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/3663.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3663.svg_3">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \upharpoonleft P_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/3666.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 10.523ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3666.svg"> (cf. *96·23).</p>

<p>When <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻP\)" src="images/3392.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3392.svg_11"> exists, there is only one family which has a beginning. In
this case, ignoring the other families (if any), we call the members
of the family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻP\)" src="images/3392.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3392.svg_12"> respectively <img alt="" data-tex="\(1_{P}\)" src="images/3394.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.846ex;" id="img_images_3394.svg_3">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{P}\)" src="images/3395.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.846ex;" id="img_images_3395.svg_2">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(3_{P}\)" src="images/3667.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.844ex;" id="img_images_3667.svg">,
.... If the family has <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_135"> members, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_136"> is an inductive
cardinal, its last member will be <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu_{P}\)" src="images/3396.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.507ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_3396.svg_2">. If on the other hand the
number of members of the family is not an inductive cardinal, it must
be <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_15">; in this case, the family forms a progression, whose
members are <img alt="" data-tex="\(1_{P}\)" src="images/3394.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.846ex;" id="img_images_3394.svg_4">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{P}\)" src="images/3395.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.846ex;" id="img_images_3395.svg_3">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(3_{P}\)" src="images/3667.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.844ex;" id="img_images_3667.svg_1">, ..., <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu _{P}\)" src="images/3397.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.507ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_3397.svg_10">, ...,
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu _{P}\)" src="images/3397.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.507ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_3397.svg_11"> always exists when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_137"> is an inductive cardinal.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_256">[Pg 256]</span></p>

<p>In addition to the propositions already mentioned, the following are
important:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.x,y\in CʻR.\supset :xR_{\text{po}}y.\lor.x = y.\lor.yR_{\text{po}}x\)" src="images/3668.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 53.022ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3668.svg"></p>

<p>(Cf. note to <a href="#_122_21" class="pginternal">*122·21</a>, below.)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.\supset :\nu \in \text{NC induct} - \iota ʻ0.\equiv .\text{E}!\nu _{R}\)" src="images/3669.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 45.508ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3669.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·341.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .\text{D}ʻR = \hat{x} \{(\exists \nu ).\nu \in \text{NC induct} - \iota ʻ0.x = \nu _{R}\}\)" src="images/3670.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 59.849ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_3670.svg"></p>

<p>In virtue of these two propositions, the terms of a progression are
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ 1_{R},\,\, 2_{R},\,\, 3_{R},\,\, ... \nu _{R},\,\, ..., \]" src="images/3671.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 23.831ex; height: 1.946ex;" id="img_images_3671.svg"></span>
where every inductive cardinal occurs. This is the same fact as is
usually assumed when the terms are represented as
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ x_{1},\,\, x_{2},\,\, x_{3},\,\, ... x_{\nu }, .... \]" src="images/3672.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 22.131ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_3672.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·35.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\nu \in \text{NC induct} - \iota ʻ0.\supset .\overrightarrow{B}ʻR_{\nu } = R(1_{R}\vdash\dashv     \nu _{R}).\overrightarrow{B}ʻR_{\nu }\in \nu \)" src="images/3673.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 69.241ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3673.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·36.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\text{Prog} \cap  t^{11}ʻx.\supset .\text{Infin ax}(x)\)" src="images/3674.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.359ex; height: 2.452ex;" id="img_images_3674.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·37.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .\text{D}ʻR{\sim}\in \text{Cls induct}.\text{N}_{0}\text{c}ʻ\text{D}ʻR{\sim}\in \text{NC induct}\)" src="images/3675.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 60.486ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3675.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·38.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .\overrightarrow{R}_{*}ʻx\in \text{Cls induct}\)" src="images/3676.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 33.714ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_3676.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the number of terms up to any given point of a progression
is inductive.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prog} = (1\rightarrow 1)\cap \hat{R} (\text{D}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/3677.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.332ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3677.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_1">*122·1</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\equiv .R\in 1\rightarrow 1.\text{D}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR \quad[(*122·01)]\)" src="images/3678.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 57.59ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3678.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_11">*122·11</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.\equiv :R\in 1\rightarrow 1.\text{E}!BʻR:x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}.x\in \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3679.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 63.719ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_3679.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*122·1.*14·205.\supset \\ \vdash \colon\colon R\in \text{Prog}.&amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp R\in 1\rightarrow 1:(\exists a).a = BʻR.\text{D}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻa\colon\ldotp \\ [*20·43]  &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp R\in 1\rightarrow 1\colon\ldotp (\exists a):a = BʻR:x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}.x\in \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻa\colon\ldotp \\ [*14·15]  &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp R\in 1\rightarrow 1\colon\ldotp (\exists a):a = BʻR:x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}.x\in \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\colon\ldotp \\ [*14·204] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp R\in 1\rightarrow 1.\text{E}!BʻR:x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}.x\in \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\colon\colon \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3680.svg" style="vertical-align: -9.887ex; width: 87.078ex; height: 20.905ex;" id="img_images_3680.svg"></span></p>

<p>Observe that, by the conventions as to descriptive symbols,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3681.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3681.svg"> involves the
existence of <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻR\)" src="images/2904.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.792ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2904.svg_1">, whereas <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}.x\in\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3682.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 27.386ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3682.svg">
does not, since, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻR\)" src="images/2904.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.792ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2904.svg_2"> does not exist,
we have <img alt="" data-tex="\((x).x{\sim}\in \overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3683.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.468ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3683.svg">, and therefore
<img alt="" data-tex="\((x).x{\sim}\in \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/3684.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.684ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3684.svg"> will satisfy the equivalence, <i>i.e.</i>
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{\Lambda}\)" src="images/718.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 2.355ex;" id="img_images_718.svg_2"> will satisfy the equivalence although it has no first
term. This is the reason why <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!BʻR\)" src="images/3641.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.962ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3641.svg_3"> appears explicitly in
<a href="#_122_11" class="pginternal">*122·11</a>, though it was only implicit in <a href="#_122_1" class="pginternal">*122·1</a>.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·12.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\colon R\in \text{Prog}.&amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp R\in 1\rightarrow 1.\text{E}!BʻR\colon\ldotp x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv _{x}:\\ &amp;BʻR\in \alpha .\breve{R} ʻʻ\alpha \subset \alpha .\supset _{\alpha }.x\in \alpha   \quad[*122·11.*90·1]\end{align}\]" src="images/3685.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.395ex; width: 63.782ex; height: 5.921ex;" id="img_images_3685.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·15.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .R=(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R=R\upharpoonright (\overleftarrow{R}_{\text{po}}ʻBʻR)=R\upharpoonright     (\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\)" src="images/3692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 73.04ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3692.svg"></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*122·1.*35·63.  \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .R&amp;=(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R\\ [*96·2] &amp;=R\upharpoonright (\overleftarrow{R}_{\text{po}}ʻBʻR)\\ [*96·21] &amp;=R\upharpoonright (\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR):\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3693.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.015ex; width: 62.845ex; height: 13.161ex;" id="img_images_3693.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·151.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .R_{*}=(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R_{*}=R_{*}\upharpoonright     (\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\\ &amp;[35·63·66.*90·14.*122·141·1]\end{align}\]" src="images/3694.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 57.459ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_3694.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·152.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .R_{\text{po}}=(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R_{\text{po}}&amp;=R_{\text{po}}\upharpoonright     (\overleftarrow{R}_{\text{po}}ʻBʻR)\\ &amp;=R_{\text{po}}\upharpoonright (\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\\ [*35·63·66.*91·504.*121·1·14]\end{align}\]" src="images/3695.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.084ex; width: 60.389ex; height: 11.299ex;" id="img_images_3695.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_16">*122·16</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\supset .R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J  \quad[*96·23.*122·152]\)" src="images/3696.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 44.723ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3696.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition enables us to apply to progressions all the
propositions of <a href="#_121" class="pginternal">*121</a> in which we have as hypothesis
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J, or R\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J. \]" src="images/3697.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 44.242ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3697.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_17">*122·17</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\equiv .R\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR\)" src="images/3698.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 54.056ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_3698.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*35·63.  \supset \vdash :\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR.\supset .R=(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R  &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .*96·453. \supset \vdash :R\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .(\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR)\upharpoonleft     R\in 1\rightarrow 1   &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .(1).(2).*122·1. \supset \vdash :\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR.R\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\,     J.\supset .R\in \text{Prog}  &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .(3).*122·1·16.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3699.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.641ex; width: 87.337ex; height: 16.413ex;" id="img_images_3699.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_258">[Pg 258]</span></p>

<p>To illustrate this proposition, consider its application to the
inductive cardinals arranged in order of magnitude; <i>i.e.</i> take as
a value of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_34"> the relation
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \hat{\mu} \hat{\nu} (\mu \in \text{NC induct}.\nu =\mu +_{c}1). \]" src="images/3700.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.63ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_3700.svg"></span></p>

<p>We then have <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.0=BʻR\)" src="images/3701.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 21.857ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3701.svg">; also
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{NC induct}=\text{D}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}_{*}ʻBʻR. \]" src="images/3702.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 31.237ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3702.svg"></span></p>

<p>We have also
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \exists !\mu +_{c}1.\mu +_{c}1=\nu +_{c}1.\supset .\mu =\nu , \]" src="images/3703.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 34.026ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_3703.svg"></span>
so that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\upharpoonright (-\iota ʻ\Lambda )\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/3704.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.737ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3704.svg">.</p>

<p>Again
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu R_{\text{po}}\nu .\equiv .(\exists \varpi ).\varpi \in \text{NC induct}-\iota ʻ0.\nu =\mu +_{c}\varpi , \]" src="images/3705.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 49.063ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3705.svg"></span>
whence
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu R_{\text{po}}\nu .\exists !\mu .\supset .\mu \neq \nu , \]" src="images/3706.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 20.397ex; height: 2.27ex;" id="img_images_3706.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (-\iota ʻ\Lambda )\upharpoonleft R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J. \]" src="images/3707.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 17.218ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3707.svg"></span></p>

<p>But we do not get <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/726.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.288ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_726.svg_3"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/3652.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 7.14ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3652.svg_1"> unless we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Lambda {\sim}\in \text{NC induct}, \]" src="images/3708.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 16.908ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_3708.svg"></span>
which is the axiom of infinity. If this condition fails, we reach at
last an inductive cardinal which = <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_44">, and we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Lambda =\Lambda +_{c}1, \]" src="images/3709.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 11.564ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_3709.svg"></span>
so that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_45"> has two immediate predecessors, namely itself
and the last existent cardinal. The posterity of 0, in this case, is
a <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_7"> in which the circle has narrowed to a single term, namely
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_46">.</p>

<p>Thus we need the axiom of infinity in order to prove
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \hat{\mu} \hat{\nu} (\mu \in \text{NC induct}.\nu =\mu +_{c}1)\in \text{Prog}. \]" src="images/3710.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 38.086ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_3710.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.x,y\in CʻR.\supset :xR_{*}y.\lor.yR_{*}x \quad[*96·302.*122·1·141]\)" src="images/3711.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 68.198ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3711.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_21">*122·21</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.x,y\in CʻR.\supset :xR_{\text{po}}y.&amp;\lor.x=y.\lor.yR_{\text{po}}x\\ &amp;[*96·303.*122·1·141]\end{align}\]" src="images/3712.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.078ex; width: 58.825ex; height: 5.288ex;" id="img_images_3712.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition, together with <a href="#_122_16" class="pginternal">*122·16</a> and *91·56, shows that if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in \text{Prog}\)" src="images/383.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 9.173ex; height: 2.011ex;" id="img_images_383.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/3713.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_3713.svg"> has the three properties by
which transitive serial relations are defined (cf. <a href="#_204" class="pginternal">*204</a>), namely it is
(1) transitive, (2) contained in diversity, (3) connected, <i>i.e.</i>
such that it relates any two distinct members of its field. We shall at
a later stage define the ordinal number <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_5"> as the class of such
relations as <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/3713.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_3713.svg_1">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in \text{Prog}\)" src="images/383.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 9.173ex; height: 2.011ex;" id="img_images_383.svg_2">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.x,y\in \alpha -\breve{R} _{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\supset .x=y\)" src="images/3714.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 50.431ex; height: 3.064ex;" id="img_images_3714.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>

<p>This proposition shows that every existent class contained in a
progression has a first term, <i>i.e.</i> that a progression is a
well-ordered series (cf. *250).</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_260">[Pg 260]</span></p>

<p>The above proposition shows that what we may call an "arithmetical
progression" in a progression is a progression, <i>i.e.</i> if,
starting from any term of a progression, we take every other term, or
every third term, or every <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_139">th term, we still have a progression.</p>

<p>The above proposition shows that if an existent class contained in a
progression has no maximum, then any assigned member of the progression
is succeeded by members of the class.</p>

<p>The following proposition states that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_209"> has members
belonging to a progression, and there are members of the progression
which do not precede any member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_210">, then there is in the
progression a last member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_211">.</p>

<p>In virtue of <a href="#_122_34" class="pginternal">*122·34</a><a href="#_122_341" class="pginternal">·341</a>, all the terms of a progression occur in the
series <img alt="" data-tex="\(1_{R}\)" src="images/3743.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.533ex; height: 1.88ex;" id="img_images_3743.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{R}\)" src="images/3744.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.533ex; height: 1.88ex;" id="img_images_3744.svg">, ... <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu _{R}\)" src="images/3653.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.373ex;" id="img_images_3653.svg_1">, ..., and every inductive
cardinal except 0 is used in forming this series.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_263">[Pg 263]</span></p>

<p>The following series of propositions are concerned in proving that
any class contained in a progression is inductive if it has a last
term, and is a progression if it has no last term. In the latter case,
it is supposed arranged in the same order as it had in the original
progression. A certain complication is necessary in order to define
its one-one generating relation. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_35"> is the generating relation
of the original progression, we proceed first to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/3713.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_3713.svg_2">,
then to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha\)" src="images/3752.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.4ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3752.svg">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_212"> is
the class in question; this gives us a transitive generating relation
for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_213">. Calling this relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_43">, we then proceed to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\dot{-} P^{2}\)" src="images/3753.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 6.272ex; height: 2.24ex;" id="img_images_3753.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> the relation of consecutive members of
the series generated by <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_44">. This relation turns out to be one-one,
and to arrange <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_214"> in a progression; hence our proposition is
proved. The reason for the necessity of this detour is that consecutive
members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_215"> may not be consecutive members of the original
progression.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset R(BʻR\vdash\dashv y).y\in \alpha .\supset .y= \text{max}_{R}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/3756.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 53.328ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3756.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_43">*122·43</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :R\in  \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\exists !\alpha -R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\alpha \in \text{Cls induct}\\ &amp;[*122·41.*121·45.*120·481]\end{align}\]" src="images/3758.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.078ex; width: 55.572ex; height: 5.288ex;" id="img_images_3758.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus every class which is contained in a progression and has a last
term is inductive. We have next to prove
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R\in  \text{Prog} .\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\exists !\alpha .{\sim}\exists !\alpha -R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\alpha \in \text{D}ʻʻ\text{Prog}. \]" src="images/3759.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 58.161ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3759.svg"></span>
This is effected in the following propositions.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·44.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :R\in  \text{Prog} .\alpha \subset R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\exists !\alpha .P=R_{\text{po}}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha .Q&amp;=P\dot{-} P^{2}.\supset     .\\ &amp;Q\in 1\rightarrow 1.Q\,\unicode{x2abd}\, R_{\text{po}}\end{align}\]" src="images/3760.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.299ex; width: 62.763ex; height: 5.729ex;" id="img_images_3760.svg"></span></p>

conclusion, but is the hypothesis required for <a href="#_122_45" class="pginternal">*122·45</a>, for which the
present and the following propositions are lemmas.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_45">*122·45</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\exists !\alpha .P = R_{\text{po}}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha .Q = P\dot{-} P^{2}.\supset     .\\ &amp;Q\in \text{Prog}.\text{D}ʻQ = \alpha     \quad[*122·44·444·441]\end{align}\]" src="images/3775.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.257ex; width: 57.612ex; height: 5.645ex;" id="img_images_3775.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition shows that every series extracted from a progression
and having no last term is a progression.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_46">*122·46</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\supset :\alpha \in \text{Cls induct} \cup  \text{D}ʻʻ\text{Prog}\\ &amp;[*122·43·45.*120·212]\end{align}\]" src="images/3776.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 52.608ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_3776.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition shows that any number less than the number of terms in
a progression is inductive. This result will be developed in the next
number (<a href="#_123" class="pginternal">*123</a>).</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·47.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\supset :\alpha \in \text{Cls induct} - \iota ʻ\Lambda .\equiv .\exists !\alpha -R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha     \)" src="images/3777.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 65.21ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_3777.svg"></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*122·45.&amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\exists !\alpha .{\sim}\exists !\alpha -R_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\alpha \in \text{D}ʻʻ\text{Prog}.\\ [*122·37]    &amp;\supset .\alpha {\sim}\in \text{Cls induct}  &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*122·43.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3778.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.775ex; width: 82.94ex; height: 8.681ex;" id="img_images_3778.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·48.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\alpha \in \text{Cls induct}.\supset .\text{D}ʻR-\alpha {\sim}\in \text{Cls induct}\)" src="images/3779.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 64.636ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3779.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*120·71.&amp;\supset \vdash :\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\alpha ,\text{D}ʻR-\alpha \in \text{Cls induct}.\supset .\text{D}ʻR\in \text{Cls induct}:\\ [\text{Transp}]    &amp;\supset \vdash :\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\alpha \in \text{Cls induct}.\text{D}ʻR{\sim}\in \text{Cls induct}.\supset .\\ &amp;\text{D}ʻR-\alpha {\sim}\text{Cls induct}  &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*122·37.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3780.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 98.395ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_3780.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*122·49.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :R\in \text{Prog}.\alpha \subset \text{D}ʻR.\alpha \in \text{Cls induct}.\supset .\text{D}ʻR-\alpha \in \text{D}ʻʻ\text{Prog}\\ &amp;[*122·46·48]\end{align}\]" src="images/3781.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 62.631ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_3781.svg"></span></p>

<p>The following propositions are concerned with circumstances under which
the posterity or the family of a term forms a progression.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_51">*122·51</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.I_{P}ʻx=\Lambda .x\in \text{D}ʻP.\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx\subset \text{D}ʻP.\supset .(\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx)\upharpoonleft     P\in \text{Prog}\)" src="images/3782.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 73.259ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3782.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*71·261.*96·13.\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.Q&amp;=(\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx)\upharpoonleft P.\supset .\\ &amp;Q\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.Q_{\text{po}}=(\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx)\upharpoonleft P_{\text{po}}. &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [*96·104]   &amp;\supset .Q_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .*35·61.*37·4.  \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}(1).\supset .\text{D}ʻQ=\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx.\text{ᗡ}ʻQ&amp;=\breve{P} ʻʻ\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ [*91·52]  &amp;=\overleftarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻx\\ [(1)]  &amp;=\overleftarrow{Q}_{\text{po}}ʻx\\ [(2).*91·542]  &amp;=\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻx-\iota ʻx &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \vdash .(1).(3).(4). &amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}(1).\supset .\text{D}ʻQ=\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻx.\text{ᗡ}ʻQ=\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻx-\iota ʻx.\\ [*93·101]  &amp;\supset .\overrightarrow{B}ʻQ=\iota ʻx.\text{D}ʻQ=\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻx &amp;\qquad \text{(5)}\\ \vdash .(1).(2).(5).\supset \\ \vdash :\text{Hp}.Q&amp;=(\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx)\upharpoonleft P.\supset .Q\in  \text{Cls} \rightarrow 1.Q_{\text{po}}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\text{D}ʻQ=\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻBʻQ.\\ [*122·17]  &amp;\supset .Q\in  \text{Prog} :\supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3784.svg" style="vertical-align: -25.125ex; width: 121.853ex; height: 51.381ex;" id="img_images_3784.svg"></span></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*96·492.\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .I_{P}ʻx=\Lambda &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*122·51.\supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/3786.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.149ex; width: 42.497ex; height: 5.43ex;" id="img_images_3786.svg"></span></p>

<p>The remaining propositions (<a href="#_122_53" class="pginternal">*122·53</a><a href="#_122_54" class="pginternal">·54</a><a href="#_122_55" class="pginternal">·55</a>) are not used in the sequel.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_122_53">*122·53</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in 1\rightarrow 1.x\in sʻ \text{gen}ʻP.\overleftarrow{P}_{*}ʻx\subset \text{D}ʻP.\supset .(\overleftrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻx)\upharpoonleft     P\in  \text{Prog}\)" src="images/3787.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 64.691ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_3787.svg"></p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_268">[Pg 268]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_123">*123. <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_16">.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *123.</p>

<p>In this number we are concerned with the arithmetical properties of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_17">, the smallest of Cantor's transfinite cardinals.
Cantor defines <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_18"> as the cardinal number of any class
which can be put into one-one relation with the inductive cardinals.
This definition assumes that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu \neq \nu +_{c}1\)" src="images/3793.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 10.193ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_3793.svg">, when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_140">
is an inductive cardinal; in other words, it assumes the axiom of
infinity; for without this, the inductive cardinals would form a
finite series, with a last term, namely <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_47">. For this reason
among others, we do not make similarity with the inductive cardinals
our <i>definition</i>. We define <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_19"> as the class of
those classes which can be arranged in progressions, <i>i.e.</i> as
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻʻ\text{Prog}\)" src="images/3794.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 9.133ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_3794.svg">. We then have to prove that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_20">
so defined is a cardinal, and that if it is not null, it is the number
of the inductive numbers.</p>

<p>For convenience we put for the moment <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg"> for the relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_156">
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu +_{c}1\)" src="images/3325.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.142ex; height: 1.995ex;" id="img_images_3325.svg_1"> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_157"> is an inductive cardinal. We then easily
prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·21·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .N\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.\text{D}ʻN=\text{NC induct}.BʻN=0.\overleftarrow{N}_{*}ʻ0=\text{NC induct}\)" src="images/3796.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 64.031ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_3796.svg"></p>

<p>The only thing further required to prove <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\in \text{Prog}\)" src="images/3797.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 9.465ex; height: 2.011ex;" id="img_images_3797.svg"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/3798.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.579ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_3798.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu ,\nu \in \text{NC induct}.\mu +_{c}1=\nu +_{c}1.\supset .\mu =\nu . \]" src="images/3799.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 42.893ex; height: 2.084ex;" id="img_images_3799.svg"></span></p>

<p>By <a href="#_120_311" class="pginternal">*120·311</a>, this holds if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists !\mu +_{c}1\)" src="images/3800.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 8.029ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_3800.svg">, which holds if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Infin ax}\)" src="images/380.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 7.545ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_380.svg_3"> holds. Hence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·25·26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{Infin ax}(x).\supset .N\unicode{x0294f}t^{3}ʻx\in \text{Prog}.\text{NC induct}\cap t^{3}ʻx\in \aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3801.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 55.586ex; height: 2.451ex;" id="img_images_3801.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">whence, by <a href="#_123_36" class="pginternal">*123·36</a>,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·27.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\aleph _{0}(x).\supset .\text{NC induct}\cap t^{3}ʻx\in \aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3802.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.013ex; height: 2.451ex;" id="img_images_3802.svg"></p>

<p>Again it is obvious from <a href="#_122_34" class="pginternal">*122·34</a><a href="#_122_341" class="pginternal">·341</a> that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_36"> is a progression,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_4"> can always be put into a <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/1429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.782ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_1429.svg_6"> relation
to the inductive cardinals (<a href="#_123_3" class="pginternal">*123·3</a>) since <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_5"> consists of
the terms <img alt="" data-tex="\(1_{R}\)" src="images/3743.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.533ex; height: 1.88ex;" id="img_images_3743.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{R}\)" src="images/3744.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.533ex; height: 1.88ex;" id="img_images_3744.svg_1">, ... <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu _{R}\)" src="images/3653.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.373ex; width: 2.52ex; height: 1.373ex;" id="img_images_3653.svg_2">, ..., and all the
inductive cardinals are used in putting <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_6"> into this form.
Hence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \in \aleph _{0}.\supset .\alpha \text{ sm }\text{NC induct}\)" src="images/3803.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 28.534ex; height: 1.97ex;" id="img_images_3803.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">whence also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·311.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha ,\beta \in \aleph _{0}.\supset .\alpha \text{ sm }\beta\)" src="images/3804.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 21.918ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_3804.svg"></p>

<p>It remains to prove that any class similar to the inductive cardinals
is an <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_21">; this can only be proved by assuming the axiom
of infinity. We prove<span class="pagenum" id="Page_269">[Pg 269]</span> first (<a href="#_120_32" class="pginternal">*120·32</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_37"> is a progression,
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_16"> is a one-one whose converse domain is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2909.svg_7">,
then <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\mid R\mid \breve{S}\)" src="images/3805.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 8.407ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_3805.svg"> is a progression whose domain is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻS\)" src="images/3806.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.545ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3806.svg">. Hence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·321.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \in \aleph _{0}.\alpha \text{ sm }\beta .\supset .\beta \in \aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3807.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 27.054ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_3807.svg"></p>

<p>From this and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_216">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta \in \aleph _{0}.\supset .\alpha\text{ sm }\beta\)" src="images/3808.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 16.825ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_3808.svg">,
we obtain</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·322.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \in \aleph _{0}.\supset .\aleph _{0}=\text{Nc}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/3809.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 23.89ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3809.svg"></p>

<p>Hence by our previous results</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{Infin ax}(x).\supset .\aleph _{0}=\text{Nc}ʻ(\text{NC induct}\cap t^{3}ʻx)\)" src="images/3810.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 45.372ex; height: 2.451ex;" id="img_images_3810.svg"></p>

<p>Also we have, by <a href="#_120_322" class="pginternal">*120·322</a> above,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \exists !\aleph _{0}.\supset .\aleph _{0}\in \text{NC}, \]" src="images/3811.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 17.124ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_3811.svg"></span>
whence, since <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda \in \text{NC}\)" src="images/3812.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 7.666ex; height: 1.71ex;" id="img_images_3812.svg">, we obtain at last</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·36.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\aleph _{0}\in \text{NC}\)" src="images/3813.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 10.855ex; height: 1.97ex;" id="img_images_3813.svg"></p>

<p>As to the existence of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_22"> in various types, if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Infin ax}(x)\)" src="images/3814.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.6ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_3814.svg"> holds, <i>i.e.</i> if, given any inductive
cardinal <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_141">, there are classes having <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_142"> terms and composed
of terms of the same type as <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_90">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{NC induct}(tʻx)\in\aleph _{0}(t^{2}ʻx)\)" src="images/3815.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.764ex; height: 2.452ex;" id="img_images_3815.svg">.
Thus</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·37.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{Infin ax}(x).\supset .\exists !\aleph _{0}(t^{2}ʻx).\aleph _{0}(t^{2}ʻx)\in \text{N}_{0}\text{C}\)" src="images/3816.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.161ex; height: 2.452ex;" id="img_images_3816.svg"></p>

<p>The arithmetical properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.37ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_295.svg_23"> in regard to addition,
multiplication and exponentiation by an inductive cardinal are easily
proved. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \in \text{NC induct}.\supset .\aleph _{0}=\aleph _{0}+_{c}\nu\)" src="images/3817.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 33.163ex; height: 1.97ex;" id="img_images_3817.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·421.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\aleph _{0}=\aleph _{0}+_{c}\aleph _{0}=2\times _{c}\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3818.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 26.326ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_3818.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·422.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \in \text{NC induct}-\iota ʻ0.\supset .\nu \times _{c}\aleph _{0}=\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3819.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 39.469ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3819.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·52.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\aleph _{0}=\aleph _{0}\times _{c}\aleph _{0}=\aleph _{0}^{2}\)" src="images/3820.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.687ex; width: 21.549ex; height: 2.573ex;" id="img_images_3820.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*123·53.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \in \text{NC induct}-\iota ʻ0.\supset .\aleph _{0}^\nu =\aleph _{0}\)" src="images/3821.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.687ex; width: 34.672ex; height: 2.383ex;" id="img_images_3821.svg"></p>

<p>All these propositions are well known.</p>

immediate consequences of propositions proved in <a href="#_122" class="pginternal">*122</a>.</p>
