<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_458">[Pg 458]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_176">*176. EXPONENTIATION.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *176.</p>

<p>The definition of exponentiation is framed on the analogy of the
definition in cardinals, <i>i.e.</i> we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q=\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{,.}^{;}Q \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/5912.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 29.915ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5912.svg"></span>
We put also, what is often a more convenient form,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P^{Q}=\dot{s} ^{;}(P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q) \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/5913.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 23.518ex; height: 2.626ex;" id="img_images_5913.svg"></span></p>

<p>The relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_5"> has for its field (unless <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q=\dot{\Lambda}\)" src="images/5914.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.377ex; height: 2.794ex;" id="img_images_5914.svg">) the
class of Cantor's "Belegungen," <i>i.e.</i> the class <img alt="" data-tex="\((CʻP\uparrow CʻQ)_{\Delta }ʻCʻQ\)" src="images/5915.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.535ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5915.svg">.
It arranges these by a form of the principle of
first differences, namely as follows : Suppose <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_31"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_26"> are two
members of <img alt="" data-tex="\((CʻP\uparrow CʻQ)_{\Delta }ʻCʻQ\)" src="images/5915.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.535ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5915.svg_1">, and suppose there is
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_38"> a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_90"> for which the <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_32">-representative <img alt="" data-tex="\((Mʻy)\)" src="images/5916.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 6.604ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5916.svg">
precedes the <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_27">-representative <img alt="" data-tex="\((Nʻy)\)" src="images/5917.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 6.235ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5917.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> for which
<img alt="" data-tex="\((Mʻy)P(Nʻy)\)" src="images/5465.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.538ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5465.svg_1">, and suppose further that all terms in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_39"> which
are earlier than <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_91">, <i>i.e.</i> for which <img alt="" data-tex="\(zQy.z\neq y\)" src="images/5918.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 10.134ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_5918.svg">, have
their <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_33">-representative and their <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_28">-representative identical;
in this case we say that <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_34"> has to <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_29"> the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_6">. This
may be stated as follows, provided we assume that <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_264"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_179"> are
series: Let <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_35"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_30"> be two one-valued functions whose possible
arguments are all the members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_40">, while their values are some
or all of the members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_62">. Then we say that <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_36"> has to <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_31">
the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_7"> if the first argument for which the two functions
do not have the same value gives an earlier value to <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_37"> than to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_32">.</p>

<figure class="figcenter width500" style="width: 1200px;" id="i_458">
<img alt="Diagram showing two ordered sets: P={a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₅} (top row, 5 elements) and Q={b₁,b₂,b₃,b₄} (bottom row, 4 elements), each represented by dots with subscripted labels. Arrows indicate P and Q as distinct ordered sequences, illustrating sets with different cardinalities in formal logic or set theory." height="585" src="images/i_458.jpg" width="1200" id="img_images_i_458.jpg">
</figure>

<p>Thus for example let <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_265"> be the series <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{1}\)" src="images/5919.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5919.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{2}\)" src="images/5920.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5920.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{3}\)" src="images/5921.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.372ex;" id="img_images_5921.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{4}\)" src="images/5922.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5922.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{5}\)" src="images/5923.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.372ex;" id="img_images_5923.svg">, and let <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_180"> be the series <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{1}\)" src="images/5924.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5924.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{2}\)" src="images/5925.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5925.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{3}\)" src="images/5926.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_5926.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{4}\)" src="images/5927.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5927.svg">. Then <img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_38"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_33"> are to be such
that <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb\)" src="images/5928.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.706ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5928.svg"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(Nʻb\)" src="images/5929.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.337ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5929.svg"> is defined when, and only when, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b\)" src="images/5930.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.971ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_5930.svg"> is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{1}\)" src="images/5924.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5924.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{2}\)" src="images/5925.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5925.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{3}\)" src="images/5926.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_5926.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{4}\)" src="images/5927.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5927.svg_1">, and the value of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb\)" src="images/5928.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.706ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5928.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(Nʻb\)" src="images/5929.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.337ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5929.svg_1"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{1}\)" src="images/5919.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5919.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{2}\)" src="images/5920.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5920.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{3}\)" src="images/5921.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.372ex;" id="img_images_5921.svg_1"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{4}\)" src="images/5922.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.337ex;" id="img_images_5922.svg_1">
or <img alt="" data-tex="\(a_{5}\)" src="images/5923.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.185ex; height: 1.372ex;" id="img_images_5923.svg_1">. Then if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb_{1} = a_{1}\)" src="images/5931.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.895ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5931.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Nʻb_{1} \neq a_{1}\)" src="images/5932.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 10.526ex; height: 2.183ex;" id="img_images_5932.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(M\)" src="images/1671.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.378ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_1671.svg_39"> precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(N\)" src="images/3795.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.009ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_3795.svg_34">; if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb_{1} = Nʻb_{1} = a_{1}\)" src="images/5933.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 19.237ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5933.svg">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb_{2} = a_{1} . Nʻb_{2} \neq a_{1}\)" src="images/5934.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 22.428ex; height: 2.183ex;" id="img_images_5934.svg">,

Thus in this case the first term of
the series generated by <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_8"> is the one for which <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻb = a_{1}\)" src="images/5935.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.907ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5935.svg">
when <img alt="" data-tex="\(b\)" src="images/5930.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.971ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_5930.svg_1"> has any of the values <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{1}\)" src="images/5924.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5924.svg_2">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{2}\)" src="images/5925.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5925.svg_2">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{3}\)" src="images/5926.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.945ex;" id="img_images_5926.svg_2">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(b_{4}\)" src="images/5927.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 1.958ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_5927.svg_2">. Thus the first term of the series is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻa_{1}\uparrow CʻQ\)" src="images/5936.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.598ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5936.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻBʻP\uparrow CʻQ\)" src="images/5937.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.187ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5937.svg">. The next term will be
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} \iota ʻa_{1}\uparrow &amp;(\iota ʻb_{1}\cup \iota ʻb_{2}\cup \iota ʻb_{3})\unicode{x228d} \iota ʻa_{2}\uparrow \iota ʻb_{4},\\ \textit{i.e.}\quad &amp;\iota ʻBʻP\uparrow \text{D}ʻQ\unicode{x228d} 2_{P}\downarrow BʻQ. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/5938.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 38.076ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_5938.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_459">[Pg 459]</span>
The next is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻBʻP\uparrow \text{D}ʻQ\unicode{x228d}3_{P}\downarrow Bʻ\breve{Q}\)" src="images/5939.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.326ex; height: 2.914ex;" id="img_images_5939.svg">,
and so on. This makes it evident that our series has the structure
required of a series which is to represent the <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_181">th power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_266">.</p>

<p>The two relations <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q\)" src="images/5940.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 8.457ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5940.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_9"> are ordinally
similar, since <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{s}\)" src="images/722.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.061ex; height: 1.758ex;" id="img_images_722.svg_5"> is one-one when its field is limited to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Cʻ(P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5941.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 13.294ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5941.svg">. This follows from <a href="#_116_131" class="pginternal">*116·131</a>, together with
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \dot{\exists} !Q.\supset .Cʻ(P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)=(CʻP)\,\,\text{exp}\,\,(CʻQ). \]" src="images/5942.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 42.52ex; height: 2.871ex;" id="img_images_5942.svg"></span></p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_58"> is a correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_267"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P'\)" src="images/5221.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.452ex; height: 1.717ex;" id="img_images_5221.svg_2">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(T\)" src="images/1448.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.593ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_1448.svg_20"> is a correlator
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_182"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q'\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.417ex; height: 2.156ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_3">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\((S \parallel \breve{T} )_{\in }\)" src="images/5943.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.455ex; height: 2.966ex;" id="img_images_5943.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\((S\parallel \breve{T})\)" src="images/5944.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.2ex; height: 2.966ex;" id="img_images_5944.svg">, with their converse domains limited,
are respectively correlators of <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5945.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.217ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5945.svg"> with
<img alt="" data-tex="\((Pʻ\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Qʻ)\)" src="images/5946.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.932ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5946.svg"> and of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_10"> with <img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻ^{Qʻ}\)" src="images/5947.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.47ex; height: 2.474ex;" id="img_images_5947.svg">. This
shows that the relation-number of <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5945.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.217ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5945.svg_1"> depends
only upon those of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_268"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_183">, which is of course essential if
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\,\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5945.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.217ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5945.svg_2"> is to afford a definition of exponentiation.</p>

<p>If the multiplicative axiom is assumed, then if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_56"> is a relation
which is like <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_184">, and whose field consists of relations which
are like <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_269">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}\)" src="images/5948.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.602ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_5948.svg">, the product
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_57"> is like <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5949.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.839ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5949.svg">. That is, if we put
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu =\text{Nr}ʻP.\nu =\text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/5950.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 20.975ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_5950.svg">, so that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_58"> consists of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_164"> terms each of which has <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_181"> terms, the product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_59"> has
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_15"> terms. This gives the connection of multiplication with
exponentiation.</p>

<p>There are two formal laws of exponentiation which hold for
relation-numbers, namely
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} P^{Q}&amp;\times P^{R}\text{smor}P^{Q\unicode{x2909}R}\\ \text{and}\quad &amp;(P^{Q})^{R}\text{smor}P^{R\times Q}. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/5951.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.437ex; width: 23.509ex; height: 6.005ex;" id="img_images_5951.svg"></span>
They both need a hypothesis: the first needs
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \dot{\exists} !Q.\dot{\exists} !R.CʻQ\cap CʻR=\Lambda, \]" src="images/5952.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 26.684ex; height: 2.758ex;" id="img_images_5952.svg"></span>
while the second needs <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J\)" src="images/5953.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.262ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5953.svg"> because it is proved by
means of the associative law (<a href="#_174_43" class="pginternal">*174·43</a>).</p>

<p>The first of the above formal laws can be generalized, by putting
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\Sigma ʻS\)" src="images/5119.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.45ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5119.svg_1"> in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\unicode{x2909}R\)" src="images/4929.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.864ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4929.svg_1">, and taking the product
of the various powers
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q,\quad P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q', ..., \]" src="images/5954.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 24.708ex; height: 2.269ex;" id="img_images_5954.svg"></span>
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_185">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q'\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.417ex; height: 2.156ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_4">, ... <img alt="" data-tex="\(\in CʻS\)" src="images/5955.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.674ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5955.svg">, and the products are taken in the
order determined by <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_59">. The resulting generalization is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ S\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.S\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .\{\text{Prod}ʻ(P \,\text{exp}\,\,)^{;}S\}\text{smor}\{P\,\text{exp}\,\,(\Sigma ʻS)\}. \]" src="images/5956.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 60.891ex; height: 2.584ex;" id="img_images_5956.svg"></span></p>

<p>The proof of this proposition results immediately from <a href="#_174_43" class="pginternal">*174·43</a> and
<a href="#_162_35" class="pginternal">*162·35</a>.</p>

<p>The proof of the second of the formal laws is more difficult. We
observe, to begin with, that
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P\,\text{exp}\,\,(R\times Q)=\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}\Sigma ʻQ\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R. \]" src="images/5957.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 39.27ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5957.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_460">[Pg 460]</span></p>

<p>Assuming suitable hypotheses, this, by <a href="#_162_35" class="pginternal">*162·35</a>,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ =\text{Prod}ʻ\Sigma ʻ(P\downarrow_{.,} )\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R, \]" src="images/5958.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 28.094ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5958.svg"></span>
which is like <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻ\text{Prod}^{;}(P\downarrow_{.,})\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\)" src="images/5959.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 27.534ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5959.svg">,
by <a href="#_174_43" class="pginternal">*174·43</a>. But
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\,\text{exp}\,\,R=\text{Prod}ʻ{\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,}^{;}Q}\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\)" src="images/5960.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 43.649ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5960.svg">.
Thus our result will follow if we can prove
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \{\text{Prod}^{;}(P\downarrow_{.,} )\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\}\,\text{smor smor}\,\{(\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,}     ^{;}Q)\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\}. \]" src="images/5961.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 57.495ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5961.svg"></span>
Now one member of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}^{;}(P\downarrow_{.,})\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\)" src="images/5962.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 21.36ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5962.svg">
will be
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} z,\, \text{where}\, z\in CʻR. \]" src="images/5963.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 34.436ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5963.svg"></span></p>

<p>This is like <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\)" src="images/5964.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 13.128ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5964.svg">, because
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\downarrow_{.,} z\,\text{smor}\,Q\)" src="images/5965.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 13.646ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_5965.svg">. Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}^{;}(P\downarrow_{.,})\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,}^{;}R\)" src="images/5966.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 21.36ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5966.svg">
is a series of terms each of which is like
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\)" src="images/5964.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 13.128ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5964.svg_1">, and the whole series of such
terms is like <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_60">. If we assumed the multiplicative axiom, this would
suffice to prove the result. But it is possible to obtain our result
without assuming the multiplicative axiom.</p>

<p>For this purpose, we proceed as follows. The correlator of
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} z\, \text{and}\, \text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q \]" src="images/5967.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 35.177ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5967.svg"></span>
is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\{\mid (\text{Cnv}ʻ\downarrow z)\}_{\in }\)" src="images/5968.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.418ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_5968.svg">, by <a href="#_165_361" class="pginternal">*165·361</a> and
<a href="#_172_3" class="pginternal">*172·3</a>. Call this <img alt="" data-tex="\(Mʻz\)" src="images/2534.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.787ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2534.svg_3">. Then
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} M\in 1\rightarrow 1:&amp;z\in CʻR.\supset _{z}.(Mʻz)\in (\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} z)\,\overline{\text{smor}}\,(\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,}     ^{;}Q):\\ &amp;z,w\in CʻR.\exists !\text{D}ʻMʻz\cap \text{D}ʻMʻw.\supset _{z,w}.z=w. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/5969.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.247ex; width: 75.914ex; height: 5.625ex;" id="img_images_5969.svg"></span>
This, by the help of two or three lemmas, suffices to prove that
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \{\text{Prod}^{;}(P\downarrow_{.,} )\dagger ^{;}Q\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\}\,\text{smor smor}\,\{(\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,}     ^{;}Q)\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}R\}, \]" src="images/5970.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 57.495ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5970.svg"></span>
whence the result follows.</p>

<p>The principal propositions of the present number are the following:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q=\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q=\text{D}^{;}\Pi ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\)" src="images/5971.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 41.999ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5971.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .P^{Q}=\dot{s} ^{;}(P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)=\dot{s} ^{;}\text{Prod}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q=\dot{s} ^{;}\text{D}^{;}\Pi     ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q\)" src="images/5972.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 55.135ex; height: 2.817ex;" id="img_images_5972.svg"></p>

<p>These propositions merely embody the definitions.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\dot{\exists} !Q.\supset .Cʻ(P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)=(CʻP)\,\text{exp}\,\,(CʻQ).CʻP^{Q}=(CʻP\uparrow CʻQ)_{\Delta }ʻCʻQ\)" src="images/5973.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 75.688ex; height: 2.871ex;" id="img_images_5973.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·151.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp P=\dot{\Lambda} .\lor.Q=\dot{\Lambda} :\equiv .P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q=\dot{\Lambda} .\equiv .P^{Q}=\dot{\Lambda}\)" src="images/5974.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 47.906ex; height: 2.794ex;" id="img_images_5974.svg"></p>

<p>It will be observed that in relation-arithmetic, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^{0} = 0\)" src="images/5975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.5ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_5975.svg">,
whereas in cardinal arithmetic <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^{0} = 1\)" src="images/5976.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.5ex; height: 2.375ex;" id="img_images_5976.svg">. The difference is due to
the fact that there is no ordinal number 1 (cf. <a href="#_153" class="pginternal">*153</a>).</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_461">[Pg 461]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·181.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .P^{Q}\,\text{smor}\,(P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\)" src="images/5977.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.055ex; height: 2.513ex;" id="img_images_5977.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·182.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  . (P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q)\,\text{smor}\,(\Pi ʻP \downarrow_{.,}  ^{;}Q)\)" src="images/5978.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 29.546ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_5978.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·19.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash  \colon\colon S (P^{Q}) &amp;T . \equiv  \colon\ldotp  S, T \in  (CʻP \uparrow  CʻQ)_\Delta ʻCʻQ\colon\ldotp \\ &amp;(\exists y) : y \in  CʻQ . (Sʻy) P (Tʻy) : yʻQy . yʻ \neq  y . \supset _y . Sʻyʻ = Tʻyʻ\end{align}\]" src="images/5979.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.269ex; width: 72.163ex; height: 5.669ex;" id="img_images_5979.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·2.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash  : U \upharpoonright  CʻR \in  P\, &amp;\overline{\text{smor}}\, R . W \upharpoonright  CʻS \in  Q \overline{\text{smor}}  S . \supset  .\\ &amp;(U \parallel  \breve{W} )_\in  \upharpoonright  Cʻ(R \,\text{exp}\,\, S) \in  (P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q) \,\overline{\text{smor}}\,(R \,\text{exp}\,\, S)\end{align}\]" src="images/5980.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.412ex; width: 68.209ex; height: 5.955ex;" id="img_images_5980.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·21.</b> With the same hypothesis, <img alt="" data-tex="\((U \parallel  \breve{W} ) \upharpoonright  Cʻ(R^{S})\)" src="images/5981.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.229ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_5981.svg"> correlates <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{Q}\)" src="images/5458.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 3.278ex; height: 1.948ex;" id="img_images_5458.svg_11"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{S}\)" src="images/5982.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.937ex; height: 1.997ex;" id="img_images_5982.svg">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  : P \,\text{smor}\,R . Q\,\text{smor}\,S . \supset  . (P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q)\,\text{smor}\,(R \,\text{exp}\,\, S) . P^{Q} \text{smor} R^{S}\)" src="images/5983.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 62.114ex; height: 2.515ex;" id="img_images_5983.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*176·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  \colon\ldotp  \text{Mult ax} . \supset  : R \in  \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl} \cap  \text{Nr}ʻQ . CʻR \subset  \text{Nr}ʻP . \supset  . \Pi ʻR\,\text{smor}\,(P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q)\)" src="images/5984.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 74.389ex; height: 2.584ex;" id="img_images_5984.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition connects multiplication and exponentiation.</p>

<p>The above proposition is used in <a href="#_176_19" class="pginternal">*176·19</a>. It has the merit of giving a
direct formula for <img alt="" data-tex="\(P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q\)" src="images/5998.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 8.079ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5998.svg">, instead of one which proceeds

<p>Owing to this proposition, propositions stating analogies between
ordinal and cardinal powers mostly require the hypothesis

index is zero is itself zero, whereas a cardinal power whose index is
zero is 1.</p>

<h2 class="nobreak" id="_177">
*177. PROPOSITIONS CONNECTING <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{df}}\)" src="images/5.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.357ex; width: 3.019ex; height: 1.902ex;" id="img_images_5.svg_12"> WITH PRODUCTS AND POWERS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *177.</p>

<p>The principal proposition on this subject is</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*177*13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :x\neq y.\supset .P_{\text{df}}\,\text{smor}\,\{(x\downarrow y)^{P}\}\)" src="images/6074.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.604ex; height: 2.48ex;" id="img_images_6074.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which is the analogue of <a href="#_116_72" class="pginternal">*116·72</a>, or rather leads to the analogue of
*116·72 as soon as powers of relation-numbers have been defined; for
then it becomes
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P_{\text{df}}\in 2_{r}^{\text{Nr}ʻP}. \]" src="images/6075.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.576ex; width: 11.721ex; height: 2.711ex;" id="img_images_6075.svg"></span>
Another proposition is an extension of <a href="#_171_69" class="pginternal">*171·69</a>, namely</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*177·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.P\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .\text{Prod}ʻ\text{df}^{;}P \,\text{smor}\,(\Sigma ʻP)_{\text{df}}\)" src="images/6076.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.269ex; height: 2.584ex;" id="img_images_6076.svg"></p>

<p>where we put <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{df}ʻQ=Q_{\text{df}}\)" src="images/6077.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.471ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6077.svg">.</p>

<p>The remaining propositions of this number are lemmas for the above two.</p>

<p><a href="#_177_13" class="pginternal">*177·13</a> shows, for example, that all classes of finite integers can be
arranged in a series of which the relation-number is <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{r}^\omega\)" src="images/6078.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.576ex; width: 2.314ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_6078.svg">,
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/2870.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2870.svg_7"> is the relation-number of the series of finite
integers. <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{r}^\omega\)" src="images/6078.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.576ex; width: 2.314ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_6078.svg_1"> is not the relation-number of the continuum,
but is closely allied to it.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*177·1.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :x\neq y.T=\hat{\mu} \hat{R} &amp;[R\in \{(\iota ʻx\cup \iota ʻy)\uparrow \alpha\}_{\Delta }ʻ\alpha .\mu =\overleftarrow{R}ʻx].\supset .\\ &amp;T\in (\text{Cl}ʻ\alpha )\,\overline{\text{ sm }}\, \{(\iota ʻx\cup \iota ʻy)\uparrow \alpha\}_{\Delta }ʻ\alpha     \quad[*116·712·713·715]\end{align}\]" src="images/6079.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.8ex; width: 77.155ex; height: 6.731ex;" id="img_images_6079.svg"></span></p>

<p>In the propositions of <a href="#_116" class="pginternal">*116</a> referred to, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_69"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{V}\)" src="images/208.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.697ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_208.svg_4">
appear in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_135"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_92">, but no property of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\)" src="images/194.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.57ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_194.svg_70"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{V}\)" src="images/208.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.697ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_208.svg_5"> is used in the proof except <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda\neq \text{V}\)" src="images/6080.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 6.284ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_6080.svg">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*177·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{Hp}*177·1.\alpha =CʻP.\supset .T^;(x\downarrow y)^P=P_{\text{df}}\)" src="images/6081.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.862ex; height: 2.48ex;" id="img_images_6081.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*176·19.\supset \\ \vdash \colon\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset \colon\colon\mu \{T^{;}(x\downarrow y)^{P}\}\nu     .&amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp (\exists R,S):R,S\in \{(\iota ʻx\cup \iota ʻy)\uparrow CʻP\}_{\Delta }ʻCʻP:\\ &amp;(\exists z):z\in CʻP.Rʻz(x\downarrow y)Sʻz:\\ &amp;wPz.w\neq z.\supset _{w}.Rʻw=Sʻw:\mu =\overleftarrow{R}ʻx.\nu =\overleftarrow{S}ʻx\colon\ldotp \\ [*55·13] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp (\exists R,S):R,S\in {(\iota ʻx\cup \iota ʻy)\uparrow CʻP}_{\Delta }ʻCʻP\colon\ldotp \\ &amp;(\exists z)\colon\ldotp z\in CʻP.Rʻz=x.Sʻz=y\colon\ldotp \mu =\overleftarrow{R}ʻx.\nu =\overleftarrow{S}ʻx\colon\ldotp \\ &amp;wPz.w\neq z.\supset _{w}:xRw.\equiv .xSw:yRw.\equiv .ySw\colon\ldotp \\ [*71·36] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp (\exists R,S):R,S\in {(\iota ʻx\cup \iota ʻy)\uparrow CʻP}_{\Delta }CʻP\colon\ldotp \\ &amp;(\exists z)\colon\ldotp z\in CʻP.z\in \mu -\nu .\mu =\overleftarrow{R}ʻx.\nu =\overleftarrow{S}ʻx\colon\ldotp \\ &amp;wPz.w\neq z.\supset _{w}:w\in \mu .\equiv .w\in \nu \colon\ldotp \\ [*177·1] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp \mu ,\nu \in \text{Cl}ʻCʻP\colon\ldotp (\exists z)\colon\ldotp z\in CʻP.z\in \mu -\nu \colon\ldotp \\ &amp;wPz.w\neq z.\supset _{w}:w\in \mu .\equiv .w\in \nu \colon\ldotp \\ [*171·11] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp \mu (P_{\text{df}})\nu \colon\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/6082.svg" style="vertical-align: -22.073ex; width: 86.773ex; height: 45.278ex;" id="img_images_6082.svg"></span></p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_473">[Pg 473]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="SECTION_D">SECTION D.<br>
<span class="allsmcap">ARITHMETIC OF RELATION-NUMBERS.</span></h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of Section D.</i></p>

<p>In the present section, we shall be concerned with the arithmetical
operations on relation-numbers. Their purely logical properties have
been dealt with in Section A; in the present section, it is their
arithmetical properties that are to be established. These properties
result immediately from the arithmetical properties of relations which
have been established in Sections B and C. The subjects treated of
in the present section are analogous to those treated of in Section
B of Part III. with the exception of such as have already had their
analogues discussed in Sections B and C of Part IV. The analogy is
sufficiently close to render it often unnecessary to give proofs, since
these are often step by step analogous to the proofs of corresponding
propositions in Part III, Section B.</p>

<p>The two chief requisites in defining the arithmetical operations with
relation-numbers are (1) to take due account of types, (2) to construct
what may be called <i>separated</i> relations, <i>i.e.</i> relations
of mutually exclusive relations derived from and ordinally similar
to given relations. Each of these points calls for some preliminary
explanations.</p>

<p>The sum of two relation-numbers <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_182">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_165"> will be denoted by
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{+} \nu\)" src="images/6092.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.543ex;" id="img_images_6092.svg">," in order to distinguish this kind of addition
from <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu + \nu\)" src="images/6093.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 5.329ex; height: 1.808ex;" id="img_images_6093.svg"> (the arithmetical addition of classes) and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu +_{c}\nu\)" src="images/4073.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.21ex; height: 1.808ex;" id="img_images_4073.svg_1"> (the addition of cardinals). In defining <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{+}\nu\)" src="images/6094.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.543ex;" id="img_images_6094.svg">,
we have to take account of the following considerations.</p>

<p>Suppose <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_270"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_186"> are two relations which are of the same type,
and have mutually exclusive fields. Then obviously we shall want
to frame our definition of the sum of two relation-numbers in such
a way that the sum of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/4146.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.64ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4146.svg_11"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/4487.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.731ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4487.svg_5"> shall be
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻ(P\unicode{x2909}Q)\)" src="images/6095.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.548ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6095.svg">. But if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_271"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_187"> are not of
the same type, <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x2909}Q\)" src="images/4740.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.846ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4740.svg_4"> is meaningless; and if <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_63">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_41"> overlap, <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x2909}Q\)" src="images/4740.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.846ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4740.svg_5"> may be too small to have
as its relation-number the sum of the relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_272"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_188">. Both these difficulties can be met by observing that, if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP=\text{Nr}ʻR\)" src="images/6096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.316ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6096.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻQ\text{Nr}ʻS\)" src="images/6097.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.131ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6097.svg">, we must
make such definitions as to have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ=\text{Nr}ʻR\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻS. \]" src="images/6098.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 29.596ex; height: 2.507ex;" id="img_images_6098.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_474">[Pg 474]</span>
Hence, in defining the sum of the relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_273"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_189">,
we may replace <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_274"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_190"> by any two relations <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_61"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_60">
which are respectively like <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_275"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_191">. Therefore what we require
for our definition is to find two relations <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_62"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_61"> which
(1) are respectively like <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_276"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_192">, (2) are of the same type,
(3) have mutually exclusive fields. All these three requisites are
satisfied if we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R=\downarrow (\Lambda\cap CʻQ)^{;}\iota ^{;}P.S=(\Lambda\cap CʻP)\downarrow ^{;}\iota ^{;}Q. \]" src="images/6099.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.318ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6099.svg"></span>
We then define <img alt="" data-tex="\(P+Q\)" src="images/6100.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.254ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6100.svg"> as meaning <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\unicode{x2909}S\)" src="images/6101.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.534ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6101.svg">, and we
define the sum of the relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_277"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_193"> as the
relation-number of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P+Q\)" src="images/6100.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.254ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6100.svg_1">. This procedure is exactly analogous to that
of <a href="#_110" class="pginternal">*110</a>; in fact, we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ Cʻ(P+Q)=CʻP+CʻQ. \]" src="images/6102.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.146ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6102.svg"></span></p>

<p>In defining the sum of the relation-numbers of a field, we do not have
to consider types, because the members of a field are necessarily
all of the same type. But we do have to consider the question of
overlapping. If a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_136"> occurs both in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_42"> and in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/389.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_389.svg_7">
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q,R\in CʻP\)" src="images/6103.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.055ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6103.svg">, we want a method of counting x twice over in
forming the arithmetical sum. Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻP\)" src="images/6104.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.631ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6104.svg"> cannot be
taken as the sum of the relation-numbers of members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_64">, unless
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P \in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}\)" src="images/6105.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.584ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_6105.svg">. Suppose, for instance, we have three
series
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (a, b, c),\quad ( b, c, a),\quad (c, a, b). \]" src="images/6106.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.924ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6106.svg"></span>
These each have three terms; and we want the sum of their
relation-numbers to be the relation-number of a series of nine terms.
But if we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} Q &amp;= a\downarrow b\downarrow c \qquad(\text{where}\, a\downarrow b\downarrow c\, \text{is written for}\, a\downarrow b\unicode{x228d} a\downarrow c\unicode{x228d} b\downarrow c),\\ R &amp;= b\downarrow c\downarrow a,\\ S &amp;= c\downarrow a\downarrow b,\\ \end{aligned} \]" src="images/6107.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.507ex; width: 63.196ex; height: 8.145ex;" id="img_images_6107.svg"></span>
and if we further put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P = Q\downarrow R\downarrow S, \]" src="images/6108.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 15.087ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_6108.svg"></span>
so that <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_278"> places the above three series in the above order, we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Sigma ʻP=(\iota ʻa\cup \iota ʻb\cup \iota ʻc)\uparrow (\iota ʻa\cup \iota ʻb\cup \iota ʻc), \]" src="images/6109.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.547ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6109.svg"></span>
which is not a series, and does not have the relation-number which we
require as the sum of the relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_194">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_63">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_62">.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_475">[Pg 475]</span></p>

<p>What is wanted is a method of distinguishing the various occurrences
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_3"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(b\)" src="images/5930.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.971ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_5930.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(c\)" src="images/6110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.98ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_6110.svg">. For this reason, when <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_4"> occurs as
a member of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_195">, we replace it by <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\downarrow Q\)" src="images/6111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.375ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6111.svg">;
when as a member of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_64">, by <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\downarrow R\)" src="images/6112.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.302ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6112.svg">; and
when as a member of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_63">, by <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\downarrow S\)" src="images/6113.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.044ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_6113.svg">. Thus
the series <img alt="" data-tex="\((a, b, c)\)" src="images/6114.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 6.919ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6114.svg"> is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\((a\downarrow Q, b\downarrow Q, c\downarrow Q)\)" src="images/6115.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.452ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6115.svg">;
<img alt="" data-tex="\((b, c, a)\)" src="images/6116.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 6.919ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6116.svg"> is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\((b\downarrow R, c\downarrow R, a\downarrow R)\)" src="images/6117.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.235ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6117.svg">;
and <img alt="" data-tex="\((c, a, b)\)" src="images/6118.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 6.919ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6118.svg"> is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\((c\downarrow S, a\downarrow S, b\downarrow S)\)" src="images/6119.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.462ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6119.svg">.
The sum of these three series then has the relation-number which is
required as the sum of the relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_196">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_65">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/26.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_26.svg_64">.</p>

<p>The above process is symbolized as follows. The generating relation
of the series <img alt="" data-tex="\((a\downarrow Q, b\downarrow Q, c\downarrow Q)\)" src="images/6115.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.452ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6115.svg_1"> is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.971ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6120.svg">; thus the three relations whose sum is to be
taken are <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.971ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6120.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow R^{;}R\)" src="images/6121.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.827ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6121.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow S^{;}S\)" src="images/6122.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.427ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_6122.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> using the notation of <a href="#_182" class="pginternal">*182</a>, according to which
we put <img alt="" data-tex="\(\unicode{x2640}ʻx=x\unicode{x2640}x\)" src="images/6123.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.972ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6123.svg">, our three relations
are <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ\)" src="images/6124.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.356ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6124.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻR\)" src="images/6125.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.283ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6125.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻS\)" src="images/6126.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.025ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6126.svg">. But the generating relation of the
series <img alt="" data-tex="\((\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ,\, \breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻR,\,\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻS)\)" src="images/6127.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 20.192ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6127.svg">
is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg">, since
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P=(Q\downarrow R\downarrow S)\)" src="images/6129.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.219ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6129.svg">. Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_1">
is the relation required for defining the sum of the relation-numbers
of members of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_279">; <i>i.e.</i> we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P   \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6130.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 26.443ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6130.svg"></span>
We will call <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_2"> the <i>separated</i>
relation corresponding to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_280">. <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_3"> is
constructed, as above, by replacing every member <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_137"> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_43">,
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\in CʻR\)" src="images/6131.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.35ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6131.svg">, by <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow Q\)" src="images/5450.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.472ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5450.svg_2">; so that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_138"> belongs both
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_44"> and to <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/389.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_389.svg_8">, it is duplicated by being transformed once
into <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow Q\)" src="images/5450.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.472ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5450.svg_3">, and once again into <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow R\)" src="images/5451.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.399ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_5451.svg_1">.</p>

<p>For the treatment of products, we do not require
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_4">, because <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/5446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.753ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5446.svg_24"> has been so defined
as to effect the requisite separation. We might, however, by the use
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_5">, have dispensed with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/5446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.753ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5446.svg_25"> as a
fundamental notion, and contented ourselves with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}ʻP\)" src="images/5445.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.873ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5445.svg_8">; for
we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi ʻP = \dot{s} ^{;}\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P. \]" src="images/6132.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 20.175ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6132.svg"></span>
Thus we might have taken <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}\)" src="images/2216.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.817ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_2216.svg_11"> as the fundamental notion, and
defined <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi\)" src="images/5673.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.697ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_5673.svg_6"> by means of it.</p>

<p>The addition of unity to a relation-number has to be treated
separately from the addition of two relation-numbers, for the same
reasons which necessitate the treatment of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x21f8} x\)" src="images/4869.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4869.svg_1"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\unicode{x21f7}P\)" src="images/4868.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4868.svg_1"> separately from <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x2909}Q\)" src="images/4740.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.846ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4740.svg_6">. There is no
ordinal number 1, but we can define the <i>addition</i> of one to a
relation-number. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP=\mu\)" src="images/5348.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 10.022ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_5348.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x{\sim}\in CʻP\)" src="images/5412.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.596ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5412.svg_1">, we must
have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Nr}ʻ(P\unicode{x21f8} x)=\mu \dot{+} \dot{1} , \]" src="images/6133.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.954ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6133.svg"></span>
where we write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_1">" for unity as an addendum. We do not
write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(1_r\)" src="images/6134.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.357ex; width: 2.041ex; height: 1.864ex;" id="img_images_6134.svg">," because we shall, at a later stage, give a general
definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu _r\)" src="images/6135.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.274ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_6135.svg">, in virtue of which, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_183"> is an
inductive cardinal, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu _r\)" src="images/6135.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.274ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_6135.svg_1"> will be the corresponding ordinal. This
definition entails <img alt="" data-tex="\(1_r=\Lambda\)" src="images/6136.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.357ex; width: 6.628ex; height: 1.977ex;" id="img_images_6136.svg">, and therefore we use a different
symbol "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_2">" for 1 as addendum. The symbol <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_3"> is only
defined in its uses, and has no significance except in a use which has
been specially defined.</p>

<p>We define the product <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{\times} \nu\)" src="images/6137.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.335ex;" id="img_images_6137.svg"> as the relation-number
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\times Q\)" src="images/5714.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.254ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5714.svg_1">, when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu =\text{N}_0\text{r}ʻP\)" src="images/6138.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 11.009ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_6138.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu=\text{N}_0\text{r}ʻQ\)" src="images/6139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.935ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6139.svg">. The product so defined obeys the
associative law, and obeys the distributive law in the form
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\nu \dot{+} \varpi )\dot{\times} \mu =(\nu \dot{\times} \mu )\dot{+} (\varpi \dot{\times} \mu ) \]" src="images/6140.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.336ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6140.svg"></span>
but not, in general, in the form
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu \dot{\times} (\nu \dot{+} \varpi )=(\mu \dot{\times} \nu )\dot{+} (\mu \dot{\times} \varpi ). \]" src="images/6141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.965ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6141.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_476">[Pg 476]</span>
The latter form holds when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_184">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_166">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\varpi\)" src="images/274.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.873ex; height: 0.998ex;" id="img_images_274.svg_4"> are finite
ordinals, as we shall prove at a later stage (*262). The commutative
law also does not hold in general for ordinal addition and
multiplication, but holds where finite ordinals are concerned.</p>

<p>The product of the numbers of the members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_65">, in the order
generated by <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_281">, is defined as being <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻ\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/6142.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.695ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6142.svg">, and
is denoted by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi \text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/6143.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.337ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6143.svg">. It will be seen that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi\text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/6144.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.337ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6144.svg"> is not a function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_66">, since the value of a
product depends upon the order of the factors; it is also not a
function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}^{;}P\)" src="images/6145.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 4.915ex; height: 1.616ex;" id="img_images_6145.svg">, unless no two members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_67"> have the
same relation-number. The properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi \text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/6143.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.337ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6143.svg_1"> result from
<a href="#_172" class="pginternal">*172</a> and <a href="#_174" class="pginternal">*174</a>.</p>

<p>"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_185"> to the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_167">th power" is denoted by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_r\nu\)" src="images/6146.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 8.063ex; height: 1.502ex;" id="img_images_6146.svg">"
and is defined as the relation-number of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P \,\text{exp}\,\, Q\)" src="images/5998.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 8.079ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5998.svg_2">, where
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu =\text{N}_0\text{r}ʻP\)" src="images/6138.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 11.009ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_6138.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu = \text{N}_0\text{r}ʻQ\)" src="images/6147.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.935ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6147.svg">. Its
properties result from the propositions of <a href="#_176" class="pginternal">*176</a> and <a href="#_177" class="pginternal">*177</a>.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_477">[Pg 477]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_180">
*180. THE SUM OF TWO RELATION-NUMBERS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *180.</p>

<p>In order to define the sum of two relation-numbers, we proceed (as
in <a href="#_110" class="pginternal">*110</a>) to construct a relation whose relation-number shall be the
required sum. For this purpose, we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P+Q=\{\downarrow (\Lambda\cap CʻQ)^{;}\iota ^{;}P\}\unicode{x2909}\{(\Lambda\cap CʻP)\downarrow ^{;}\iota ^{;}Q\}   \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6148.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 53.567ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6148.svg"></span>
This definition has the following merits: (1) whatever may be the
types of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_282"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_197">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow (\Lambda \cap CʻQ)^{;}\iota ^{;}P\)" src="images/6149.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.236ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6149.svg">
is of the same type as <img alt="" data-tex="\((\Lambda \cap CʻP)\downarrow ^{;}\iota ^{;}Q\)" src="images/6150.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.865ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6150.svg">;
(2) however the fields of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_283"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_198"> may overlap, and even if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P=Q\)" src="images/5209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.506ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5209.svg_2">, the fields of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow (\Lambda \cap CʻQ)^{;}\iota ^{;}P\)" src="images/6149.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.236ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6149.svg_1"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\((\Lambda \cap CʻP)\downarrow ^{;}\iota ^{;}Q\)" src="images/6150.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.865ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6150.svg_1"> are mutually exclusive;
(3) these two relations are respectively similar to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_284"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_199">.
Hence it is evident that, without placing any restriction upon <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_285"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_200">,
we may take the relation-number of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P+Q\)" src="images/6100.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.254ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6100.svg_2"> as defining the sum of the
relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_286"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_201">. Hence we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu \dot{+} \nu =\hat{R} \{(\exists P,Q).\mu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP.\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ.R\,\text{smor}\,(P+Q)\}   \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6151.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 64.389ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6151.svg"></span>
From this definition it follows that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{+} \nu\)" src="images/6092.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.543ex;" id="img_images_6092.svg_1"> is null unless
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_186"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_168"> are homogeneous relation-numbers, but that if they
are the homogeneous relation-numbers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_287"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_202">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{+} \nu\)" src="images/6152.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.543ex;" id="img_images_6152.svg"> is the relation-number of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P+Q\)" src="images/6100.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.254ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6100.svg_3">.</p>

<p>In order to be able to deal with typically ambiguous relation-numbers,
we put, as in <a href="#_110" class="pginternal">*110</a>,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \nu &amp;=\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP\dot{+} \nu   \quad\text{Df},\\ \mu \dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ&amp;=\mu \dot{+} \text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ  \quad\text{Df}. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/6153.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.394ex; width: 27.027ex; height: 5.919ex;" id="img_images_6153.svg"></span></p>

<p>The principal propositions of the present number are</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·111.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .Cʻ(P+Q)=CʻP+CʻQ\)" src="images/6154.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 28.905ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6154.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·3.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash .\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ&amp;=\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ=\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ\\ &amp;=\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP\dot{+} \text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ=\text{Nr}ʻ(P+Q)\end{align}\]" src="images/6155.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.394ex; width: 49.792ex; height: 5.919ex;" id="img_images_6155.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\,\text{smor}\,R.Q\text{smor}S.\supset .\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ=\text{Nr}ʻR\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻS\)" src="images/6156.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 53.394ex; height: 2.507ex;" id="img_images_6156.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition is essential, since otherwise <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+}\text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/6157.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.131ex; height: 2.507ex;" id="img_images_6157.svg">
would not be a function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/4146.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.64ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4146.svg_12"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/4487.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.731ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4487.svg_6">, but would depend upon the particular <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_288"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_203">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·32.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :CʻP\cap CʻQ=\Lambda .\supset .\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ=\text{Nr}ʻ(P\unicode{x2909}Q)\)" src="images/6158.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.852ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6158.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which is the associative law.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·61.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  . \text{Nr}ʻP \dot{+}  0_r = \text{Nr}ʻP = 0_r \dot{+}  \text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/6162.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 32.945ex; height: 2.507ex;" id="img_images_6162.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*180·71.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash  : \mu , \nu  \in  \text{NR} . \supset  . Cʻʻ(\mu  \dot{+}  \nu ) = Cʻʻ\mu  +_c Cʻʻ\nu \)" src="images/6163.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.723ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6163.svg"></p>
