It should be observed that, in virtue of <a href="#_154_9" class="pginternal">*154·9</a>, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Cʻʻ\mu\)" src="images/4469.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 5.799ex; height: 2.186ex;" id="img_images_4469.svg_1"> and

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_482">[Pg 482]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_181">
*181. ON THE ADDITION OF UNITY TO A RELATION-NUMBER.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *181.</p>

<p>The relation-number <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_5"> has, according to our definitions, no
meaning in isolation, because our definitions are framed with a view to
series, and a series cannot consist of one term. But we can <i>add</i>
one term to a series; hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_6"> is required as an addendum.
In order to get our definitions in the most manageable form, we first
construct a relation, which we call <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\dot{\unicode{x21f8}}x\)" src="images/6221.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.885ex;" id="img_images_6221.svg">, which
is such that, whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_289"> exists, <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\dot{\unicode{x21f8}}x\)" src="images/6221.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.885ex;" id="img_images_6221.svg_1"> has
one more term in its field than <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_290">; the relation-number of this
relation is then defined as <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \dot{1}\)" src="images/6222.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.532ex; height: 2.695ex;" id="img_images_6222.svg">. We add also
a definition
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} =2_r    \quad\text{Df} \]" src="images/6223.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.357ex; width: 13.763ex; height: 2.599ex;" id="img_images_6223.svg"></span>
which is purely formal, and serves to minimize exceptions to the
associative law of addition.</p>

<p>The definitions are closely analogous to those of <a href="#_180" class="pginternal">*180</a>. We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P\dot{\unicode{x21f8}}  x = \downarrow \Lambda _{x}^{;}{℩}^{;}P\unicode{x21f8} (\Lambda \cap CʻP)\downarrow {℩}ʻx    \quad\text{Df} \]" src="images/6224.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.576ex; width: 37.92ex; height: 3.009ex;" id="img_images_6224.svg"></span>
with a similar definition for <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\dot{\unicode{x21f7}} P\)" src="images/6225.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.885ex;" id="img_images_6225.svg">. <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_139"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_291"> may be of any relative types, and we have always
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \downarrow \Lambda _{x}^{;}{℩}^{;}P \,\,\text{smor}\, P.(\Lambda \cap CʻP)\downarrow {℩}ʻx{\sim}\in Cʻ\downarrow \Lambda _{x}^{;}{℩}^{;}P        \quad(*181·11·12). \]" src="images/6226.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.576ex; width: 67.096ex; height: 2.273ex;" id="img_images_6226.svg"></span>
We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu \dot{+} \dot{1}  = \hat{R} \{(\exists P,x).\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP = \mu .R \,\text{smor}\, (P\dot{\unicode{x21f8}}  x)\}    \quad\text{Df} \]" src="images/6227.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.352ex; height: 2.998ex;" id="img_images_6227.svg"></span>
with a similar definition for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1} \dot{+} \mu\)" src="images/6228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.256ex; height: 2.731ex;" id="img_images_6228.svg">. We also
introduce definitions analogous to <a href="#_180_03" class="pginternal">*180·03</a><a href="#_180_031" class="pginternal">·031</a>.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_486">[Pg 486]</span></p>

<p>The last line in the above proof, in which *24·1 is used, is legitimate
because <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_140"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_93"> may be of any type whatever, and therefore
the fact that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Lambda \neq \text{V}\)" src="images/640.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.486ex; width: 6.284ex; height: 2.106ex;" id="img_images_640.svg_2"> is sufficient to establish
<img alt="" data-tex="\((\exists x,y).x\neq y\)" src="images/697.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.853ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_697.svg_1"> in the sense wanted.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*181·561.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{+} \dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} =\mu \dot{+} (\dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} )  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6275.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 23.755ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6275.svg"></p>

<p>This definition adopts the opposite convention to that usually adopted.
But it is convenient to have <img alt="" data-tex="\(0_{r}\dot{+} \dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1}=2_{r}\)" src="images/6276.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.357ex; width: 12.881ex; height: 2.599ex;" id="img_images_6276.svg">,
and also to have as much similarity as possible between the
results of adding <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_9"> at the beginning and end of a relation.
Both reasons lead to the adoption of the above convention. (Cf.
*181·57·571, below.)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*181·57.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :\mu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .\dot{1} \dot{+} (\dot{1} \dot{+} \mu )=(\dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} )\dot{+} \mu =2_{r}\dot{+} \mu \\ &amp;[\text{Proof as in *181·56}]\end{align}\]" src="images/6277.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.309ex; width: 42.476ex; height: 5.749ex;" id="img_images_6277.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*181·571.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} \dot{+} \mu =(\dot{1} \dot{+} \dot{1} )\dot{+} \mu   \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6278.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 23.755ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6278.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*181·58.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \neq 0_{r}.\nu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .(\mu \dot{+} \dot{1} )\dot{+} \nu =\mu \dot{+} (\dot{1} \dot{+} \nu )   \quad[*161·232]\)" src="images/6279.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 54.137ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6279.svg"></p>

<p>The proof proceeds in the same way as that of <a href="#_181_54" class="pginternal">*181·54</a>.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*181·59.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \neq 0_{r}.\nu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .(\mu \dot{+} \dot{1} )\dot{+} (\dot{1} \dot{+} \nu )=\mu \dot{+} 2_{r}\dot{+} \nu    \quad[*161·25]\)" src="images/6280.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 56.807ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6280.svg"></p>

<p>The above propositions show that, except when one of the summands is
zero, the associative law holds for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_10"> just as if it were a
relation-number.</p>

<p>The following propositions are concerned with relations to cardinal
addition.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_487">[Pg 487]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_182">
*182 ON SEPARATED RELATIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *182.</p>

<p>In this number, we have to consider, as a preliminary to the
addition of the relation-numbers of a field, the properties of
the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_6">, which is defined
as follows. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\unicode{x2640}y\)" src="images/6286.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 3.76ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_6286.svg"> is any function of two
arguments in the sense of *38, we put <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\unicode{x2640}}ʻx= x\unicode{x2640}x\, \text{Df}\)" src="images/6287.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.77ex; height: 3.018ex;" id="img_images_6287.svg">.
Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ= Q\downarrow_{.,} Q\)" src="images/6288.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.417ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6288.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ= \downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6289.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 13.716ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6289.svg">.
Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_7"> is
the relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.971ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6120.svg_2"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow R^{;}R\)" src="images/6121.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.827ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6121.svg_1"> when
<img alt="" data-tex="\(QPR\)" src="images/6290.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.206ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6290.svg">. Thus the symbol <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_8"> is only
significant when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_292"> is a relation of relations; when this is the
case, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_9"> is the relation which results
when, for every <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_204"> which is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_68">, every member
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_141"> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_45"> is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow Q\)" src="images/5450.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.472ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_5450.svg_4">. The result is a
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}\)" src="images/4760.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 8.119ex; height: 2.068ex;" id="img_images_4760.svg_12">, whose arithmetical properties serve to
define the arithmetical properties of the sum of the relation-numbers
of members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_69"> the next number, we shall put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP = \text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6291.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 26.443ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6291.svg"></span>
We shall put later
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi \text{Nr}ʻP = \text{Nr}ʻ\Pi ʻP \]" src="images/6292.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 19.049ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6292.svg"></span>
and we shall find
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi ʻP = \dot{s} ^{;}\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P.\text{Nr}ʻ\Pi ʻP = \text{Nr}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P. \]" src="images/6293.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 46.916ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6293.svg"></span>
Thus we might have dispensed with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/5446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.753ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5446.svg_26"> as a fundamental notion,
using <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Prod}\)" src="images/2216.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.817ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_2216.svg_12"> instead, and putting
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Pi ʻP = \dot{s} ^{;}\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6294.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 24.858ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6294.svg"></span>
But this course is on the whole less convenient than that adopted in
<a href="#_172" class="pginternal">*172</a> and <a href="#_173" class="pginternal">*173</a>.</p>

<p>The notation <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\unicode{x2640}}\)" src="images/6295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 3.018ex;" id="img_images_6295.svg"> is thus required in
connection with ordinal addition, where it is almost indispensable.
It has besides certain minor uses. The object of the notation is to
enable us to exhibit as a function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_142"> an expression of the form
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\unicode{x2640}x\)" src="images/6296.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 3.946ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6296.svg">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\unicode{x2640}\)" src="images/2828.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2828.svg_3"> is any descriptive
double function which exists for all possible pairs of arguments. Thus
for example <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\downarrow x\)" src="images/1204.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.976ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1204.svg_7"> is a function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_143">, but the notations
hitherto introduced do not enable us to exhibit it in the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻx\)" src="images/2834.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.369ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2834.svg_1">.
Hence if we wish (say) to deal with the class
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \hat{P} \{(\exists x).x\in \alpha .P = x\downarrow x\} \]" src="images/6297.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.486ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6297.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_488">[Pg 488]</span>
we cannot write it in the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/4156.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.88ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4156.svg_2"> unless we introduce a new
notation. We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \breve{{\downarrow}}ʻx=x\downarrow x \]" src="images/6298.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.776ex; height: 2.891ex;" id="img_images_6298.svg"></span>
whence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\hat{P} \{(\exists x).x\in \alpha .P=x\downarrow x\}=\breve{{\downarrow}}ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6299.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.798ex; height: 3.005ex;" id="img_images_6299.svg">.
We introduce the notation generally for all descriptive double
functions which exist for all possible pairs of arguments.
Thus "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\unicode{x2640}\)" src="images/2828.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2828.svg_4">" in this number corresponds to
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\unicode{x2640}\)" src="images/2828.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2828.svg_5">" in *38.</p>

<p>In the present number, we shall begin by a few propositions
illustrating possible uses of the notation <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\unicode{x2640}}\)" src="images/6295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 3.018ex;" id="img_images_6295.svg_1">.
Thus for example if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_53"> is a class of relations, we have
hitherto had no simple notation for expressing the class of their
squares. But since <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{2}=\breve{\mid}ʻR\)" src="images/6300.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 9.426ex; height: 3.129ex;" id="img_images_6300.svg">, the class of the squares
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_54">'s is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\mid}ʻʻ\lambda\)" src="images/6301.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 4.663ex; height: 3.129ex;" id="img_images_6301.svg">. The notation is,
however, introduced chiefly in order to be applied to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow\)" src="images/34.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_34.svg_1">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow_{.,}\)" src="images/6302.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 2.22ex;" id="img_images_6302.svg">. We therefore proceed almost at once to
propositions on <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}\)" src="images/6303.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6303.svg">, and especially on
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_10">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·16·162.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}\in     1\rightarrow 1.\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\,\,\text{smor}\,\,P\)" src="images/6304.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 41.484ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6304.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ=\Pi ʻ(Q\downarrow Q)=\Pi ʻ\breve{{\downarrow}}ʻQ\)" src="images/6305.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 31.892ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6305.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\Pi ^{;}\breve{{\downarrow}}^{;}P\)" src="images/6306.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 15.105ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6306.svg"></p>

<p>We next prove (<a href="#_182_27" class="pginternal">*182·27</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}\)" src="images/5046.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.584ex; height: 2.109ex;" id="img_images_5046.svg_7">,
then <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_293"> has double likeness to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_11">,
the double correlator being <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\iota} \mid \text{D}\)" src="images/2809.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 4.415ex; height: 2.432ex;" id="img_images_2809.svg_2"> with its
converse domain limited to <img alt="" data-tex="\(Cʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6307.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 9.975ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6307.svg">
(<a href="#_182_26" class="pginternal">*182·26</a>). We then prove (<a href="#_182_33" class="pginternal">*182·33</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(T\upharpoonright Cʻ\Sigma ʻP\)" src="images/6308.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.56ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6308.svg">
is a double correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_294"> with <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_205">, then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(T\parallel \text{Cnv}ʻT\dagger\)" src="images/6309.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.022ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6309.svg"> (with its converse domain limited)
is a double correlator of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_12"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}Q\)" src="images/6310.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.998ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6310.svg">, whence we deduce</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\,\text{smor}\, \,\text{smor}\,Q.\supset .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\,\text{smor}\, \,\text{smor}\,\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}Q\)" src="images/6311.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 40.005ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6311.svg"></p>

<p>We next proceed to prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\Pi ʻP=\dot{s} ^{;}\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\dot{s} ^{;}\text{D}^{;}\Pi ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\Pi     ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{{\downarrow}}^{;}P\)" src="images/6312.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 48.493ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6312.svg"></p>

<p>The proof of this is as follows: In virtue of <a href="#_182_21" class="pginternal">*182·21</a> and the
associative law for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi\)" src="images/5673.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.697ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_5673.svg_7">, we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \dot{s}^{;}\text{D}^{;}\Pi ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\Pi ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{{\downarrow}}^{;}P. \]" src="images/6313.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 24.171ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6313.svg"></span>
<span class="pagenum" id="Page_489">[Pg 489]</span>
Now <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Sigma ʻ\breve{{\downarrow}}^{;}P=P\unicode{x228d} I\upharpoonright CʻP \)" src="images/6314.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.644ex; height: 2.891ex;" id="img_images_6314.svg">
(<a href="#_182_413" class="pginternal">*182·413</a>), and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi ʻ(P\unicode{x228d} I\upharpoonright CʻP)=\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/6315.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 23.758ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6315.svg"> (<a href="#_172_51" class="pginternal">*172·51</a>).</p>

<p>Hence our proposition results. Hence we arrive at</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·44.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Nr}ʻ\Pi ʻP=\text{Nr}ʻ\text{Prod}ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\text{Nr}ʻ\Pi ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6316.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 42.043ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6316.svg"></p>

<p>Finally we have some propositions showing how the notation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\unicode{x2640}}\)" src="images/6295.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 3.018ex;" id="img_images_6295.svg_2"> can be applied in cardinals.
It is then applied to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow_{,,}\)" src="images/6317.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 2.22ex;" id="img_images_6317.svg">, instead of, as
above, to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow_{.,}\)" src="images/6302.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 2.22ex;" id="img_images_6302.svg_1">. We have (<a href="#_182_5" class="pginternal">*182·5</a><a href="#_182_51" class="pginternal">·51</a><a href="#_182_52" class="pginternal">·52</a>)
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}\unicode{x21A7}\alpha =\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}ʻ\alpha .\in\unicode{x21A7}ʻʻ\kappa =\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}ʻʻ\kappa .\Sigmaʻ\kappa =sʻ\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}ʻʻ\kappa\)" src="images/6318.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 47.071ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6318.svg">.
Thus the notation of the present number might have been employed in
dealing with cardinal addition (<a href="#_112" class="pginternal">*112</a>) instead of the notation <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}\unicode{x21A7}\alpha\)" src="images/6319.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.314ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6319.svg">.
The general notation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x21A7}x\)" src="images/6320.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6320.svg"> was, however, required for
other purposes (cf. *85) and could not have been dispensed with.</p>

<p>In <a href="#_183" class="pginternal">*183</a> we shall put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P, \]" src="images/6321.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 21.76ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6321.svg"></span>
and by <a href="#_182_52" class="pginternal">*182·52</a> we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \Sigma \text{Nc}ʻ\kappa =\text{Nc}ʻsʻ\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}ʻʻ\kappa . \]" src="images/6322.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 23.345ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6322.svg"></span>
It will be seen that these formulae have the usual kind of analogy.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·021.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\unicode{x2640}}ʻx=x\unicode{x2640}x   \quad[*182·02.*30·3]\)" src="images/6325.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.096ex; height: 3.131ex;" id="img_images_6325.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·022.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{E}!\breve{\unicode{x2640}}ʻx   \quad[*182·021.*14·21]\)" src="images/6326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.566ex; height: 3.131ex;" id="img_images_6326.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·023.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\breve{\unicode{x2640}}\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}:(\alpha ).\alpha \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻ\breve{\unicode{x2640}}   \quad[*182·022.*71·166.*33·431]\)" src="images/6327.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 62.391ex; height: 3.131ex;" id="img_images_6327.svg"></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_55"> is a class of relations, the class of their squares
is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\mid}ʻʻ\lambda\)" src="images/6301.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 4.663ex; height: 3.129ex;" id="img_images_6301.svg_1">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·031.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\uparrow}ʻ\alpha =\alpha \uparrow \alpha    \quad[*182·021]\)" src="images/6329.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.7ex; height: 3.005ex;" id="img_images_6329.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·032.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{{\downarrow}}ʻx=x\downarrow x   \quad[*182·021]\)" src="images/6330.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.238ex; height: 3.005ex;" id="img_images_6330.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·033.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\dot{2} -2_{r}=\text{D}ʻ\breve{{\downarrow}}=1_{s}   \quad[*56·13.*182·032.*153·3]\)" src="images/6331.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 51.57ex; height: 3.005ex;" id="img_images_6331.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}ʻ\alpha =\downarrow \alpha ʻʻ\alpha    \quad[*182·021.*38·2]\)" src="images/6332.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 38.029ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6332.svg"></p>

<p>Observe that in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow_{,,}}\)" src="images/6333.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6333.svg">, we first take
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow_{,,}\)" src="images/6317.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 2.208ex; height: 2.22ex;" id="img_images_6317.svg_1">, and then put a circumflex over it. If we first
took <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{{\downarrow}}\)" src="images/6334.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.878ex;" id="img_images_6334.svg">, we could not then place two commas
under it, because <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{{\downarrow}}\)" src="images/6334.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.878ex;" id="img_images_6334.svg_1"> is a relation, not a double
descriptive function, and two commas can only significantly be placed
under a double descriptive function.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_490">[Pg 490]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·05.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ=\downarrow Q^{;}Q=Q\downarrow_{.,} Q   \quad[*182·021.*150·6]\)" src="images/6335.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 48.164ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6335.svg"></p>

<p>The relation for the sake of which the above notation is chiefly
introduced is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_13">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_295"> is a
relation of relations. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_296"> relates <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_206"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_66">, then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_14"> relates <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.971ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6120.svg_3"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow R^{;}R\)" src="images/6121.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.827ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6121.svg_2">. This is stated in the following proposition:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·1.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash .\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\hat{X} \hat{Y} \{(\exists Q,R).QPR.X=Q\downarrow_{.,} Q.Y=R\downarrow_{.,} R\}\\ &amp;[*182·023·05.*150·4]\end{align}\]" src="images/6336.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.559ex; width: 55.245ex; height: 6.249ex;" id="img_images_6336.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .Cʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻʻCʻP   \quad[*150·22]\)" src="images/6337.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 34.032ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6337.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·12.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .Cʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ=\downarrow QʻʻCʻQ=F\unicode{x21A7}Q   \quad[*182·05.*150·22.*33·5.(*85·5)]\)" src="images/6338.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 70.54ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6338.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .CʻʻCʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P=F\unicode{x21A7}ʻʻCʻP    \quad[*182·11·12]\)" src="images/6339.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 43.206ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6339.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*182·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .F\unicode{x21A7}\in 1\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/6340.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.988ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6340.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_496">[Pg 496]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_183">
*183. THE SUM OF THE RELATION-NUMBERS OF A FIELD.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *183.</p>

<p>In this number we have to define and consider the sum of the
relation-numbers of the members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_70">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_297"> is a relation
of relations. Since relational sums are not commutative, we cannot
define the sum of the relation-numbers of members of a class of
relations <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_56">: it is necessary that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\lambda\)" src="images/1407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.027ex; width: 1.319ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_1407.svg_57"> should be given
as the field of a relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_298">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_299"> determines the order in
which the summation is to be effected.</p>

<p>In order to avoid repetition, we replace <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_300"> by
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P\)" src="images/6128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 3.908ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6128.svg_15">, so that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_207"> is a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_71">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_208"> is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}ʻQ\)" src="images/6124.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.356ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6124.svg_1">,
<i>i.e.</i> by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow Q^{;}Q\)" src="images/6120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.971ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6120.svg_4">. This relation is like <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_209">, and
its field has no members in common with the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\downarrow R^{;}R\)" src="images/6121.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.827ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6121.svg_3">,
unless <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q=R\)" src="images/6398.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.524ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_6398.svg">. Hence we are led to the following definition:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻ\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P   \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 25.814ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6399.svg"></p>

<p>This definition is analogous to <a href="#_112_01" class="pginternal">*112·01</a>, as appears from <a href="#_182_52" class="pginternal">*182·52</a>, and
the propositions of the present number are analogous to some of the
propositions of <a href="#_112" class="pginternal">*112</a>.</p>

<p>We have not merely</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P \,\,\text{smor}\, \,\text{smor}\, Q.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/6400.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 39.033ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6400.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">but also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·15.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}P \,\,\text{smor}\, \,\text{smor}\, \breve{\downarrow}_{.,}^{;}Q.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/6401.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 43.45ex; height: 3.308ex;" id="img_images_6401.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which is a proposition with a weaker hypothesis than that of <a href="#_183_11" class="pginternal">*183·11</a>
(cf. note to <a href="#_182_34" class="pginternal">*182·34</a>).</p>

<p>Important propositions in this number are</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.\supset . \text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻP=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP\)" src="images/6402.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 37.918ex; height: 2.471ex;" id="img_images_6402.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=0_{r}.\equiv .\Sigma ʻP=\dot{\Lambda}\)" src="images/6403.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 28.021ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6403.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> a sum is only zero when there is no summand except (at
most) zero. (Cf. <a href="#_162_4" class="pginternal">*162·4</a><a href="#_162_45" class="pginternal">·45</a>.)</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_497">[Pg 497]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP\downarrow_{.,} ^{;}Q=\text{Nr}ʻ(Q\times P)\)" src="images/6404.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 29.89ex; height: 2.566ex;" id="img_images_6404.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183-26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :P\in \text{Nr}ʻR.CʻP\subset \text{Nr}ʻS.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP= \text{Nr}ʻ(R\times S)\)" src="images/6405.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 65.181ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6405.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition connects addition and multiplication.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\neq Q.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻ(P\downarrow Q)=\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻQ\)" src="images/6406.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 42.278ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6406.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition connects the two kinds of addition. We have also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·33.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\dot{\exists} !P.Z{\sim}\in CʻP.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻ(P\unicode{x21f8} Z)=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP\dot{+} \text{Nr}ʻZ\)" src="images/6407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 51.597ex; height: 2.871ex;" id="img_images_6407.svg"></p>

<p>The associative law of addition in a very general form is</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·43.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ^{;}\breve{\downarrow}_{.,}\dagger ^{;}P=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻ\Sigma ʻP\)" src="images/6408.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 46.669ex; height: 3.089ex;" id="img_images_6408.svg"></p>

<p>Finally the connection of ordinal and cardinal addition is given by</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*183·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :C\upharpoonright CʻP\in 1\rightarrow 1.\supset .Cʻʻ\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP=\Sigma \text{Nc}ʻCʻʻCʻP\)" src="images/6409.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 53.535ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6409.svg"></p>

<hr class="tb">

<h2 class="nobreak" id="id_184_THE_PRODUCT_OF_TWO_RELATION-NUMBERS">
*184. THE PRODUCT OF TWO RELATION-NUMBERS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *184.</p>

<p>The propositions of this number are for the most part analogous to
those of the propositions of <a href="#_113" class="pginternal">*113</a> which are concerned with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \times _{c} \nu\)" src="images/171.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 6.21ex; height: 1.6ex;" id="img_images_171.svg_2">.
Those of *113 which are concerned with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \times \beta\)" src="images/1849.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.494ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_1849.svg_4">
have their analogues in <a href="#_166" class="pginternal">*166</a>. We put</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{\times} \nu =\hat{R} \{(\exists P,Q).\mu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP.\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ.R\,\text{smor}\,(P\times Q)\} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6444.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 63.76ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6444.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Nr}ʻP\dot{\times} \nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP\dot{\times} \nu  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6445.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.887ex; height: 2.299ex;" id="img_images_6445.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{\times} \text{Nr}ʻQ=\mu \dot{\times} \text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 26.398ex; height: 2.335ex;" id="img_images_6446.svg"></p>

<p>We prove that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{\times} \nu\)" src="images/6137.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 4.324ex; height: 2.335ex;" id="img_images_6137.svg_1"> is only zero when one of its
factors is zero (<a href="#_184_16" class="pginternal">*184·16</a>); we prove the associative law (<a href="#_184_31" class="pginternal">*184·31</a>), and
the distributive law in the forms</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·33.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}.\supset .\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻP\dot{\times} \text{Nr}ʻR=\Sigma \text{Nr}ʻ(\times R)^{;}P\)" src="images/6447.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.849ex; height: 2.584ex;" id="img_images_6447.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·35.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .(\nu \dot{+} \varpi )\dot{\times} \mu =(\nu \dot{\times} \mu )\dot{+} (\varpi \dot{\times} \mu )\)" src="images/6448.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.724ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6448.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">and we prove <img alt="" data-tex="\(2_{r}\dot{\times} \mu =\mu \dot{+} \mu\)" src="images/6449.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 12.671ex; height: 2.543ex;" id="img_images_6449.svg"> (<a href="#_184_4" class="pginternal">*184·4</a>). Also
we extend the distributive law to the case where one of the summands is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\dot{1}\)" src="images/4748.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 2.242ex;" id="img_images_4748.svg_11">, <i>i.e.</i> we prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .(\nu \dot{+} \dot{1} )\dot{\times} \mu =(\nu \dot{\times} \mu )\dot{+} \mu\)" src="images/6450.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.869ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6450.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .(\dot{1} \dot{+} \nu) \dot{\times} \mu =\mu \dot{+} (\nu \dot{\times} \mu )\)" src="images/6451.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.869ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6451.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">and the connection of cardinal and ordinal multiplication is given by</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*184·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu ,\nu \in \text{NR}.\supset .Cʻʻ(\mu \dot{\times} \nu )=Cʻʻ\mu \times _{c}Cʻʻ\nu\)" src="images/6452.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.723ex; height: 2.412ex;" id="img_images_6452.svg"></p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*184·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \dot{\times} \nu =\hat{R} \{(\exists P,Q).\mu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP.\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ.R\,\text{smor}\,(P\times Q)\} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6444.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 63.76ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6444.svg_1"></p>

<p><i>Summary of</i> *185.</p>

<p>The subject of this number is analogous to part of the subject of <a href="#_114" class="pginternal">*114</a>.
The propositions concerned are immediate consequences of previously
proved properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\Pi ʻP\)" src="images/5446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.753ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_5446.svg_27">, and offer no difficulty of any kind.</p>

<h2 class="nobreak" id="id_186_POWERS_OF_RELATION-NUMBERS">
*186. POWERS OF RELATION-NUMBERS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *186.</p>

<p>For "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/139.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_139.svg_189"> to the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\nu\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.199ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_171">th power," where ordinal powers are
concerned, we use the notation "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu\)" src="images/6500.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 8.063ex; height: 1.502ex;" id="img_images_6500.svg">." We cannot
use "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu ^\nu\)" src="images/172.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 2.4ex; height: 2.017ex;" id="img_images_172.svg_16">" or "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,\nu\)" src="images/6501.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 7.154ex; height: 1.502ex;" id="img_images_6501.svg">" because these have
been already used for cardinals and classes (<a href="#_116" class="pginternal">*116</a>). We therefore put a
suffix <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/6502.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_6502.svg"> to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\,\text{exp}\,\)" src="images/6503.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.213ex; height: 1.452ex;" id="img_images_6503.svg">" to show that it is <i>relational</i>
powers that we are dealing with. We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu =\hat{R} \{(\exists P,Q).\mu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP.\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ.R\,\text{smor}\,(P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\} \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/6504.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 69.953ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6504.svg"></span></p>

<p>The following are the principal propositions of this number:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu \in \text{N}_{0}\text{R}.\supset .0_{r}\,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\mu =0_{r}.\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}0_{r}=0_{r}\)" src="images/6505.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 44.074ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_6505.svg"></p>

<p>We do not have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}0_{r}=1\)" src="images/6506.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 13.053ex; height: 1.995ex;" id="img_images_6506.svg">, because there is no
ordinal 1.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}2_{r}=\mu \dot{\times} \mu\)" src="images/6507.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 18.799ex; height: 2.335ex;" id="img_images_6507.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\alpha \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}(\beta \dot{+} \dot{1} )=(\alpha \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\beta )\dot{\times} \alpha\)" src="images/6508.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.482ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6508.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\alpha \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}(\dot{1} \dot{+} \beta )=\alpha \dot{\times} (\alpha \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\beta )\)" src="images/6509.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.482ex; height: 2.808ex;" id="img_images_6509.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\nu \neq 0_{r}.\varpi \neq 0_{r}.\supset .\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}(\nu \dot{+} \varpi )=(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu     )\dot{\times} (\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\varpi )\)" src="images/6510.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 59.161ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_6510.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·15.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\varpi \subset \text{Rl}ʻJ.\supset .\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}(\varpi \dot{\times} \nu )=(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu )\,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\varpi\)" src="images/6511.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 50.056ex; height: 2.412ex;" id="img_images_6511.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·31.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Mult ax}.\supset :\mu \nu \in \text{NR}-\iota ʻ\Lambda .P\in \text{Rel}^{2}\text{excl}\cap &amp;\mu .CʻP\subset \nu .\supset .\\ &amp;\Pi \text{Nr}ʻP=\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu\end{align}\]" src="images/6512.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.197ex; width: 63.853ex; height: 5.525ex;" id="img_images_6512.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">which connects exponentiation with multiplication.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·4.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{Nr}ʻP_{\text{df}}=2_{r}\,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}(\text{Nr}ʻP)\)" src="images/6513.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.307ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6513.svg"> (cf.*177)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*186·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\mu ,\nu \in \text{N}_{0}\text{R}.\nu \neq 0_{r}.\supset .Cʻʻ(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu )=(Cʻʻ\mu )^{Cʻʻ\nu }\)" src="images/6514.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 53.365ex; height: 2.587ex;" id="img_images_6514.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which connects ordinal and cardinal exponentiation.</p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*186·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu \,\text{exp}\,\,_{r}\nu =\hat{R} \{(\exists P,Q).\mu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻP.\nu =\text{N}_{0}\text{r}ʻQ.R\,\text{smor}\,(P\,\text{exp}\,\,Q)\} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6515.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 69.324ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6515.svg"></p>
