<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_577">[Pg 577]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_206">*206. SEQUENT POINTS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *206.</p>

<p>A "sequent" of a class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_316"> is a minimum of the terms that come
after the whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_3">; that is, we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻpʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP). \]" src="images/7220.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.794ex; height: 4.048ex;" id="img_images_7220.svg"></span>
Thus the sequents of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_317"> are its immediate successors. If
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_318"> has a maximum, the sequents are the immediate successors
of the maximum; but if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_319"> has no maximum, there will be no
one term of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_320"> which is immediately succeeded by a sequent
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_321">; in this case, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_322"> has a single sequent,
the sequent is the "upper limit" of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_323">. Whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_368"> is
connected, and therefore whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_369"> is serial, every class has one
sequent or none with respect to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_370">, by <a href="#_205_3" class="pginternal">*205·3</a>.</p>

<p>It will be seen that the sequents of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_324"> are the same
as the sequents of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_4">, and therefore that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{seq}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7221.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 7.285ex; height: 3.501ex;" id="img_images_7221.svg"> depends only upon <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\cap CʻP\)" src="images/7222.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7222.svg">:
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_325"> has terms not belonging to <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_97">, they are
irrelevant.</p>

<p>For the immediate predecessors of a class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_326">, we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overrightarrow{\text{prec}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻpʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP). \]" src="images/7223.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.36ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7223.svg"></span>
We have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{prec}_{P}=\text{seq}(\breve{P})\)" src="images/7224.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.11ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_7224.svg">, so that propositions
about <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{prec}_{P}\)" src="images/7225.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 5.543ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_7225.svg"> result from those about <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{seq}_{P}\)" src="images/7226.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 4.48ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_7226.svg"> by
merely writing <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_4"> in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_371">; they will therefore not
be given in what follows.</p>

<p>Among the elementary properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{seq}_{P}\)" src="images/7226.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 4.48ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_7226.svg_1"> with which this
number begins, the following are the most important:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻpʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7227.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.554ex; height: 4.048ex;" id="img_images_7227.svg"></p>

<p>This merely embodies the definition.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·131.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.027ex; height: 3.548ex;" id="img_images_7228.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·134.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha     =CʻP\cap \hat{x} \{\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset -pʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\}\)" src="images/7229.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 68.123ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7229.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_578">[Pg 578]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \cap CʻP=\Lambda .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/7230.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 34.814ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7230.svg"></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_372"> has a first term, this is the sequent of the null class,
or of any other class which has no members in common with <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_98">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·16.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha \in 0\cup 1\)" src="images/7231.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 32.556ex; height: 3.501ex;" id="img_images_7231.svg"></p>

<p>This follows at once from <a href="#_205_3" class="pginternal">*205·3</a>. It leads to</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·161.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .\supset .\text{seq}_{P}\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/7232.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 32.778ex; height: 2.114ex;" id="img_images_7232.svg"></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_373"> is a connected relation, no class has more than one
sequent. This is not in general the case with relations which are
not connected, even where the idea of sequents is quite naturally
applicable. Take, <i>e.g.</i>, the relation of descendent to ancestor,
and let <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_327"> be the class of monarchs of England. Then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7233.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 7.285ex; height: 3.501ex;" id="img_images_7233.svg"> will be such parents of
monarchs as were not themselves monarchs.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·171.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P&amp;\in \text{connex} .P^{2}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =CʻP\cap \hat{x} \{\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset (\alpha \cap CʻP)\cup Pʻʻ\alpha\}\end{align}\]" src="images/7234.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.934ex; width: 68.844ex; height: 7ex;" id="img_images_7234.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition states that <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_154"> is a sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_328"> if the
whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_5"> precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_155">, but every term that
precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_156"> either belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_329"> or precedes some term of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_330">. When <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_374"> is a series and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_331"> has no maximum, we
have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =CʻP\cap \hat{x} (\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha ) \quad(*206·174), \]" src="images/7235.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 48.082ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7235.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> the sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_332">, if any, is a term whose
predecessors are identical with the predecessors of members of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_333">. This is the case of a limit (cf. <a href="#_207" class="pginternal">*207</a>).</p>

<p>We have next a set of propositions (<a href="#_206_211" class="pginternal">*206·211</a><a href="#_206_28" class="pginternal">·28</a>) concerned
with <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7236.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 10.342ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7236.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7237.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 11.278ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7237.svg">. When <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_375"> is transitive
and connected, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_334"> is an existent class contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_99">
and having a sequent, we shall have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha =\alpha \cup Pʻʻ\alpha .{℩}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha \cup \overleftarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha =pʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ\alpha . \]" src="images/7238.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 60.923ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7238.svg"></span>
That is, the predecessors of the sequent are the members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_335">
and the predecessors of members, while the sequent and its successors
are the successors of the whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_336">. The various parts of
this statement require various parts of the hypothesis. Thus we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·211.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7239.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 37.964ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7239.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·213.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha \subset (\alpha \cap CʻP)\cup Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7240.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 60.423ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7240.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·22.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P\in \text{trans}\cap \text{connex} .&amp;\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha =(\alpha \cap CʻP)\cup Pʻʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha \cup Pʻʻ\alpha\end{align}\]" src="images/7241.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 74.179ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7241.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·23.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P\in \text{trans}\cap \text{connex} .&amp;\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\\ &amp;{℩}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha \cup \overleftarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha     =pʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\cap CʻP\end{align}\]" src="images/7242.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 74.592ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7242.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_579">[Pg 579]</span></p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_376"> is transitive, the value of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{seq}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7221.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 7.285ex; height: 3.501ex;" id="img_images_7221.svg_1">
is unchanged if we add to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_337"> any set of
terms contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6550.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.862ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6550.svg_10"> (<a href="#_206_24" class="pginternal">*206·24</a>); thus in particular,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ(\alpha \cup Pʻʻ\alpha ) =\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7243.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.724ex; height: 3.548ex;" id="img_images_7243.svg">
(<a href="#_206_25" class="pginternal">*206·25</a>). Thus we can fill up any gaps in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_338">, and take the
whole series up to the end of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_339">, without altering the sequent.</p>

<p>We have next a set of propositions (<a href="#_206_3" class="pginternal">*206·3</a>—<a href="#_206_38" class="pginternal">*206·38</a>) on the sequent of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6550.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.862ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6550.svg_11">, <i>i.e.</i> of the segment defined by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_340">. If
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_377"> is a series, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7244.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 11.699ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7244.svg"> is the maximum of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_341"> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_342"> has a maximum, the sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_343"> if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_344"> has a sequent but no maximum, and non-existent if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_345"> has
neither a maximum nor a sequent (<a href="#_206_35" class="pginternal">*206·35</a><a href="#_206_331" class="pginternal">·331</a><a href="#_206_36" class="pginternal">·36</a>).</p>

<p>Our next set of propositions (<a href="#_206_4" class="pginternal">*206·4</a>—<a href="#_206_52" class="pginternal">·52</a>) concerns the sequents of
unit classes, especially of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻ\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7245.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.563ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7245.svg">, and of
classes of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_2">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·4.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.x\in CʻP.\supset .x \text{seq}_{P}\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/7246.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 31.623ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7246.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :x\in CʻP.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\iota ʻx = \overleftarrow{P\dot{-} P^{2}}ʻx     = \overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/7247.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 51.301ex; height: 4.542ex;" id="img_images_7247.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">whence the three following propositions:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·43.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in  \text{trans} \cap  \text{Rl}ʻJ.x\in CʻP.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\iota ʻx = \overleftarrow{P}_{1}ʻx\)" src="images/7248.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 51.947ex; height: 3.709ex;" id="img_images_7248.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·45.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in  \text{Ser}.x\in CʻP.\supset :\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\iota ʻx. \equiv  .x\in \text{D}ʻP_{1}\)" src="images/7249.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 49.692ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7249.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·46.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in  \text{trans} \cap  \text{connex}  .\text{E}! \text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha      = \overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7250.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 61.415ex; height: 3.501ex;" id="img_images_7250.svg"></p>

<p>From the above propositions it results that, when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_378"> is a series,
any member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_100"> is the sequent of the class of its predecessors,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P} _{1}ʻx\)" src="images/7251.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.092ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_7251.svg"> is the sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\iota ʻx\)" src="images/407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 3.452ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_407.svg_8"> if either exists,
and the sequent of a class which has a maximum is the immediate
successor (if any) of the maximum, <i>i.e.</i></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in  \text{trans} \cap  \text{connex} .\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha     (P\dot{-} P^{2})\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7252.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 71.053ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_7252.svg"></p>

<p>We then have a set of propositions (<a href="#_206_53" class="pginternal">*206·53</a>—<a href="#_206_57" class="pginternal">·57</a>) on the sequent
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7253.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7253.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
the sequent of the predecessors of the whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_6">.
These propositions are specially useful in connection with
"Dedekindian" series, <i>i.e.</i> series in which every class
has either a maximum or a sequent (<a href="#_214" class="pginternal">*214</a>). These propositions all
require the full hypothesis that <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_379"> is a series. In this case,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻpʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP) = \overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.229ex; height: 4.048ex;" id="img_images_7254.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> the sequent (if any) of the predecessors of the whole of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_7"> is the minimum (if any) of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_346">. Moreover
by definition the maximum of <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7253.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7253.svg_1">,
if any, is the precedent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_347">. Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_348"> has
either a minimum or a precedent if <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha\cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7052.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7052.svg_1">
has either a sequent or a maximum (<a href="#_206_54" class="pginternal">*206·54</a>). Moreover the
sequent and maximum of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_349"> are respectively (if they exist)
the sequent and maximum of the predecessors of all the successors
of the whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_8"> (<a href="#_206_551" class="pginternal">*206·551</a>). Hence we arrive at
the conclusion that the assumption that every class of the form
<img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\)" src="images/7253.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.408ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7253.svg_2"> has either a maximum or
a sequent is equivalent both to the<span class="pagenum" id="Page_580">[Pg 580]</span> assumption that every class has
either a maximum or a sequent (<a href="#_206_56" class="pginternal">*206·56</a>) and to the assumption that
every class has either a minimum or a precedent (<a href="#_206_55" class="pginternal">*206·55</a>). It follows
that these two latter assumptions are equivalent (<a href="#_206_57" class="pginternal">*206·57</a>), <i>i.e.</i>
that a series is Dedekindian when, and only when, its converse is
Dedekindian (<a href="#_214_14" class="pginternal">*214·14</a>).</p>

<p>We deal next (<a href="#_206_6" class="pginternal">*206·6</a>—<a href="#_206_63" class="pginternal">*206·63</a>) with correlations, showing that if two
relations are correlated, the sequents of the correlates of any class are the
correlates of the sequents, <i>i.e.</i></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·61.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :S\in P\overline{\,\text{smor}\,}Q.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =Sʻʻ\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{Q}ʻ\breve{S} ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7255.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.829ex; width: 45.676ex; height: 3.811ex;" id="img_images_7255.svg"></p>

<p>We end with a set of propositions (<a href="#_206_7" class="pginternal">*206·7</a>—<a href="#_206_732" class="pginternal">·732</a>) showing that the
sequent of a class is unchanged if we remove from the class any
term other than its maximum (<a href="#_206_72" class="pginternal">*206·72</a>); that if a class has terms in
<img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_101">, and has both a precedent and a sequent, the precedent has the
relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{2}\)" src="images/2902.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 2.812ex; height: 1.887ex;" id="img_images_2902.svg_1"> to the sequent (<a href="#_206_73" class="pginternal">*206·73</a>), and that the precedent is
not identical with the sequent (<a href="#_206_732" class="pginternal">*206·732</a>). These propositions are in
the nature of lemmas, whose use is chiefly in the theory of stretches
(<a href="#_215" class="pginternal">*215</a>).</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_583">[Pg 583]</span></p>

<p>The propositions <a href="#_206_173" class="pginternal">*206·173</a><a href="#_206_174" class="pginternal">·174</a> deal with limits. When a class
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_350"> has no maximum, <i>i.e.</i> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\subset Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7289.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 17.618ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7289.svg">,
its sequent (if any) is called its <i>limit</i>. By the
above propositions, the limit is a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_157"> such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_10">
precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_158">, but every predecessor of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_159"> precedes some
member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_11"> (*206·173); it is also a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_160">
whose predecessors are identical with the predecessors of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_351">
(*206·174). The subject of limits will be explicitly treated in <a href="#_207" class="pginternal">*207</a>.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_206_3">*206·3</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P\in  \text{trans} \cap  \text{connex} .\alpha \subset CʻP.Pʻʻ\alpha \subset &amp;\alpha .\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha  = \alpha  \quad[*206·22]\end{align}\]" src="images/7311.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 67.77ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7311.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*206·31.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :P\in  \text{trans} \cap  \text{connex} .\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha      = Pʻʻ\alpha\\ &amp;[*206·3.*201·5]\end{align}\]" src="images/7312.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 64.428ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7312.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*206·31.*205·22.&amp;\supset \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :\overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha  = \overrightarrow{P}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha :\\ [*205·194.*206·133]&amp;\supset :{\sim}(\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha P \text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha ).{\sim}(\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha P \text{seq}_{P}ʻʻ\alpha ):\\ [*202·103]   &amp;\supset :\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha  = \text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha \colon\ldotp \supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7314.svg" style="vertical-align: -4.48ex; width: 77.133ex; height: 10.09ex;" id="img_images_7314.svg"></span></p>

<p>In the hypothesis of <a href="#_206_32" class="pginternal">*206·32</a>, we have both
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7315.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.575ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7315.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7316.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 13.869ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7316.svg">. So long as <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_380"> is not
contained in diversity, these are both necessary. For example, suppose
we take
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P = \alpha \uparrow (\alpha \cup \iota ʻx),\,\text{where}\, x{\sim}\in \alpha .\exists !\alpha . \]" src="images/7317.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.515ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7317.svg"></span>
Then <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_381"> is transitive and connected, but not contained in diversity.
We have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \alpha \cup \iota ʻx = CʻP.Pʻʻ(\alpha \cup \iota ʻx) = \alpha  = \text{D}ʻP. \]" src="images/7318.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 42.7ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7318.svg"></span>
Also
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} \text{max}_{P}ʻ(\alpha \cup \iota ʻx) &amp;= x\,\\ \overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻPʻʻ(\alpha \cup \iota ʻx) &amp;= \overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻpʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ\alpha  = \overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ(\alpha     \cup \iota ʻx) = \Lambda . \end{aligned} \]" src="images/7319.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.929ex; width: 62.183ex; height: 6.989ex;" id="img_images_7319.svg"></span>
Thus in this case <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}ʻ(\alpha \cup \iota ʻx)\)" src="images/7320.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.132ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7320.svg">
exists, but <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ(\alpha \cup \iota ʻx)\)" src="images/7321.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.426ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7321.svg"> does not
exist. When <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_382"> is serial, <i>i.e.</i> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_383"> is contained
in diversity, in addition to being transitive and connected,
the existence of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7322.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.405ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7322.svg"> involves that of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7244.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 11.699ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7244.svg_1">, and therefore the hypothesis
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7316.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 13.869ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7316.svg_1">, which appears in <a href="#_206_32" class="pginternal">*206·32</a>,
becomes unnecessary.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*206·35·331.&amp;\supset \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Hp}:\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\lor.\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha :\supset .\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha       &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .*206·34.    \supset \vdash \colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.&amp;\supset :\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻPʻʻ\alpha .\supset .{\sim}\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .  &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [*206·33]  &amp;\supset .{\sim}\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .(1).(2).(3).&amp;\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7331.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 84.186ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_7331.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_587">[Pg 587]</span></p>

<p>The condition <img alt="" data-tex="\((\alpha ):\text{E}!\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha.\lor.\text{E}!\text{seq}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7332.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 28.645ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7332.svg">
is the definition of what may be called "Dedekindian" series,
<i>i.e.</i> series in which, when any division of the field into two
parts is made in such a way that the first part wholly precedes the
second, then either the first part has a last term or the second part
has a first term. (When these alternatives are also mutually exclusive,
the series has "Dedekindian continuity.") If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_352"> is any class,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6550.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.862ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6550.svg_12"> is the segment of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_104"> defined by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_353">. In
virtue of the above proposition, every segment of a Dedekindian series
has a sequent. The sequent of a class having no maximum is what is
commonly called a <i>limit</i>. Thus in a series having Dedekindian
continuity (in which segments never have maxima), every segment has a
limit.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_206_57">*206·57</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}.\supset :&amp;(\alpha ).\alpha \in \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{min}_{P}\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{prec}_{P}. \equiv  .\\ &amp;(\alpha ).\alpha \in \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{max}_{P}\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}         \quad[*206·55·56]\end{align}\]" src="images/7371.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 56.695ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_7371.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition is important, since it shows that when a serial
relation satisfies Dedekind's axiom, so does its converse. Thus if all
classes which have no maximum have an upper limit, then all classes
which have no minimum have a lower limit, and vice versa.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_594">[Pg 594]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_207">*207. LIMITS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *207.</p>

<p>A term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_161"> is said to be the "upper limit" of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_354"> in <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_384">
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_355"> has no maximum and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_162"> is the sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_356">.
In this case, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_163"> immediately follows the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_357">, though
there is no one member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_358"> which <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_164"> immediately follows.
Sequents which are limits have special importance, and it is convenient
to have a special notation for them. We write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{lt}_Pʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7393.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.704ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7393.svg">"
for the upper limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_359">; or, if it is more convenient,
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{lt}(P)ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7394.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.774ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7394.svg">". (This is more convenient when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_385"> is
replaced by an expression consisting of several letters, or by a letter
with a suffix.) The <i>lower</i> limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_360"> will be the
immediate predecessor of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_361"> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_362"> has no minimum;
this we denote by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{tl}_Pʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7395.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.704ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7395.svg">.</p>

<p>The following propositions on limits for the most part follow
immediately from the propositions of <a href="#_206" class="pginternal">*206</a> on sequents.</p>

<p>Our definition is so framed that the limit of the null-class is
the first member of our series (if any). This departure from
usage is convenient in order that, whenever our series contains
any limiting point in the ordinary sense, the <i>series</i>
of limiting points may exist, <i>i.e.</i> in order that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x0294f}\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P\)" src="images/7396.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.041ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7396.svg"> may exist whenever there
are existent parts of CʻP which have upper limits. The series
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\unicode{x0294f}\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P\)" src="images/7396.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.041ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7396.svg_1"> is the "first derivative" of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_386">. The definition of a limit is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{lt}_P=\text{seq}_{P}\upharpoonright (-\text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{max}_{P})   \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/7397.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.743ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7397.svg"></span></p>

<p>Besides the limit, we require, for many purposes, a single notation for
the "limit or maximum." This we denote by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}_P\)" src="images/7398.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 6.858ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_7398.svg">," putting
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{limax}_P=\text{max}_{P}\unicode{x228d} \text{lt}_P   \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/7399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.042ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7399.svg"></span>
Similarly for the lower limit or minimum we use "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}_{P}\)" src="images/7400.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 6.419ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_7400.svg">,"
putting
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{limin}_{P}=\text{min}_{P}\unicode{x228d} \text{tl}_P   \qquad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/7401.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 26.427ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7401.svg"></span>
We have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{tl}_P=\text{lt}(\breve{P})\)" src="images/7402.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.884ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_7402.svg"> (<a href="#_207_101" class="pginternal">*207·101</a>) and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}_{P}=\text{limax}(\breve{P})\)" src="images/7403.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.363ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_7403.svg"> (<a href="#_207_401" class="pginternal">*207·401</a>). Hence it is
unnecessary to prove propositions concerning lower limits, since they
result immediately from propositions concerning upper limits.</p>

<p>In virtue of our definition of a limit, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_165"> limits <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_363">
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_166"> is a sequent of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_364"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_365"> has no maximum
(<a href="#_207_1" class="pginternal">*207·1</a>). Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_366"> has a maximum, it has no limit (<a href="#_207_11" class="pginternal">*207·11</a>),
but if it has no maximum, the class of its limits is the class of
its sequents (<a href="#_207_12" class="pginternal">*207·12</a>). Thus the existence of the class of limits is
equivalent<span class="pagenum" id="Page_595">[Pg 595]</span> to the existence of the class of sequents combined with the
non-existence of the class of maxima, <i>i.e.</i></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha .\equiv .{\sim}\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha     .\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7404.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 36.233ex; height: 3.734ex;" id="img_images_7404.svg"></p>

<p><a href="#_207_2" class="pginternal">*207·2</a>—<a href="#_207_232" class="pginternal">·232</a> consist of various formulae for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{lt}}_Pʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7405.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.704ex; height: 3.667ex;" id="img_images_7405.svg">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .x\,\text{lt}_P\,\alpha .\supset .\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7406.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 55.472ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7406.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the whole of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_12"> precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_167">, but any
predecessor of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_168"> precedes some member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_367">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·231.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Ser}.\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha     =CʻP\cap \hat{x} (\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha )\)" src="images/7407.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 54.918ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7407.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_368">, if it exists, is the term whose
predecessors are identical with the predecessors of some part of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_369">.</p>

<p>We have also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·232.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}.\supset :x=\text{lt}_Pʻ\alpha .\equiv .x\in CʻP-\alpha .\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7408.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 56.105ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7408.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition should be compared with <a href="#_205_54" class="pginternal">*205·54</a>, which (slightly
re-written) is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}.\supset :x=\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\equiv .x\in CʻP\cap \alpha .\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha \]" src="images/7409.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 58.555ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7409.svg"></span></p>

<p>From the two together we arrive at</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·51.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}.\supset :x=\text{limax}_Pʻ\alpha .\equiv .x\in CʻP.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7410.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 55.851ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7410.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which serves to illustrate the utility of "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}_P\)" src="images/7398.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 6.858ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_7398.svg_1">."</p>

<p>We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha \in 0\cup 1.\text{lt}_P\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/7411.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 45.072ex; height: 3.667ex;" id="img_images_7411.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_387"> is connected, a class cannot have more than one
limit; also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{trans}.\beta \subset Pʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ(\alpha \cup \beta )=\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7412.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 47.07ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7412.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> any terms which have some <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_370">'s beyond them may be
added to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_371"> without altering the limit.</p>

<p>We next have a set of propositions (<a href="#_207_251" class="pginternal">*207·251</a>—<a href="#_207_27" class="pginternal">·27</a>) proving that if a
class has a limit, any single term of the class may be removed without
altering the limit (<a href="#_207_261" class="pginternal">*207·261</a>), and that in any case, provided the
class is not a unit class, its minimum (if any) may be removed without
altering the limit (<a href="#_207_27" class="pginternal">*207·27</a>). We then prove (<a href="#_207_291" class="pginternal">*207·291</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_388"> is
a series, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_372"> is a class which has a limit, the predecessors of
the limit are the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{*}ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7413.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.603ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7413.svg">.</p>

<p>We then have a set of propositions (<a href="#_207_3" class="pginternal">*207·3</a>—<a href="#_207_36" class="pginternal">·36</a>) on the limit of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_3"> and kindred matters. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_169"> has no immediate
predecessor, the limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_4"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_170">, and vice
versa (<a href="#_207_32" class="pginternal">*207·32</a><a href="#_207_33" class="pginternal">·33</a>). Hence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·35.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Rl}ʻJ\cap \text{connex} .\supset .\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P=CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻ(P\dot{-} P^{2})\)" src="images/7414.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 52.616ex; height: 2.62ex;" id="img_images_7414.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the limit-points of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_389"> are those which have no immediate
predecessors.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_596">[Pg 596]</span></p>

<p>We next turn our attention to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}_P\)" src="images/7398.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 6.858ex; height: 1.91ex;" id="img_images_7398.svg_2">." This again is
one-many, provided <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_390"> is connected (<a href="#_207_41" class="pginternal">*207·41</a>). We have by the
definition</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7415.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 37.789ex; height: 3.991ex;" id="img_images_7415.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·43.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha     =\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7416.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 48.09ex; height: 4.057ex;" id="img_images_7416.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·44.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{limax}_P=\text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{max}_{P}\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{lt}_P=\text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{max}_{P}\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{seq}_{P}\)" src="images/7417.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.519ex; width: 52.461ex; height: 2.216ex;" id="img_images_7417.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·45.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha \cup \overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7418.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 31.692ex; height: 3.991ex;" id="img_images_7418.svg"></p>

<p>Also we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·46.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp x=\text{limax}_Pʻ\alpha .\equiv :x=\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\lor.x=\text{lt}_Pʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7419.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 47.645ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7419.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">which is a very useful proposition, as is also <a href="#_207_51" class="pginternal">*207·51</a> (given above).</p>

<p>A useful proposition in dealing with classes of classes contained in a
series is</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·54.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Ser}.\kappa \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻ\text{lt}_P.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ\text{lt}_Pʻʻ\kappa =\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻsʻ\kappa     =\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻsʻ\kappa\)" src="images/7420.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 66.046ex; height: 3.991ex;" id="img_images_7420.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> if every member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\kappa\)" src="images/49.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.303ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_49.svg_122"> has a limit, the limit or
maximum (if any) of the limits is the limit or maximum, and in fact the
limit, of <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\kappa\)" src="images/1358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 3.722ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_1358.svg_12">.</p>

<p>We have next a set of propositions (<a href="#_207_6" class="pginternal">*207·6</a>—<a href="#_207_66" class="pginternal">·66</a>) on correlations,
proving that the limit, or the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}\)" src="images/7421.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.468ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_7421.svg">, of the correlates is
the correlate of the limit or <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}\)" src="images/7421.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.468ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_7421.svg_1">, <i>i.e.</i></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·6.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :S\in P\,\overline{\,\text{smor}\,}\,Q.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =Sʻʻ\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{Q}ʻ\breve{S} ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7422.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 43.268ex; height: 3.865ex;" id="img_images_7422.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·64.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :S\in P\,\overline{\,\text{smor}\,}\,Q.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =Sʻʻ\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{Q}ʻ\breve{S} ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/7423.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 51.187ex; height: 4.188ex;" id="img_images_7423.svg"></p>

<p>The last three propositions (<a href="#_207_7" class="pginternal">*207·7</a>—<a href="#_207_72" class="pginternal">·72</a>) are lemmas for use in the
theory of stretches (<a href="#_215_5" class="pginternal">*215·5</a><a href="#_215_51" class="pginternal">·51</a>).</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}_P=\text{min}_{P}\unicode{x228d} \text{tl}_P  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/7427.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 23.535ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7427.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_207_1">*207·1</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :x\,\text{lt}_P\,\alpha .\equiv .x\text{seq}_{P}\alpha .{\sim}\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha  \quad[(*207·01)]\)" src="images/7428.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 46.79ex; height: 3.548ex;" id="img_images_7428.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_207_101">*207·101</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\text{tl}_P=\text{lt}(\breve{P} ) \quad[*205·102.*206·101.(*207·02)]\)" src="images/7429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 48.344ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_7429.svg"></p>

<p>We shall not give further propositions on lower limits, unless for some
special reason, since all of them result from propositions on upper
limits by means of <a href="#_207_101" class="pginternal">*207·101</a>.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_207_11">*207·11</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda    \quad[*207·1]\)" src="images/7430.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.806ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7430.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_597">[Pg 597]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_207_12">*207·12</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha       \quad[*207·1]\)" src="images/7431.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 46.221ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7431.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·121.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\alpha \cap CʻP\subset Pʻʻ\alpha .\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha  \quad[*207·12.*205·123]\)" src="images/7432.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 63.165ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7432.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha .\equiv .{\sim}\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha     .\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha   \quad[*207·1]\)" src="images/7433.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 47.044ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7433.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·14.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp \exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\lor.\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{seq}} _{P}ʻ\alpha     :\equiv :\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\lor.\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha \\ &amp;[*207·13.*5·63]\end{align}\]" src="images/7434.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.795ex; width: 52.687ex; height: 6.722ex;" id="img_images_7434.svg"></span></p>

<p>The above proposition is important because
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\alpha ):\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha .\lor.\exists !\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha \]" src="images/7435.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.498ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7435.svg"></span>
is the characteristic of "Dedekindian" series, <i>i.e.</i> of such as
fulfil Dedekind's axiom.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·15.</b>
    <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :x\,\text{lt}_P\,\alpha .\equiv .x\in CʻP.\alpha \cap CʻP\subset Pʻʻ\alpha \cap \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset -pʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)\\ &amp;[*207·1.*205·123.*206·134]\end{align}\]" src="images/7436.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 76.241ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7436.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·17.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\Lambda =\overrightarrow{B}ʻP    \quad[*207·12.*205·161.*206·14]\)" src="images/7438.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 49.191ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7438.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*207·17.\supset \vdash :\text{ᗡ}ʻP\subset \text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P.&amp;\equiv .\text{ᗡ}ʻP\cup \overrightarrow{B}ʻP\subset \text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P.\\ [*93·103]  &amp;\equiv .CʻP\subset \text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P.\\ [*207·15]  &amp;\equiv .CʻP=\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P:\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7440.svg" style="vertical-align: -4.48ex; width: 59.541ex; height: 10.09ex;" id="img_images_7440.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_207_2">*207·2</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .x\,\text{lt}_P\,\alpha .\supset .\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset Pʻʻ\alpha \\ &amp;[*207·15.*202·503]\end{align}\]" src="images/7441.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.783ex; width: 56.1ex; height: 6.697ex;" id="img_images_7441.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*200·53.&amp;\supset \vdash :P^{2}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .Pʻʻ\alpha \subset -pʻ\overleftarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP)  &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).    \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.&amp;\supset .x\in CʻP.\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset -pʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻP).\\ [*206·134]  &amp; \supset .x\text{seq}_{P}\alpha  &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .*22·44. \supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.&amp;\supset .\alpha \cap CʻP\subset Pʻʻ\alpha .\\ [*205·123]  &amp;\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .(2).(3).*207·1.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7443.svg" style="vertical-align: -10.62ex; width: 96.524ex; height: 22.371ex;" id="img_images_7443.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·22.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :P\in \text{connex} .P^{2}\,\unicode{x2abd}\, J.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha     =CʻP\cap \hat{x} (\alpha \cap CʻP\subset \overrightarrow{P}ʻx.\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\subset Pʻʻ\alpha )\\ &amp;[*207·2·21]\end{align}\]" src="images/7444.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.795ex; width: 75.128ex; height: 6.722ex;" id="img_images_7444.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_598">[Pg 598]</span></p>

<p>This is very often the most convenient form for
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}\alpha\)" src="images/7445.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 4.346ex; height: 3.554ex;" id="img_images_7445.svg">. It states that a limit of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_373"> is a member <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_171"> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_105"> such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻP\)" src="images/6836.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.739ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6836.svg_13">
wholly precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_172">, but every predecessor of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_173"> precedes some
member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_374">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*207·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P\in \text{Ser}.\supset .\overrightarrow{\text{lt}} _{P}ʻ\alpha =CʻP\cap \hat{x} (\overrightarrow{P}ʻx=Pʻʻ\alpha .\alpha \cap CʻP\subset Pʻʻ\alpha )\)" src="images/7446.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 64.946ex; height: 3.781ex;" id="img_images_7446.svg"></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*207·32.&amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻ(P\dot{-} P^{2})=\text{lt}_Pʻʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ\{CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻ(P\dot{-} P^{2})\} &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*207·35.&amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P=\text{lt}_Pʻʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ\{CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻ(P\dot{-} P^{2})\} &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash .*207·33. &amp;\supset \vdash .\text{lt}_Pʻʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻ\{CʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻ(P\dot{-} P^{2})\}=\Lambda &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash .(2).(3). &amp;\supset \vdash :\text{Hp}.\supset .\text{D}ʻ\text{lt}_P=\text{lt}_Pʻʻ\overrightarrow{P}ʻʻCʻP  &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \vdash .(2).(4).\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7478.svg" style="vertical-align: -9.887ex; width: 94.1ex; height: 20.905ex;" id="img_images_7478.svg"></span></p>

<p>In virtue of this proposition, all limits are limits of classes
of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_5">. In this respect, limits (in
general) differ from segments. If we call <img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6550.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.862ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6550.svg_13"> the segment
defined by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_375">, there will in general be segments not of the
form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_6">. These, however, will be the segments
which have no sequents, and therefore no limits; thus their existence
does not introduce limits not derivable from classes of the form
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{P}ʻx\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.351ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg_7">.</p>
