<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_737">[Pg 737]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_232">
*232. ON THE OSCILLATION OF A FUNCTION AS THE ARGUMENT
APPROACHES A GIVEN LIMIT.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *232.</p>

<p>In the preceding number, we considered the ultimate oscillation
of a function when the argument grows without limit. If, in the
propositions of the last number, we confine the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_260"> to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg">, where <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\in \text{ᗡ}ʻQ\)" src="images/8884.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.565ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8884.svg">, the ultimate
oscillation becomes the ultimate oscillation as the argument
approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_224"> from below. If the ultimate oscillation consists
of a single term, this is the limit of the function as the argument
approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_225"> from below. If, instead of confining the argument
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg_1">, we confine it to any other class whose
limit is <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_226">, we shall, under a very usual hypothesis, obtain
the same value for the ultimate oscillation as if we confined it
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg_2">. And more generally, under a similar
hypothesis, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_464"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_202"> are two classes of arguments
which define the same section (<i>i.e.</i> such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ\alpha=Q_{*}ʻʻ\beta\)" src="images/8885.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 16.73ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8885.svg">),
then, whether or not this section has a limit, the ultimate sections
and the ultimate oscillation are the same for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_465"> as they
are for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_203">. Hence we are led to consider first the result
of confining the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_261">, not to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg_3">,
but to any class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_466">. In order not to have to exclude
explicitly the case in which <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \in 1\)" src="images/7027.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.345ex; height: 1.597ex;" id="img_images_7027.svg_2">, we deal with
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha\)" src="images/8677.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.583ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8677.svg_1">, not <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\unicode{x0294f}\alpha\)" src="images/8676.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.595ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8676.svg_1">. Hence
we are led to the following definitions:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha )   \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/8886.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.288ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8886.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha =P\overline{R} _{os}(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha )   \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/8887.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.563ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8887.svg"></p>

<p>Most of the propositions of the present number are immediate
consequences of corresponding propositions in <a href="#_231" class="pginternal">*231</a>. The most important
application of the propositions of the present number is to the case
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_467"> is of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg_4">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_227"> being
a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\delta _{Q}ʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/8888.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 8.247ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_8888.svg">. We may, in this case, take
in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻx\)" src="images/8883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.441ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8883.svg_5"> any other class of arguments
(<i>e.g.</i> a progression of arguments <img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{1}\)" src="images/1380.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.282ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_1380.svg_5">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{2}\)" src="images/1381.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.282ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_1381.svg_6">, ...
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{\nu }\)" src="images/8628.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.33ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_8628.svg_6">, ...) having <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_228"> for its limit, without altering the
limiting sections or the ultimate oscillation. Hence the limit of the
function for a given argument (if it exists) may be determined by
choosing any selection of arguments having the given argument as their
limit (cf. <a href="#_233_142" class="pginternal">*233·142</a>, below).</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_738">[Pg 738]</span></p>

<p>From the definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8889.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8889.svg"> we
obtain immediately</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·11.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp x\in (P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ&amp;\alpha .\equiv :\\ &amp;y\in \alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR.\supset _{y}.x\in P_{*}ʻʻRʻʻ(\alpha \cap \overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻy):x\in CʻP\end{align}\]" src="images/8890.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.14ex; width: 77.697ex; height: 7.412ex;" id="img_images_8890.svg"></span></p>

<p>We prove that <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha = (P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8891.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 41.705ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8891.svg">
(<a href="#_232_131" class="pginternal">*232·131</a>), and that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR=\Lambda\)" src="images/8892.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.363ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8892.svg">, the
two limiting sections and the ultimate oscillation are all equal to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_137"> (<a href="#_232_15" class="pginternal">*232·15</a>). Also we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :Q\in \text{trans}\cap \text{connex}  .\alpha \cap CʻQ{\sim}\in 1.\supset .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}(Q\unicode{x0294f}\alpha     )\)" src="images/8893.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 66.741ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8893.svg"></p>

<p>Thus the substitution of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\)" src="images/8894.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.777ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_8894.svg"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_262"> in our definitions has
the effect of making them applicable to unit classes, and of enabling
us to substitute the hypothesis <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\in \text{connex}\)" src="images/8895.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.394ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_8895.svg"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\in\text{trans}\cap \text{connex}\)" src="images/8896.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 18.968ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_8896.svg">.
But when <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_263"> is transitive and connected (and therefore when <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_264"> is
a series), the substitution of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\)" src="images/8894.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.777ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_8894.svg_1"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_265"> in the definitions
makes no difference unless <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_468"> is a unit class. This case is
trivial, since the only interest of our definitions is when a has no
maximum in <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_266">.</p>

<p>From <a href="#_231_22" class="pginternal">*231·22</a> we obtain</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·22.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P_{*},Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha \in \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ)&amp;\subset CʻP.\supset .\\ CʻP=(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \cup (\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \end{align}\]" src="images/8897.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.395ex; width: 48.501ex; height: 5.921ex;" id="img_images_8897.svg"></span></p>

<p>We have next a set of propositions concerned in discovering
circumstances under which two classes <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_469"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\beta\)" src="images/36.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.281ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_36.svg_204"> which
determine the same section in <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_267"> (and therefore have the same limit,
if any) give the same values for the two limiting sections. For this
purpose, it is only necessary to discover circumstances under which
we may substitute <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8682.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.647ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8682.svg_1"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_470">.
When this can be done, the ultimate oscillation of the function as the
argument approaches the limit of a can be determined by taking any set
of arguments having this limit. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·301.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \subset (P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8898.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 42.204ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8898.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·32.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\in 0\cup 1.\supset .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha \in 0\cup 1\)" src="images/8899.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 58.727ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8899.svg"></p>

<p>Thus if the function has a limit as the argument approaches the limit
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8682.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.647ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8682.svg_2">, it also has a limit as the
argument approaches the limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_471">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·33.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :P_{*},Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha \in \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ)\subset CʻP.\supset .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \cup (\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha     \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\cup (\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)=CʻP\end{align}\]" src="images/8900.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.395ex; width: 89.437ex; height: 5.921ex;" id="img_images_8900.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">whence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·34.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :\text{Hp} *232·33.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)=\Lambda .\supset .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha     \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR).(\breve{P} \overline{R} Qʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ*ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\end{align}\]" src="images/8901.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.678ex; width: 79.379ex; height: 6.486ex;" id="img_images_8901.svg"></span></p>

<p>We have also</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·341.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :P_{*}\in \text{connex}  .\exists !(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha .(P\overline{R} .Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha     \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\in 1.\supset .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha     \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR).(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\end{align}\]" src="images/8902.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.678ex; width: 80.638ex; height: 6.486ex;" id="img_images_8902.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_739">[Pg 739]</span></p>

<p>Hence we arrive at the conclusion that, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/2876.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.33ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_2876.svg_17">
is a series, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_229"> is the limit of the function for the
class a <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8682.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.647ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8682.svg_3">, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_230"> is a
member of <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8680.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8680.svg_2">, it is
its maximum (<a href="#_232_352" class="pginternal">*232·352</a>), while if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_231"> is not a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8680.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8680.svg_3">, it is its sequent (<a href="#_232_356" class="pginternal">*232·356</a>),
assuming <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \cup (\breve{P}\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha = CʻP\)" src="images/8903.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.907ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_8903.svg">,
which, as we saw (<a href="#_233_22" class="pginternal">*233·22</a>), is generally the case, and
assuming also <img alt="" data-tex="\(P \in \text{Ser}\)" src="images/8904.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 7.614ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_8904.svg">. On the other hand, if
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8680.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8680.svg_4"> has no maximum, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_232"> is
the minimum of <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8680.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8680.svg_5">; and if
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8680.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8680.svg_6"> has a maximum other than <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_233">,
this is <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_1ʻx\)" src="images/8905.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.092ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8905.svg"> (<a href="#_232_357" class="pginternal">*232·357</a><a href="#_232_358" class="pginternal">·358</a>). This latter case is impossible unless
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_234"> has an immediate predecessor. Hence we arrive at the following
proposition:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·38.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash  : P \in  \text{Ser} . Q_{*} \unicode{x0294f} &amp;\alpha  \in  \text{connex}   . Rʻʻ(\alpha  \cap  CʻQ) \subset  CʻP .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha  \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR) \in  0 \cup  (1 - \text{Cl}ʻCʻP_1) . \supset  .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _pʻ(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha  = \overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _pʻ(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha      \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR) .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{\text{limin}} _pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha  = \overrightarrow{\text{limin}} _pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha      \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\end{align}\]" src="images/8906.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.186ex; width: 71.476ex; height: 15.503ex;" id="img_images_8906.svg"></span></p>

<p>Applying this to a series having Dedekindian continuity, we know
that <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_1 = \dot{\Lambda}\)" src="images/8907.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 7.027ex; height: 2.695ex;" id="img_images_8907.svg">, and that the <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}\)" src="images/7421.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.468ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_7421.svg_2"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}\)" src="images/8908.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 5.029ex; height: 1.57ex;" id="img_images_8908.svg"> always exist. Hence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·39.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash  \colon\ldotp  P \in  \text{Ser} \cap  &amp;\text{Ded} . P^{2} = P . Q_{*} \in  \text{connex}   . RʻʻCʻQ \subset  CʻP . \supset  :\\ &amp;(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha  \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR) \in  0 \cup  1 . \supset _\alpha  .\\ &amp;\text{limax}_pʻ(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha  = \text{limax}_pʻ(P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha  \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR) =\\ &amp;\text{limin}_pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha  = \text{limin}_pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha  \cap  \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\end{align}\]" src="images/8909.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.137ex; width: 70.359ex; height: 13.406ex;" id="img_images_8909.svg"></span></p>

<p>That is to say, if the value-series <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_549"> has Dedekindian continuity,
and contains all values for arguments in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_53">, then, provided the
function has a definite limit for the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap\text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8910.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.647ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8910.svg">,
this is its limit also for the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_472">; that is
to say, any collection of arguments having the same limit or maximum as
a given section will give the same limit for the function.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_740">[Pg 740]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·12.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =pʻP_{*}ʻʻʻRʻʻʻ(\alpha \cap )ʻʻ\overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha     \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\cap CʻP\\ &amp;[*232·11]\end{align}\]" src="images/8917.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.807ex; width: 70.544ex; height: 6.744ex;" id="img_images_8917.svg"></span></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .*90·13. &amp;\supset \vdash .\alpha \cap \overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻy=\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻy.\\ [*37·26] &amp;\supset \vdash .Rʻʻ(\alpha \cap \overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻy)=Rʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\cap \overleftarrow{Q}_{*}ʻy) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .(1).*232·11.\supset \vdash .\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/8919.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.274ex; width: 90.484ex; height: 11.679ex;" id="img_images_8919.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_232_131">*232·131</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR) \quad[*232·13]\)" src="images/8921.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 56.035ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8921.svg"></p>

<p>From the above propositions it follows that the values of
<img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8889.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8889.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\((\breve{P} \overline{R}Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8922.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.3ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_8922.svg">,
and <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8923.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.389ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8923.svg"> depend only upon
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/8924.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 15.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8924.svg">; thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_473"> is not contained
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/8669.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.813ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8669.svg_2">, the part not contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\cap\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/8788.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.813ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8788.svg_1">
is irrelevant.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_232_14">*232·14</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :Q\in  \text{trans} \cap\text{connex}  .\alpha \cap CʻQ{\sim}\in 1.\supset .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}(Q\unicode{x0294f}\alpha     )\\ &amp;[*232·1.*202·54·541]\end{align}\]" src="images/8925.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.319ex; width: 67.37ex; height: 5.769ex;" id="img_images_8925.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_232_15">*232·15</a>.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR=\Lambda .\supset .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha     =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha =CʻP\\ &amp;[*232·12·101.*37·29.*40·2]\end{align}\]" src="images/8926.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.395ex; width: 75.22ex; height: 5.921ex;" id="img_images_8926.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·151.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash :\dot{\exists} !P.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda .\supset .\exists !\alpha \cap CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\\ &amp;[*232·15.\text{Transp}.*33·24]\end{align}\]" src="images/8927.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.34ex; width: 45.272ex; height: 5.812ex;" id="img_images_8927.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*232·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\subset \alpha .\supset .(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha =P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q\)" src="images/8928.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 43.742ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8928.svg"></p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_745">[Pg 745]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_233">
*233. ON THE LIMITS OF FUNCTIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *233.</p>

<p>There are four limits of a function as the argument approaches some
term <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_12"> in the argument-series, namely the upper and lower limits
of the ultimate oscillation for approaches from below and above
respectively. If the ultimate oscillation for approaches to <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_13">
from below reduces to a single term, <i>i.e.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa \in 1\)" src="images/8973.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.183ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_8973.svg">,
that one term is <i>the</i> limit of the function for approaches to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_14"> from below. If this one term is also the ultimate oscillation
for approaches from above, we may call it simply the limit of the
function for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_15">. This may or may not (when it exists)
be equal to the value for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_16">. It is characteristic
of <i>continuous</i> functions that <i>the</i> limit exists for
every argument, and is always equal to the value for that argument.
Continuous functions will be considered in <a href="#_234" class="pginternal">*234</a>.</p>

<p>The upper limit or maximum of the ultimate oscillation as the argument
approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_17"> is the upper limit or maximum of the ultimate section.
Hence if we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa =\text{limax}_Pʻ(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa     \quad\text{Df}, \]" src="images/8974.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 40.261ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_8974.svg"></span>
the four limits of the function as the argument approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_18"> will be
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa,\quad R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa,\quad R(P\breve{Q} )ʻa,\quad R(\breve{P} \breve{Q} )ʻa . \]" src="images/8688.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 48.516ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_8688.svg_1"></span>
It will be seen that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R(PQ)ʻa\)" src="images/8692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.52ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8692.svg_1"> is a function of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/8975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.344ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8975.svg">. It may happen that, if we put <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_474"> in
place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/8975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.344ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8975.svg_1">, the function will have a definite
limit as the argument increases in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_475">, although <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_476"> has
no limit or maximum. Thus if, for example, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_268"> consists of the series
of rationals, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_550"> of the series of real numbers, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_477">
is a class of rationals not having a rational limit, we may regard
the limit of the function (if it exists), as the argument increases
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_478">, as the value of the function for the irrational limit
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_479">. In this way we can extend the domain of definition of a
function. In order to be able to deal with the cases in which
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_480"> has no limit, we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha =\text{limax}_Pʻ(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha     \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/8976.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 40.426ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8976.svg"></span>
If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_551"> is a Dedekindian series, <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8977.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.581ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8977.svg">
always exists. If we take <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_481"> to be any segment of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_269">, we
thus get a new function, derived from <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_93">, but having segments of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_270"> instead of members of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_54"> as its arguments. Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_94">
had<span class="pagenum" id="Page_746">[Pg 746]</span> rationale for its arguments, this new function will have real
numbers for its arguments. (Real numbers may be regarded as segments of
the series of rationals.)</p>

<p>The function <img alt="" data-tex="\(R(PQ)ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8978.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.771ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8978.svg"> is a particular case of the above; thus
we take as our definition
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻ\alpha =(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻ\alpha   \quad\text{Df}, \]" src="images/8979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.829ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_8979.svg"></span>
or, what comes to the same thing,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)=(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}\mid \overrightarrow{Q}    \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/8980.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 28.747ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_8980.svg"></span></p>

<p>The following propositions of this number are important:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·15.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in &amp;\text{Ser}\cap \text{Ded}.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha \cup (\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{sc}}ʻ\alpha     =CʻP.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha =\Lambda .\supset :\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha .\lor.\{(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha \}P_{1}\{(\breve{P}     \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\}\end{align}\]" src="images/8981.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.753ex; width: 71.177ex; height: 6.638ex;" id="img_images_8981.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·16.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}\cap \text{Ded}.&amp;P^{2}=P.Q_{*}\in \text{connex}  .RʻʻCʻQ\subset CʻP.\supset :\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\alpha \in 0\cup 1.\supset _{\alpha }.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha     =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\end{align}\]" src="images/8982.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.546ex; width: 70.491ex; height: 6.224ex;" id="img_images_8982.svg"></span></p>

<p><a href="#_233_2" class="pginternal">*233·2</a>—<a href="#_233_25" class="pginternal">·25</a> are applications of the more important of the propositions
<a href="#_232_34" class="pginternal">*232·34</a>—<a href="#_232_39" class="pginternal">·39</a>, showing circumstances under which the limit of the
function for the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_482"> is the same as for the class
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8682.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.647ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8682.svg_4">.</p>

<p><a href="#_233_4" class="pginternal">*233·4</a> and following propositions apply the earlier propositions
of <a href="#_233" class="pginternal">*233</a> to the case where <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_483"> is replaced by
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8983.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.595ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8983.svg">, and therefore <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R}Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8977.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.581ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_8977.svg_1">
is replaced by <img alt="" data-tex="\(R(PQ)ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8978.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.771ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8978.svg_1">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·43.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P_{\text{po}}\in \text{Ser}.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa &amp;\in 1.\supset .\\ &amp;R(PQ)ʻa =R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa =\breve{{℩}} ʻ(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\end{align}\]" src="images/8984.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.619ex; width: 69.251ex; height: 8.369ex;" id="img_images_8984.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·433.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}.&amp;Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa \in \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa \subset CʻP.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa=\Lambda .\\ &amp;\text{E}!R(PQ)ʻa.\text{E}!R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa.\supset :\\ &amp;R(PQ)ʻa=R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa.\lor.\{R(PQ)ʻa \}P_{1}\{R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa\}\end{align}\]" src="images/8985.svg" style="vertical-align: -4.994ex; width: 67.816ex; height: 11.12ex;" id="img_images_8985.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·45.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in \text{Ser}\cap \text{Ded}.&amp;P^{2}=P.Q_{*}\in \text{connex}  .RʻʻCʻQ\subset CʻP.\supset :\\ &amp;R(PQ)ʻa =R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa.\equiv _{a}.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa \in 0\cup 1\end{align}\]" src="images/8986.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.958ex; width: 66.836ex; height: 7.047ex;" id="img_images_8986.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> in a series having Dedekindian continuity, the necessary
and sufficient condition that the two limits of the function as the
argument approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_484"> from below should be equal is that the
ultimate oscillation should not have more than one term.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_747">[Pg 747]</span></p>

<p>We have next a set of propositions (<a href="#_233_5" class="pginternal">*233·5</a>—<a href="#_233_53" class="pginternal">·53</a>) on the possibility of
replacing <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/8975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.344ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_8975.svg_2"> by a class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_485"> having <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_19">
for its limit, without altering the limits of the function. We have to
begin with</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :Q\in \text{Ser}.\alpha =\text{lt}_{Q}ʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR).\supset .\overrightarrow{Q}ʻ\alpha =Q_{*}ʻʻ(\alpha \cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR)\)" src="images/8987.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 57.322ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_8987.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">in virtue of <a href="#_207_291" class="pginternal">*207·291</a>. Thence by earlier propositions of this number,</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·512.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp &amp;\text{Hp}*233·5.P\in \text{Ser}.Rʻʻ(\alpha \cap CʻQ)\subset CʻP.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa     =\iota ʻx.\supset :\\ &amp;x=R(PQ)ʻa =R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa:x=(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha .\lor.(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha P_{1}x\end{align}\]" src="images/8988.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.165ex; width: 71.488ex; height: 7.462ex;" id="img_images_8988.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">whence we obtain</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·514.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :\text{Hp}*233·512.x{\sim}\in CʻP_{1}.\supset .x=(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8989.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 64.383ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_8989.svg"></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_552">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_271"> are series, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_235"> is the limit of the function
for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_486"> (<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_236"> being a term which has no immediate
successor or predecessor), <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_237"> is the limit of the function for any
class of arguments whose limit is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_487">. Hence we arrive at the
proposition</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*233·53.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :Q\in \text{Ser}.&amp;P\in \text{Ser}\cap \text{Ded}.P^{2}=P.RʻʻCʻQ\subset CʻP.\alpha \subset \text{ᗡ}ʻR.\text{E}!\text{lt}_{Q}ʻ\alpha .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{os}}ʻQ_{*}ʻʻ\alpha \in 0\cup 1.\supset .\\ &amp;(P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha =(\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha =R(PQ)ʻ\text{lt}_{Q}ʻ\alpha     =R(\breve{P} Q)ʻ\text{lt}_{Q}ʻ\alpha\end{align}\]" src="images/8990.svg" style="vertical-align: -4.384ex; width: 73.37ex; height: 9.899ex;" id="img_images_8990.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_553"> has Dedekindian continuity, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_488"> is a class
of arguments having a limit, and if the ultimate oscillation as the
argument approaches this limit has not more than one term, the limit of
the function for the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_489"> exists, and is equal to the limit
of the function for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{lt}_{Q}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/8991.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.768ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_8991.svg">.</p>
