<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_753">[Pg 753]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_234">
*234. CONTINUITY OF FUNCTIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p class="nind"><i>Summary of</i> *234.</p>

<p>In the present number we are concerned with the definition and analysis
of the continuity of functions. The following definition of continuity
is given by Dini<a class="fnanchor pginternal" href="#Footnote_17" id="FNanchor_17">[17]</a>:</p>

<div class="blockquot">

<p>"We call it [the function] <i>continuous</i> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(x = a\)" src="images/9060.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 5.508ex; height: 1.505ex;" id="img_images_9060.svg">, or in the
point <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_20">, in which it has the value <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(a)\)" src="images/9061.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.201ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9061.svg">, if, for every positive
number <img alt="" data-tex="\(\sigma\)" src="images/136.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.292ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_136.svg_41">, different from 0 but as small as we please, there
exists a positive number <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}\)" src="images/4765.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 1.509ex; height: 1.312ex;" id="img_images_4765.svg_3">, different from 0, such that, for
all values of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\delta\)" src="images/302.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.005ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_302.svg_27"> which are numerically less than <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}\)" src="images/4765.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 1.509ex; height: 1.312ex;" id="img_images_4765.svg_4">,
the difference <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(a + \delta ) - f(a)\)" src="images/9062.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.939ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9062.svg"> is numerically less than
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\sigma\)" src="images/136.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.292ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_136.svg_42">. In other words, <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(x)\)" src="images/8625.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.299ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8625.svg_2"> is continuous in the point <img alt="" data-tex="\(x =a\)" src="images/9063.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 5.508ex; height: 1.505ex;" id="img_images_9063.svg">
where it has the value <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(a)\)" src="images/9061.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.201ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9061.svg_1">, if the limit of its values to the
right and left of <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_21"> is the same and equal to <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(a)\)" src="images/9061.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.201ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9061.svg_2">...."</p>
</div>

<p>By the second form of the above definition, the function <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_95"> of
previous numbers is to be called continuous at the point <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_22"> if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa = R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa = R(P\breve{Q} )ʻa = R(\breve{P} \breve{Q} )ʻa = Rʻa. \]" src="images/9064.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 55.05ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_9064.svg"></span>
The first form of the definition can also be so stated as to be free
from any reference to number, and derivable from the ideas dealt with
in the previous numbers of the present section. For this purpose,
instead of "a positive number <img alt="" data-tex="\(\sigma\)" src="images/136.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.292ex; height: 1ex;" id="img_images_136.svg_43">" we take an interval in which
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_2"> is contained, say <img alt="" data-tex="\(P(z - w)\)" src="images/9065.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.897ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9065.svg">. Similarly the "values of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\delta\)" src="images/302.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.005ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_302.svg_28"> which are numerically less than <img alt="" data-tex="\({\in}\)" src="images/4765.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 1.509ex; height: 1.312ex;" id="img_images_4765.svg_5">" are replaced by
arguments in a certain interval containing <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_23">.</p>

<p>By <a href="#_233_423" class="pginternal">*233·423</a>, if the limits of the function as the argument approaches
<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_24"> are to be all equal, <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_25"> must not be the maximum or minimum
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/2905.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2905.svg_3">. We therefore take the interval containing <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_26"> to
be an interval in which the end-points are not included, say <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q(y -y')\)" src="images/9066.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.16ex; height: 2.283ex;" id="img_images_9066.svg">.
Thus our definition becomes
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} (\text{A})\quad Rʻa\in &amp;P(z-w).\supset _{z, w}.\\ &amp;(\exists y,y').y,y'\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR.a\in Q(y-y').RʻʻQ(y\vdash\dashv y')\subset P(z-w) \end{aligned} \]" src="images/9067.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.145ex; width: 72.95ex; height: 5.421ex;" id="img_images_9067.svg"></span></p>

<p>We require further, what is tacitly assumed in Dini's definition, that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_3"> is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_138"> which has no immediate predecessor or
successor, <i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ Rʻa\in CʻP-CʻP_{1}. \]" src="images/9068.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.725ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_9068.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_754">[Pg 754]</span></p>

<p>In order to deal more easily with the above definition, we analyse it
into the product of four factors, which concern respectively <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_554"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_272">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_16"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_273">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_555"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{Q}\)" src="images/9069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.9ex;" id="img_images_9069.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_17">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{Q}\)" src="images/9069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.9ex;" id="img_images_9069.svg_1">. In the first place, it is obvious that (A) is the
product of
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\text{B})\quad Rʻa \in  P(z-w). \supset _{z,w} . (\exists y) . y \in  \text{ᗡ}ʻR . y \in  \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa . RʻʻQ(y \unicode{x27dd} a) \subset  P(z-w) \]" src="images/9070.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 75.082ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9070.svg"></span>
and a factor obtained by substituting <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{Q}\)" src="images/9069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.9ex;" id="img_images_9069.svg_2"> for
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_274"> in (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{B}\)" src="images/9071.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.602ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_9071.svg">). If <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*} \in \text{connex}\)" src="images/9072.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.394ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_9072.svg">, and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\in\text{Ser}\)" src="images/9073.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 9.245ex; height: 2.245ex;" id="img_images_9073.svg">, (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{B}\)" src="images/9071.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.602ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_9071.svg_1">) is the product of
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\text{C}) Rʻa \in  \overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻw     . \supset _w . (\exists y) . y \in  \text{ᗡ}ʻR . y \in  \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa . RʻʻQ (y \unicode{x27dd}  a) \subset  \overrightarrow{P}_{*}ʻw \]" src="images/9074.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 65.593ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9074.svg"></span>
and a factor obtained by writing <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_18"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_556"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/2071.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_2071.svg_40"> for
<img alt="" data-tex="\(w\)" src="images/2358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.62ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_2358.svg_5"> in (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{C}\)" src="images/9075.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.633ex; height: 1.643ex;" id="img_images_9075.svg">); and in virtue of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa {\sim}\in CʻP_{1}\)" src="images/9076.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 14.315ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_9076.svg">,
(<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{C}\)" src="images/9075.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.633ex; height: 1.643ex;" id="img_images_9075.svg_1">) becomes
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ Rʻa \in  \overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻw . \supset _w . (\exists y) . y \in  \text{ᗡ}ʻR . y \in  \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa . RʻʻQ (y \unicode{x27dd}  a) \subset  \overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻw. \]" src="images/9077.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 63.718ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9077.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_275"> is transitive,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\text{D}) Rʻa \in  \overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻw . \supset _w . R(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)_{\text{cn}} (\overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻw) \]" src="images/9078.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 43.749ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9078.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence the function is continuous for the argument a if a satisfies
(<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}\)" src="images/720.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.729ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_720.svg_6">) and the three other hypotheses resulting from replacing
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_557"> by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_19">, or <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_276"> by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{Q}\)" src="images/9069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.9ex;" id="img_images_9069.svg_3">, or <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_558"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_277"> by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\)" src="images/3655.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_3655.svg_20"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{Q}\)" src="images/9069.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.9ex;" id="img_images_9069.svg_4">. If we substitute <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_238"> for
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_4">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_278"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*} \unicode{x0294f} \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9079.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.479ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_9079.svg">,
(<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}\)" src="images/720.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.729ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_720.svg_7">) becomes
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (\text{E}) \overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\overleftarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻx \subset  \overleftarrow{Q}_{\text{cn}}ʻR \]" src="images/9080.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 26.84ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9080.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence continuity can be studied by studying the hypothesis
(<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}\)" src="images/9081.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.541ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_9081.svg">), and replacing <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_239"> by <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_5"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_279"> by
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f} \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9082.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.479ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_9082.svg">.</p>

<p>The hypothesis (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}\)" src="images/9081.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.541ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_9081.svg_1">) is an interesting one on its own account.
We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR = CʻP \cap  \hat{x}  (\overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\overleftarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻx \subset  \overleftarrow{Q}_{\text{cn}}ʻR) \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/9083.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 53.439ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9083.svg"></span>
Thus "<img alt="" data-tex="\(x \in \text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9084.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.286ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9084.svg">" means that <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_240"> is a member of the
value-series such that, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_117"> is any later member, the function
ultimately becomes less than <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_118">. If we put further
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{os}(P,Q)ʻR = \text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR \cap  \text{sc}(\breve{P} ,Q)ʻR \quad\text{Df}, \]" src="images/9085.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.647ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9085.svg"></span>
then, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_241"> is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg">, the function
ultimately becomes less than any later member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_139">, and greater
than any earlier member. Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_242"> is the limit of the function as
the argument increases indefinitely. Hence, if we substitute
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f} \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9082.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.479ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_9082.svg_1"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_280">, and if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\in \text{os}(P,Q_{*} \unicode{x0294f} \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR\)" src="images/9087.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.101ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9087.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_243"> is the limit of the function as the argument approaches a from
below, <i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa = R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa = x. \]" src="images/9088.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.998ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9088.svg"></span>
(This is proved in <a href="#_234_462" class="pginternal">*234·462</a>.) Hence, putting <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_6"> in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_244">,
the function is continuous from below at the point <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_27"> if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ Rʻa \in  \text{os}(P,Q_{*} \unicode{x0294f} \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR, \]" src="images/9089.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.708ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9089.svg"></span><span class="pagenum" id="Page_755">[Pg 755]</span>
and is continuous from above if
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ Rʻa\in \text{os}(P,\breve{Q} _{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overleftarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR. \]" src="images/9090.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.369ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9090.svg"></span>
These results, and various others connected with them, are proved
below. The equivalence of Dini's two definitions is proved in <a href="#_234_63" class="pginternal">*234·63</a>.
It will be observed that practically nothing in the theory of
continuous functions requires the use of numbers.</p>

<p>We use the symbol "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR\)" src="images/9091.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.208ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9091.svg">" for the class of arguments
<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_28"> for which the limit of the function for approaches to a from
below is <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_7">. Thus, in virtue of what was said above, we may put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{ct}(PQ)ʻR=\hat{a}\{Rʻa\in \text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}_{\text{po}}ʻa)ʻR-CʻP_{1}\} \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/9092.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 57.235ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9092.svg"></span>
Then a function is continuous at the point <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_29"> if a belongs to the
two classes <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR\)" src="images/9091.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.208ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9091.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(P\breve{Q} )ʻR\)" src="images/9093.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.208ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_9093.svg">. Hence
we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{contin}(PQ)ʻR=\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR\cap \text{ct}(P\breve{Q} )ʻR \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/9094.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 45.744ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_9094.svg"></span>
The function <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_96"> is continuous with respect to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_559"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_281"> if it
is continuous for all arguments in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_55">. Thus we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P\overline{\text{contin}} Q=\hat{R}\{\exists !CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR.CʻQ\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR\subset \text{contin}(PQ)ʻR\} \quad\text{Df}. \]" src="images/9095.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 65.979ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_9095.svg"></span></p>

<p>Our propositions in this number begin with the properties of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.225ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9096.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_1">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·103.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :P_{\text{po}}\in \text{Ser}.\exists !\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR.\supset .P\overline{R} _{\text{os}}Q\in 0\cup 1\)" src="images/9097.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 44.269ex; height: 2.912ex;" id="img_images_9097.svg"></p>

<p>Thus the hypothesis <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists !\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9098.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 13.239ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9098.svg"> enables us to use
propositions of previous numbers having the hypothesis <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\overline{R}_{\text{os}}Q\in 0\cup 1\)" src="images/8675.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 14.367ex; height: 2.701ex;" id="img_images_8675.svg_1">.</p>

<p>The identification of our definitions with the usual definitions of
continuity of functions proceeds by means of the proposition</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·12.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\colon Q_{*}\in &amp;\text{connex}  .\supset \colon\ldotp x\in \text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\cap \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP.\equiv :\\ &amp;x\in \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP:x\in P(z-w).\supset _{z,w}.RQ_{\text{cn}}\{P(z-w)\}\end{align}\]" src="images/9099.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.078ex; width: 61.674ex; height: 5.288ex;" id="img_images_9099.svg"></span></p>

<p>We have a collection of propositions dealing with the relations of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.225ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9096.svg_1"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q\)" src="images/8784.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.734ex; height: 2.701ex;" id="img_images_8784.svg_2"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}\overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q\)" src="images/8659.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.734ex; height: 2.853ex;" id="img_images_8659.svg_2">. <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.225ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9096.svg_2"> is
an upper section of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_560"> (<a href="#_234_131" class="pginternal">*234·131</a>); <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.225ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9096.svg_3"> is the
complement of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Pʻʻ(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9100.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.908ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_9100.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q\)" src="images/8784.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.734ex; height: 2.701ex;" id="img_images_8784.svg_3"> without its maximum (if any). This is
expressed in the following proposition:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·174.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P_{\text{po}}\in \text{Ser}.Q_{*}\in \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ&amp;CʻQ\subset CʻP.\supset .\\ &amp;CʻP\cap pʻ\overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR=Pʻʻ(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q)=CʻP-\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\end{align}\]" src="images/9101.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.867ex; width: 95.489ex; height: 6.865ex;" id="img_images_9101.svg"></span></p>

<p>We thus arrive at</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·182.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash :P\in \text{Ser}.Q_{*}\in \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ&amp;CʻQ\subset CʻP.\supset .\\ &amp;\overrightarrow{\text{limax}} _{P}ʻ(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q) = \overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ\text{sc}(P,     Q)ʻR\end{align}\]" src="images/9102.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.957ex; width: 66.563ex; height: 7.045ex;" id="img_images_9102.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_756">[Pg 756]</span></p>

<p>Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_2"> is contained in
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{max}}_{P}ʻ(P\overline{R} _{\text{sc}}Q)\cup\overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9103.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.979ex; height: 4.048ex;" id="img_images_9103.svg">
(*234·201), and therefore has not more than two terms (<a href="#_234_202" class="pginternal">*234·202</a>). If
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\overline{R}_{\text{os}}Q\)" src="images/8661.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 6.824ex; height: 2.701ex;" id="img_images_8661.svg_7"> has one term, this is the only member
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_3"> (<a href="#_234_203" class="pginternal">*234·203</a>). If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_4"> has two
terms, they have the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{1}\)" src="images/2893.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.44ex; height: 1.885ex;" id="img_images_2893.svg_11"> (<a href="#_234_242" class="pginternal">*234·242</a>); hence if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_561">
is a compact series, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_5"> is not null, its only
member is both <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}_Pʻ(P\overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9104.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.709ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_9104.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}_Pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9105.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.271ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9105.svg"> (<a href="#_234_25" class="pginternal">*234·25</a>),
while conversely, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limax}_Pʻ(P\overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9104.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.709ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_9104.svg_1">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{limin}_Pʻ(\breve{P} \overline{R}_{\text{sc}}Q)\)" src="images/9105.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.271ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9105.svg_1"> are
equal, each is the only member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_6"> (<a href="#_234_251" class="pginternal">*234·251</a>).</p>

<p>We now apply the above results to the limits of a function as its
argument approaches the limit of a class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_490">. This is done, as
before, by substituting <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha\)" src="images/8677.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.583ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8677.svg_2"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_282">.
We arrive at the proposition (<a href="#_234_33" class="pginternal">*234·33</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_562"> has Dedekindian
continuity, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha )ʻR\)" src="images/9106.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.145ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9106.svg"> is not
null, its only member is both <img alt="" data-tex="\((P\overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/9107.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.581ex; height: 2.828ex;" id="img_images_9107.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\((\breve{P} \overline{R} Q)_{\text{lmx}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/9108.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.581ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9108.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> is
the limit of the function as the argument increases in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_491">.</p>

<p>We then take for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_492"> the particular value
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{Q}_{\text{po}}ʻa\)" src="images/9109.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.221ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9109.svg">, so that we become concerned
with what happens when the argument approaches a from below. For the
comparison of our definition of continuity with such definitions as the
one quoted from Dini above, we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·41.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\colon Q\in \text{trans}.Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}&amp;\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\in \text{connex}  .\supset \colon\ldotp\\ &amp;x\in \text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR\cap \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP.\equiv :\\ &amp;x\in \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP:x\in P(z-w).\supset _{z,w}.\\ &amp;(\exists y).y\in \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR.RʻʻQ(y\unicode{x27dd} a)\subset P(z-w)\end{align}\]" src="images/9110.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.331ex; width: 63.001ex; height: 15.792ex;" id="img_images_9110.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_245"> is neither the first nor the
last member of the <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_563">-series, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_246"> belongs to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR\)" src="images/9111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.041ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9111.svg"> when, and
only when, given any interval <img alt="" data-tex="\(P(z-w)\)" src="images/9112.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.897ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9112.svg">, however small, in which <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_247">
is contained, there is an argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_119"> earlier than <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_30">, such that
the value of the function for all arguments earlier than a but not
earlier than <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_120"> lies in the interval <img alt="" data-tex="\(P(z-w)\)" src="images/9112.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.897ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9112.svg_1">.</p>

<p>We deduce from previous propositions that, with the usual hypothesis as
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_283">, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_564"> is a Dedekindian series,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa=\text{limin}_Pʻ\text{sc}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR \quad(*234·422), \]" src="images/9113.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 52.433ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9113.svg"></span>
and if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_565"> is a series and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)\)" src="images/9114.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.967ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9114.svg"> is a unit
class, its only member is both <img alt="" data-tex="\(R(PQ)ʻa\)" src="images/8692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.52ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_8692.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa\)" src="images/8693.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.52ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_8693.svg_1">,
<i>i.e.</i> is the limit of the function for approaches to <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_31"> from
below (<a href="#_234_43" class="pginternal">*234·43</a>). The following proposition sums up our results:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·45.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash \colon\ldotp P\in &amp;\text{Ser}.Q\in \text{trans}.Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\in     \text{connex}  .Rʻʻ\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\subset CʻP.P^{2}=P.\supset :\\ \exists !\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR.&amp;\equiv .\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR=\iota ʻR(PQ)ʻa.\\ &amp;\equiv .\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR=\iota ʻR(\breve{P} Q)ʻa.\\ &amp;\equiv .R(PQ)ʻa=R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa\end{align}\]" src="images/9115.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.647ex; width: 82.922ex; height: 16.425ex;" id="img_images_9115.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_757">[Pg 757]</span></p>

<p>Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR\)" src="images/9116.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.928ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9116.svg"> is,
in a compact series, the necessary and sufficient condition for
the existence of a definite limit of the function as the argument
approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_32"> from below.</p>

<p>Without assuming <img alt="" data-tex="\(P^{2} = P\)" src="images/9117.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 7.528ex; height: 2.072ex;" id="img_images_9117.svg">, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_248"> is a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa)ʻR\)" src="images/9111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 18.041ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9111.svg_1">, and
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_249"> has no immediate predecessor or successor, so that in the
neighbourhood of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/50.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_50.svg_250"> the series is compact, we still have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x =R(PQ)ʻa = R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa\)" src="images/9118.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.369ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9118.svg"> (<a href="#_234_462" class="pginternal">*234·462</a>).</p>

<p>We next consider <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR\)" src="images/9091.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.208ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9091.svg_2">. By the definition we have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :a\in \text{ct}(PQ)ʻR.\equiv .Rʻa\in \text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}_{\text{po}}ʻa)ʻR-CʻP_{1}\)" src="images/9119.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 55.822ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9119.svg"></p>

<p>Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_33"> is an argument for which the function has a single value
which has no immediate predecessor or successor in <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_566">, and which,
in virtue of <a href="#_234_462" class="pginternal">*234·462</a>, is the limit of the function as the argument
approaches <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_34"> from below (<a href="#_234_52" class="pginternal">*234·52</a>). The cases when <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa = BʻP\)" src="images/9120.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.062ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_9120.svg"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa = Bʻ\breve{P}\)" src="images/9121.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.062ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_9121.svg"> require special attention; excluding these cases,
we arrive at</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·51.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}\vdash &amp;\colon\colon Q\in \text{trans}.Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\in     \text{connex}  .Rʻa\in \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP.\supset \colon\ldotp \\ &amp;a\in \text{ct}(PQ)ʻR.\equiv :Rʻa{\sim}\in CʻP_{1}:Rʻa\in P(z-w).\supset _{z,w}.\\ &amp;(\exists y).y\in \overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻR.RʻʻQ(y\vdash\dashv a)\subset P(z-w)\end{align}\]" src="images/9122.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.09ex; width: 57.629ex; height: 11.31ex;" id="img_images_9122.svg"></span></p>

<p>This proposition is analogous to <a href="#_234_41" class="pginternal">*234·41</a>.</p>

<p>We prove (<a href="#_234_562" class="pginternal">*234·562</a>) that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_567">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_284"> are series, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_493">
is any class of arguments for which all the values belong to <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/4110.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4110.svg_140">,
and if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_494"> has a limit at which the function is continuous from
below, then the limit of the function, as the argument increases in
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_495">, is the value of the function at the limit of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_496">.</p>

<p>We next consider <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{contin}(PQ)ʻR\)" src="images/9123.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.484ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9123.svg">, which is defined as
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR\cap \text{ct}(P\breve{Q} )ʻR\)" src="images/9124.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.931ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_9124.svg">. We show that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_568">
is a series whose field contains <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻʻ(\overleftrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9125.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.317ex; height: 3.803ex;" id="img_images_9125.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_285"> is transitive, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*} \unicode{x0294f}\overleftrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9126.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.14ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_9126.svg">
is connected, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_8"> is neither <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻP\)" src="images/3392.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3392.svg_16"> nor <img alt="" data-tex="\(Bʻ\breve{P}\)" src="images/5455.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_5455.svg_7">,
then if <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_35"> belongs to the class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{contin}(PQ)ʻR\)" src="images/9123.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.484ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9123.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_9"> is the
limit of the function for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_36"> for approaches either
from below or from above (<a href="#_234_62" class="pginternal">*234·62</a>). If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_569"> is compact, the converse
also holds (<a href="#_234_63" class="pginternal">*234·63</a>). Our definition of a point of continuity is thus
identified with the second form of Dini's definition quoted above. It
is identified with the first form by the following proposition: In the
circumstances of *234·62, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\in \text{D}ʻP\cap \text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/9127.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 18.751ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_9127.svg">, we
have (<a href="#_234_64" class="pginternal">*234·64</a>)
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} a\in \text{contin}(PQ)ʻ&amp;R.\equiv :Rʻa\in CʻP-CʻP_{1}:Rʻa\in P(z-w).\supset _{z,w}.\\ &amp;(\exists y,y').y,y'\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR.a\in Q(y-y').RʻʻQ(y\vdash\dashv y')\subset P(z-w), \end{aligned} \]" src="images/9128.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.145ex; width: 78.181ex; height: 5.421ex;" id="img_images_9128.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_37"> is a point of continuity when, and only when, the
value <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_10"> for the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_38"> is a member of the <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_570">-series
having no immediate predecessor or successor, and if <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻa\)" src="images/8689.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.271ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8689.svg_11"> is
contained in the interval <img alt="" data-tex="\(P(z-w)\)" src="images/9112.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.897ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9112.svg_2">, then,<span class="pagenum" id="Page_758">[Pg 758]</span> however small this
interval may be, two arguments <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_121">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y'\)" src="images/5316.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.736ex; height: 2.181ex;" id="img_images_5316.svg_3"> can be found such that
a lies between them, and the values for all arguments from <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/51.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_51.svg_122"> to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y'\)" src="images/5316.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.736ex; height: 2.181ex;" id="img_images_5316.svg_4"> (both included) lie in the interval <img alt="" data-tex="\(P(z-w)\)" src="images/9112.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.897ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9112.svg_3">.</p>

<p>We end with a few propositions on continuous functions. The last of
these (<a href="#_234_73" class="pginternal">*234·73</a>) states that, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_571"> is a compact series and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_286">
is transitive and connected, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/25.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_25.svg_97"> is continuous with respect to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_572"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_287"> when, and only when, it has arguments in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻQ\)" src="images/4111.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.867ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_4111.svg_56">, and
for all such arguments <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_39"> we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R(PQ)ʻa=R(\breve{P} Q)ʻa=R(P\breve{Q} )ʻa=R(\breve{P} \breve{Q} )ʻa=Rʻa, \]" src="images/9129.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 55.05ex; height: 3.027ex;" id="img_images_9129.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> the value for every argument is the limit for that argument
for approaches either from above or from below.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR=CʻP\cap \hat{x} (\overrightarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻʻ\overleftarrow{P}_{\text{po}}ʻx\subset \overleftarrow{Q}_{\text{cn}}ʻR)      \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/9130.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 52.81ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9130.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR=\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\cap \text{sc}(\breve{P},Q)ʻR \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/9131.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.018ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_9131.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*234·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ct}(PQ)ʻR=\hat{a} \{Rʻa\in \text{os}(P,Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}_{\text{po}}ʻa)ʻR-CʻP_{1}\}  \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/9132.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 56.606ex; height: 3.887ex;" id="img_images_9132.svg"></p>

<p>When <img alt="" data-tex="\(x{\sim}\in \text{D}ʻP_{1}\)" src="images/9145.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.346ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_9145.svg">, the above proposition is not

<p>It is to be observed that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sc}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9096.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.225ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9096.svg_4"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{os}(P,Q)ʻR\)" src="images/9086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.352ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_9086.svg_7">
are functions of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/2876.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.33ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_2876.svg_18">, so that they are unchanged when
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/2876.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.33ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_2876.svg_19"> is substituted for <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/54.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_54.svg_573">. Hence the hypothesis
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P_{\text{po}}\in \text{Ser}\)" src="images/8206.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 9.245ex; height: 2.245ex;" id="img_images_8206.svg_3"> is as effective, with regard to them,
as the hypothesis <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in \text{Ser}\)" src="images/7003.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 7.614ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_7003.svg_2">. This is stated in the following
proposition.</p>

<p>The remaining propositions of the present number are for the most
part immediate consequences of those already proved. In order to
obtain, from propositions already proved, propositions concerning
the limit of a function as the argument approaches the limit of
some class of arguments <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_497">, we only have to substitute
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\alpha\)" src="images/8677.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.583ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_8677.svg_3"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_288">. In order to obtain the limit
of a function as the argument approaches a given term <img alt="" data-tex="\(a\)" src="images/3545.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.197ex; height: 1.02ex;" id="img_images_3545.svg_40">, we take
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q_{*}\unicode{x0294f}\overrightarrow{Q}ʻa\)" src="images/9218.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.479ex; height: 3.69ex;" id="img_images_9218.svg"> in place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/3372.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_3372.svg_289">.</p>
